READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. Jeremiah 2 spoke of the religious problems of Judah, while Jeremiah 5 speaks of the civic problems.

  2. Jeremiah 4-6 are a unified subject (i.e. Judah is sinful and will be invaded, destroyed, and exiled).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:2 "As the Lord lives"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:2 "As the Lord lives" Judeans used YHWH's name flippantly (in violation of Exod. 20:7; Lev. 19:12), but denied His lordship by their lives (cf. Isa. 29:13). This phrase is a play on YHWH, which is from the Hebrew VERB "to be" (cf. Exod. 3:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:3 Because YHWH could not find a faithful person, this verse, in a series of parallel lines, describes what He will do (all PERFECTS).

  1. You have smitten them but they refused to be sickened
  2. You consumed them but they refused to take correction
  3. You made their faces harder than rock but they refused to repent (cf. Jer. 5:5e,f)

Since repentance (see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [OT]) was no longer a real option, only judgment remained!

Just a note about the second VERB in #1 above. It could come from two possible Hebrew roots.

  1. חלה ‒ BDB 317 I, KB 316, Qal PERFECT, "to be weak" or "to be sick"
  2. חול ‒ BDB 296 I, #2, a., KB 297, "to feel anguish" (cf. Ezek. 30:16)

▣ "truth" This Hebrew term denotes "faithfulness" (BDB 53, cf. Jer. 5:1e; Hab. 2:4). See SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT. Truth is more than accurate facts (see SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN). It is a godly, faithful lifestyle.

▣ "their faces harder than rock" "Harder" (Piel PERFECT, BDB 304, KB 302) is often used as imagery for people hardening their hearts (cf. Exod. 8:15; Ezek. 3:7-9). The context confirms this play on word meaning. The Judeans refused (Piel PERFECT, BDB 549, KB 540) to repent (Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, BDB 996, KB 1427).

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:4 "the way. . .ordinance"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:4 "the way. . .ordinance" These two words (BDB 202 and 1048) are two of several terms used to describe God's revelation.

The point of Jer. 5:4-5 is that those who are uneducated and spend all their time just surviving, might not know God's revelation, but the socially elite do have education and instruction in YHWH's revelation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION (Using Deuteronomy and Psalms)

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:4-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:4-6 It seems that the prophet acknowledges Judah's rebellion, but asks permission to address them again in hopes of diverting YHWH's judgment.

  1. Judah's spiritual condition
    1. they are poor (BDB 195, the opposite of "great," BDB 152, Jer. 5:5)
    2. they are foolish (lit. "they have no sense," BDB 383 I, KB 381)
    3. they do not know the way of the Lord (i.e. not willful ignorance, but uninformed because of their poverty)
  2. Jeremiah's proposal
    1. I will go and speak (both COHORTATIVES) to the great (i.e. leadership, cf. Jer. 5:31; they had the opportunity to know the law of the Lord)
    2. I will remind them of their knowledge of YHWH's covenant
    3. I will inform them of their corporate sin (cf. Jer. 2:20)
      (1) with one accord
      (2) broken the yoke
      (3) burst the bonds

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:5 "the yoke"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:5 "the yoke" This word (BDB 760) was used by the rabbis to refer to the regulations of the Mosaic Law (cf. Matt. 11:29).

▣ "burst the bonds" These were the cords which held the yoke in place. It is more imagery of known rebellion and covenant violation.

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:5-7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:5-7 YHWH speaks to Judah and outlines their sins and His appropriate response.

  1. their sin
    1. your sons have forsaken Me (cf. Jer. 1:16)
    2. they have sworn by false gods (opposite of Jer. 4:2 and 5:2) who are not real (cf. Jer. 2:11)
    3. they committed adultery (i.e. idolatry or political alliances)
    4. they were involved in fertility worship with all the women of the community (cf. Jer. 3:8-9; Ba'al and Asherah worship)
  2. YHWH's response
    1. He will not pardon them (opposite of Jer. 5:1)
    2. He fed them to the full (revelation and blessing)
    3. they deserve judgment (Jer. 5:9)

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:6 This verse describes YHWH's judgment in the imagery of predators (imagery for invaders, cf. Jer. 2:15; 4:7; 50:17). It needs to be mentioned that attacks by wild animals were not part of the cursing section of Deut. 28 (v. 26). This threat is repeated in Jer. 7:33; 16:4; 19:7; 34:20.

  1. a lion (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LIONS IN THE OT)
  2. a wolf
  3. a leopard

The reason for the attacks was Judah's open-eyed rebellion.

  1. many transgressions (BDB 833)
  2. numerous apostasies

Notice here the parallelism in the first three lines and the last two lines of Jer. 5:6.

▣ "apostasies" See SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY (aphistēmi)

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:7 "sworn by those who are not gods"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:7 "sworn by those who are not gods" This is a denial of the existence of the Canaanite gods, but possibly used by the demonic to trick superstitious, fallen mankind, cf. Lev. 17:7; Deut. 32:17; Ps. 106:37; Jer. 2:11; 16:20; Isa. 37:19; Gal. 4:8; Rev. 9:20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEMONS/FALLEN ANGELS

▣ "sworn. . .fed them to the full" There is a word play between

  1. שׁבע ‒ swear (BDB 989, KB 1396, Niphal IMPERFECT with waw)
  2. שׂבע ‒ fed to the full (BDB 959, KB 1302, Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw)

It is even possible that "swear" should be in both lines, thereby denoting false allegiances to fertility gods.

For two good texts on the ridiculousness of worshiping that which you make, see Ps. 115:4-8; Jer. 10:2-5; Hosea 8:4-6.

▣ "trooped to the harlot's house" The MT has a word (BDB 151, KB 177 IMPERFECT) in the Hithpoel stem that has two distinct meanings.

  1. gash/cut ‒ an aspect of pagan worship (cf. Deut. 14:1; 1 Kgs. 18:28; Jer. 16:6; 41:5; 48:37; possibly Hosea 7:14)
  2. assemble in troops or bands (cf. Hosea 7:14; Micah 5:1) with the implication of spending much time in the prostitutes' house

The LXX has "lodged" (UBS Text Project, p. 187-188, gives this option a "C" rating) and the Peshitta has "fought one another." Obviously there is some confusion in meaning in the ancient versions.

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:8 Again the animal world is used to describe human activity. Humans, made in God's image, should act differently than animals in heat (i.e. Jer. 2:23-24)!

The first two PARTICIPLES are uncertain. The best guess is

  1. "well fed" ‒ BDB 402, KB 404, Pual PARTICIPLE, occurs only here. BDB suggests "testicles." KB suggests "to be in heat," from an Arabic root.
  2. "lusty" ‒ BDB 1013, KB 1488, Hiphil PARTICIPLE, which occurs only here. KB suggests it also means "possessing testicles"

The LXX has "they were lusty stallions, each neighing for his fellow's wife." Remember for interpreting poetry, look to

  1. context (i.e. the strophe)
  2. parallelism
  3. general sense of the book's larger context
  4. similar Hebrew roots
  5. cognate language roots
  6. common sense

"Bible Interpretation Seminar"

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:10 "For they are not the Lord's"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:10 "For they are not the Lord's" This is referring to the "vines." These Judeans saw their agricultural abundance as a sign of Ba'al's favor! This will change (cf. Jer. 5:12; Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-29).

▣ "But I do not execute complete destruction" A faithful remnant shall remain (cf. Jer. 4:27; 5:10,18; 30:11; 46:28)

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:10-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:10-13 This strophe is very similar to Jer. 5:7-9. These were probably independent judgment poems collected and edited.

Notice the IMPERATIVES of Jer. 5:10.

  1. "go up" ‒ BDB 748, KB 828, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. "destroy" ‒ BDB 1007, KB 1469, Piel IMPERATIVE
  3. "do not execute a complete destruction" ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERFECT negated, used in a JUSSIVE sense, cf. Jer. 4:27c; 5:18; 30:11; 46:28
  4. "strip away" ‒ BDB 693, KB 747, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

Also notice the intensified form in Jer. 5:11, "have dealt very treacherously with Me." This is a Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and an IMPERFECT VERB of the same root (BDB 93, KB 108).

In light of this, Jer. 5:10b is a startling statement of hope (cf. Jer. 4:27; 5:10,18; 30:11; 46:28)! A faithful remnant will be spared.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (three senses)

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:11 "house of Israel. . .house of Judah"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 5:11 "house of Israel. . .house of Judah" All the sons of Abraham had rebelled (cf. Jer. 3:6-10).

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:12 The VERB "lied about the Lord" (BDB 471, KB 469, Piel PERFECT) may be a word play. Its basic meaning is "lean," the exact opposite of the leaders of Jer. 5:7-8. It denotes people who seem to acknowledge one thing, but in reality acknowledge someone else (cf. Josh. 24:27; Job 8:15; Isa. 59:13). This is an example of Isa. 29:13! They say one thing ("As the Lord lives," Jer. 5:2); they do mean it but they practice fertility rites and swear by Ba'al.

▣
NASB   "Not He"
NKJV, Peshitta   "It is not He"
NRSV   "He is nothing"
TEV   "He won't really do anything"
TEV footnote   "We don't want anything to do with Him"
NJB   "He will do nothing"
JPSOA   "It is not so!"
REB   "He does not matter"
LXX   "These things are not so"

This is irony. The only true God (i.e. Deut. 32:39; Isa. 43:13) is said to be irrelevant (i.e. will not act, cf. Ezek. 8:12; 9:9; Zeph. 1:12) and the false fertility gods with their false prophets are praised and trusted!

It is possible that this brief phrase means "YHWH would never bring judgment on Jerusalem" (AB, p. 40), which was the prophecy of Isaiah (cf. Isaiah 5-12; 36-37) and the repeated message of the false prophets in Jeremiah's day. Isaiah's statement would be true if His people were faithful, but they were not and the consequences of covenant infidelity (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-29) will come to pass! The Mosaic Covenant is a "conditional" covenant!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:13 Those who were called and charged to speak for YHWH did not have His "spirit," "wind" (BDB 924, i.e. they do not have YHWH's word, Jer. 5:13b; see SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT). False prophets are a recurrent theme in Jeremiah (i.e. 5:31; 14:13-15; 23 and typified by Hananiah in chapter 28). Often people hear what they want to hear! The heart controls the ear!

But there are true prophets who do speak for God; Jeremiah was one of them. Verse 13 could be

  1. the people's comment about God's prophets, as Jer. 5:12 is their comment about God
  2. this is Jeremiah's comment about the false prophets who are speaking "peace," "safety"! They do not have the Spirit!

The last line of Jer. 5:12 favors #2. But it is hard to know "who" is speaking to "whom" in the poems of Jeremiah. The interpretation depends on the identity of the speaker and the recipients. Dogmatism is certainly inappropriate. It is best to ascertain the central truth of the literary unit or strophe (or series of strophes) and not push the details!

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:14-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:14-17 YHWH ("the Lord, the God of hosts," see SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS) discloses what He will do in response to His people's rebellion and specifically because of their words in Jer. 5:12.

There is some textual question about the PRONOUN "you" or "they." It seems that YHWH is referring, not to Jeremiah's message, but the message of "peace" and "safety" spoken by the false prophets, will destroy the nation of Judah.

God is bringing a foreign pagan nation to judge His people (cf. Isa. 5:26-30). Apparently Jer. 5:14 is YHWH speaking to Jeremiah (UBS Handbook on Jeremiah, p. 163). Notice the description of this nation.

  1. from afar
  2. an enduring nation (or "strong," cf. Jer. 5:15)
  3. an ancient nation
  4. a nation with a different language (cf. Isa. 28:11)
  5. a nation with a mighty army
    1. devour your current harvest
    2. devour your children
    3. devour your herds
    4. devour your fields
    5. demolish your walled cities and forts

It is contexts such as this that have caused me to realize that YHWH often used pagan armies to judge His people. This invasion is often called "coming." This has forced me to rethink my understanding of Jesus' Olivet Discourse (i.e. Matt. 23-25; Mark 13; Luke 17; 21), as well as the book of Revelation. I have recently (2024-2025) rewritten my exegetical verse-by-verse commentaries on all of these. They are free online.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COMING ON THE CLOUDS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SECOND COMING

SPECIAL TOPIC: SOON RETURN

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:15 "O house of Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 5:15 "O house of Israel" There is often confusion related to this term. It can refer to all of the tribes of Jacob's sons (i.e. collective term), but after the United Monarchy, split in 922 B.C. when its capital, Samaria, fell (in Isaiah's day).

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:16 The MT has אשפתו (BDB 80), which means "quiver." However, the previous line in Jer. 5:15 speaks of a language; שפתו, which means "his lip" (cf. NEB, REB, "jaws"; JPSOA footnote emendation yields "whose mouths"). The UBS Text Project gives the MT a B rating (some doubt), which is followed by most English translations.

The LXX of this verse has only "all are strong" for Jer. 5:16.

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:18-19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:18-19 This is a statement of hope, forgiveness, and restoration to

  1. the faithful remnant, see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT
  2. all of the seed of Abraham who will repent of their idolatry

The phrase "I will not make a complete destruction" (cf. Jer. 4:27; 5:10; 30:11; 46:28) implies #1.

YHWH is addressing His prophet (Jer. 5:19) about how to respond to the obvious question, "Why has God allowed this destruction and exile?" (cf. Jer. 16:10-13; Deut. 29:24-28; 1 Kgs. 9:8-9). It is theologically crucial in an ANE setting that the reason for the exile is not YHWH's weakness, but His people's idolatry!

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:20-29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:20-29 This is yet another strophe/poem about YHWH's people's (both Israel and Judah) sin (Jer. 5:20). It has imagery from Isa. 6:9-10.

It starts off like Jer. 4:5, with several IMPERATIVES related to "hear and respond."

  1. "declare" ‒ BDB 16, KB 665, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  2. "proclaim ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  3. "hear" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE

Notice how the covenant people are characterized (Jer. 5:21-23).

  1. foolish ‒ BDB 698, cf. Jer. 4:22
  2. senseless (lit. "without heart")
  3. eyes but cannot see
  4. ears but cannot hear
  5. do not fear ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, cf. Jer. 1:8; 3:8
  6. do not feel anguish ‒ BDB 296, KB 297, cf. Jer. 5:3; 4:19,31; 51:29
  7. stubborn heart ‒ BDB 710, KB 770, cf. Jer. 6:28; Deut. 21:18
  8. rebellious heart ‒ BDB 598, KB 632, cf. Jer. 4:17; Deut. 21:18
  9. turn aside ‒ BDB 693, KB 747, cf. Jer. 6:28; 15:5; 17:5; 32:40
  10. departed ‒ BDB 229, KB 246

Notice the emphasized personal element ("Me" and "My presence") of #5 and #6.

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:21 "O foolish and senseless people"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:21 "O foolish and senseless people" For the term "foolish" (BDB 698, KB 754), which denotes "thickheaded," see SPECIAL TOPIC: FOOLISH PEOPLE, #4.

"Senseless" (BDB 34 II) is simply a Hebrew negative. Context must determine what is negated. Here, it is the thought life and choices of disobedient covenant people who have been given a clear path but refuse to walk in it.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:22c-f
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:22c-f In these lines of poetry and Jer. 5:24 c-f, God describes Himself as the creator and sustainer of the planet. It is He who controls nature, not the false, non-existent fertility gods, who cannot.

The specific parallel passages that describe YHWH setting bounds on the waters are Gen. 1:9-10; Job 38:8-11 and Ps. 104:5-9.

Verse 23 describes rebellious covenant people as breaking through the set boundaries of God! The results of the self-assertion and self-directedness of the Fall (cf. Genesis 3) are obvious and pervasive!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:24 "Let us now fear the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:24 "Let us now fear the Lord" This is the often repeated admonition of Exod. 20:20; Deut. 4:10; Ps. 34:11; Prov. 1:7; 9:10; Eccl. 12:13; Isa. 11:2-3. However, these hearers would not respond to Him! They did not fear the Lord (cf. Jer. 2:19).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:25 "Your iniquities have turned these away"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 5:25 "Your iniquities have turned these away" The nation's sins caused these calamities (cf. Jer. 2:17; 4:18).

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:26-29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:26-29 These verses describe the wealthy, powerful leaders.

  1. lie in wait
    1. watch like fowlers
    2. set a trap
    3. catch men
  2. become great and wealthy by evil means
    1. fat (BDB 1031, cf. Deut. 32:15)
    2. sleek or skinny (BDB 799, found only here)
    3. excel in deeds of wickedness (i.e. could mean
      (1) "overlook evil," cf. Prov. 19:11; Mic. 7:18
      (2) "go beyond" as it is used in Jer. 5:22, BDB 716, KB 778)
  3. do not plead the case of the orphan and poor (LXX, "the widow")

Judgment is coming (Jer. 5:29)!

5:28
NASB  "they excel"
NKJV  "surpass"
NRSV  "know no limits"
TEV, NET  "there is no limit"
NJB  "go to any length"
JPSOA  "pass beyond"
REB  "turned a blind eye"
LXX  "transgressed"
Peshitta  "perverted"

The VERB'S (BDB 716, Qal PERFECT) root was used as a NOUN in v. 22 and referred to YHWH setting the permanent boundary of the waters. These sinners knew no boundaries (especially of YHWH's law).

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:29 "Shall I not avenge Myself"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 5:29 "Shall I not avenge Myself" This is the exact phrase in 5:9. Jeremiah's revelatory poetic messages were usually given verbally. His scribe, or later compilers, put these sermons together by word plays (cf. vv. 22, 28) or inclusio statements. Jeremiah is not in chronological order.

entries.title: Jeremiah 5:30-31
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
5:30-31 This short strophe is the conclusion of the description of the apostasy of Abraham's seed. The leaders are corrupt (cf. Jer. 2:8,26; 4:9; 5:13; 6:13; 8:10; 13:13; 14:14-16,18; 18:18) and the people not only tolerate it but revel (cf. Mic. 2:11) in their wickedness and, by implication, participate in it, or would like to! What has happened to covenant faith and faithfulness?

▣
NASB, NKJV   "the priests rule on their own authority"
NRSV   "the priests exploit the people"
NJB, TEV, JPSOA   "the priests rule as the prophets direct"
REB   "the priests are in league with them"

This question is, from what root does the VERB come?

  1. רדה ‒ BDB 921, KB 1190, Qal imperfect, "to rule" (NASB, NKJV)
  2. ירד ‒ BDB 432, KB 434, "to go down" in the sense of joining hands or cooperation (i.e. with the false prophets, cf. NJB, TEV. JPSOA, REB)

▣ "But what will you do at the end of it" This may refer to the false promises and hopes of the false prophets. What will they do when the invader comes? They will lose all credibility (cf. Deut. 18:20-22).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Where else does the concept of Jer. 5:1 appear? How is this passage related to that text?
  2. How are chapters 2 and 5 of Jeremiah related?
  3. Does Jeremiah have a good relationship to other prophets of his day?
  4. Why does Judah not listen to Jeremiah's message?

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:1 "Flee for safety"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:1 "Flee for safety" Usually the ancients fled to their fortified cities for protection (cf. Jer. 4:6, same VERB, same form). But here they are told to flee from the walled city of Jerusalem.

▣ "sons of Benjamin" This was Jeremiah's tribe. Jerusalem was very close to the territory of Benjamin (cf. Josh. 15:63), or in it (cf. Josh. 15:8,63; 18:16; Jdg. 1:21). Therefore, this is a literary way of addressing all the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

▣ "blow. . .Tekoa" This is a play on the Hebrew words (blow, ‒ תקעו, BDB 1075, cf. Jer. 4:5; Tekoa ‒ תקוע, BDB 1075) which have the same consonants (also note עקת, "alienated" is from the same root). Tekoa was a city about ten miles south of Jerusalem.

▣ "raise a signal" This refers to a fire signal (cf. Lachish Ostraca, cf. Jdg. 20:38,40), as the line above refers to an audible signal.

▣ "Beth-haccerem" This means "house of a vineyard" (BDB 108 CONSTRUCT BDB 501, cf. Neh. 3:14). This city was southwest of Jerusalem.

▣ "evil looks down from the north" Invaders from Mesopotamia had to follow the Euphrates to its head waters and then go south along the coastal plain because of the desert east of Palestine. Here the invading army is personified as "evil looks down."

6:2
NASB  "The comely and dainty one, the daugher of Zion,
  I will cut off"
NKJV  "I have likened the daughter of Zion to a lovely and
  delicate woman"
NRSV  "Beautiful, delicate as she is, I shall destroy the
  daughter of Zion"
NJB  "I have likened the dauther of Zion to the loveliest
  pasture"
LXX  "Your loftiness, O daughter of Zion, shall be removed"
JPSOA  "Fair Zion, the lovely and delicate, I will destroy"

There are three descriptive terms.

  1. comely ‒ BDB 610
    1. ADJECTIVE ‒ Song of Songs 1:5; 2:14; 6:4
    2. VERB (Piel) ‒ Isa. 52:7; Song of Songs 1:10
  2. delicately bred ‒ BDB 772, KB 851, Pual PARTICIPLE (only here)
  3. daughter of Zion ‒ common descriptive family phrase; see full note at Jer. 46:11

See a good note on this difficult phrase in UBS Handbook on Jeremiah, p. 180. The Tyndale commentary by R. K. Harrison takes the phrase as a question, "Have I compared you to a pleasant pasture?" (p. 80), like NJB.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXT INSIGHTS

  1. This continues the condemnation of Judah's sins. She had a witness in
    1. Scripture
    2. the true prophets' messages
    3. the fall of Israel (cf. Ezek. 23)

       but she would not repent.

  2. This chapter has many commands.
    1. Jer. 6:1-8 ‒ YHWH sends an invader from the north
      1. flee for safety, Jer. 6:1 ‒ BDB 731, KB 797, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
      2. blow a trumpet, Jer. 6:1 ‒ BDB 1075, KB 1785, Qal IMPERATIVE
      3. raise a signal, Jer. 6:1 ‒ BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERATIVE
      4. prepare war (lit. "sanctify"), Jer. 6:4 ‒ BDB 872, KB 1073, Piel IMPERATIVE
      5. arise, Jer. 6:4 ‒ BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal IMPERATIVE
      6. let us attack, Jer. 6:4 ‒ BDB 748, KB 828, Qal IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense
      7. arise, Jer. 6:5 ‒ same as e
      8. let us attack, Jer. 6:5 ‒ same as f
      9. destroy, Jer. 6:5 ‒ BDB 1007, KB 1469, Hiphil COHORTATIVE
      10. cut down, Jer. 6:6 ‒ BDB 503, KB 500, Qal IMPERATIVE
      11. cast up (lit. "pour out,"), Jer. 6:6 ‒ BDB 1049, KB 1629, Qal IMPERATIVE
      12. be warned, Jer. 6:8 ‒ BDB 415, KB 418, Niphal IMPERATIVE
    2. Jer. 6:9-15 ‒ YHWH's wrath burst forth
      1. pass your hand, Jer. 6:9 ‒ BDB 996, KB 1427, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
      2. speak, Jer. 6:10 ‒ BDB 180, KB 210, Piel COHORTATIVE
      3. give warning, Jer. 6:10 ‒ BDB 729, KB 795, Hiphil COHORTATIVE
      4. hear, Jer. 6:10 ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
      5. pour, Jer. 6:11 ‒ BDB 1049, KB 1629, Qal IMPERATIVE
    3. Jer. 6:16-21 ‒ possibly one of Jeremiah's sermons
      1. stand by, Jer. 6:16 ‒ BDB 763, KB 840, Qal IMPERATIVE
      2. see, Jer. 6:16 ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERATIVE
      3. ask, Jer. 6:16 ‒ BDB 981, KB 1371, Qal IMPERATIVE
      4. walk, Jer. 6:16 ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE
      5. find, Jer. 6:16 ‒ BDB 592, KB 619, Qal IMPERATIVE
      6. listen, Jer. 6:17 ‒ BDB 904, KB 1151, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
      7. know, Jer. 6:18 ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal IMPERATIVE
      8. hear, Jer. 6:18 ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE
      9. hear, Jer. 6:19 ‒ same as h
    4. Jer. 6:22-26 ‒ The invader comes!
      1. go out (negated), Jer. 6:25 ‒ BDB 422, KB 425, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
      2. walk (negated), Jer. 6:25 ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
      3. put on, Jer. 6:26 ‒ BDB 291, KB 291, Qal IMPERATIVE
      4. roll, Jer. 6:26 ‒ BDB 814, KB 935, Hithpael IMPERATIVE
      5. mourn, Jer. 6:26 ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERATIVE
    5. Jer. 6:27-30 ‒ YHWH's message to Jeremiah (much like Jer. 1:18) has no IMPERATIVES

  3. Notice the different titles for the covenant people (esp. Jerusalem).
    1. "sons of Benjamin," Jer. 6:1
    2. "the daughter of Zion," Jer. 6:2,23
    3. "Jerusalem" Jer. 6:6,8
    4. "the remnant of Israel," Jer. 6:9
    5. "My people," Jer. 6:14,27
    6. "O daughter of my people," Jer. 6:26

  4. Notice the names for YHWH.
    1. "the Lord of hosts," Jer. 6:6,9 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS
    2. "the Lord," Jer. 6:10,11,12,15,16,21,22,30 see (SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.)

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:3 "Shepherds"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:3 "Shepherds" This is a title used of God (i.e. Psalm 23) and the leaders of God's people (cf. Jer. 2:8; 3:15). Here it is imagery for the invaders who

  1. surround the city
  2. take over the surrounding lands (possibly bring their own animals in preparation of a long siege)

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:4 "Prepare"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:4 "Prepare" This translation is followed by most ancient and modern translations, but it hides the fact that the MT has "consecrate" (BDB 872, KB 1073, piel IMPERATIVE). The NJB has "prepare for holy war." This catches the implication of the Hebrew root. YHWH has "set apart" the Neo-Babylon army to do His biding (cf. Jer. 22:7; 51:27,28). This is a "reverse" Holy War!

▣ "Woe to us, for the day declines" This expresses the desire of the invaders to attack by daylight, but even if it is night, they will continue the attack (v. 5)!

▣ "at noon. . .at night" The enemy is so fierce that they attack even at unusual times.

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:4-5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:4-5 These are the words of the invaders! They will attack again and again because of the command of YHWH (cf. Jer. 6:6).

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:5 "palaces"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:5 "palaces" This is "fortified towers" or "citadels" (BDB 74, cf. Jer. 17:27; 49:27).

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:6 "cut down her trees"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:6 "cut down her trees" In Deut. 20:19-20, trees were used to build siege instruments, ramps, logs for the siege machines to roll on, firewood for the camp of the enemy, etc., for invading armies. Also the destruction of all of the fruit trees is an idiom of total, complete desolation!

▣ "This is the city to be punished" The UBS Text Project suggests a meaning to this Hebrew phrase, "this is the city which has been investigated" (p. 191). The VERB, פקר (BDB 823) in Hophal (BDB 824, #1) means "to visit" for either blessing or cursing. Here it is visitation by YHWH for the just destruction of an evil, idolatrous, unrepentant capital city (i.e. Jerusalem). What is worse, is that it was YHWH's special city, His special people.

▣ "In whose midst there is only oppression" See Jer. 22:17.

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:7 Jerusalem is compared to a constantly flowing well. As UBS Handbook on Jeremiah points out, the interpretive issue is, Does the VERB of line 1:

  1. fresh ‒ (lit. "cold," cf NET Bible) reflect a moral indifference?
  2. gushing/bubbling (JPSOA, "flows") fit the context best (NIV)?

Number 2 fits the context best. Jerusalem is constantly evil!

▣ "Violence and destruction are heard in her" Her violence (BDB 949) and destruction (BDB 994) were constant! YHWH knew this! He describes their sin as "sickness and wounds" (cf. Jer. 30:12-13; Isa. 1:5-6).

As sickness is used as imagery of sin, so healing is used as imagery for forgiveness. Notice the poetic parallelism of Ps. 103:3.

▣ "Sickness and wounds" This could refer to

  1. the sin of Jerusalem (i.e. NIV, cf. Isa. 1:4-5, where sin is described as sickness)
  2. the evil of the leaders against the poor and powerless (cf. Jer. 6:13)

▣ "are ever before Me" YHWH knows what is happening, especially with the covenant people (i.e. Exod. 3:7) who are His instrument of revelation and salvation to a lost, ignorant world. If they do not live out the covenant revelation of YHWH, then the world does not know Him! The same is now true for the Church.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:8 "Be warned"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:8 "Be warned" This is literally "accept for yourself discipline" (BDB 415, KB 418, Niphal IMPERATIVE).

▣ "Or I shall be alienated from you" This is literally "torn away" (BDB 429, KB 431, Qal IMPERFECT). It is the worst possible happening. This possibility may be alluded to in Jer. 6:4, line 1, "prepare," NASB, which is literally "sanctify" (BDB 872, KB 1073, Piel IMPERATIVE), which was a "Holy War" term. It was used to address the invaders in Jer. 6:6, but here Judah hopes YHWH will be on her side, but He will not!

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:9 YHWH calls on the invaders to "thoroughly glean" (BDB 760, KB 834; this is the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Poel IMPERFECT VERB of the same root, used for intensity; see SPECIAL TOPIC: GLEANINGS). Nothing will be left, everyone will be exiled or killed. This may be hyperbolic because of Jer. 4:27; 5:10,18; 30:11; 46:28.

The TEV takes this phrase to refer to Jeremiah reaching as many as possible with YHWH's message of repentance (i.e. the remnant).

▣ "the remnant of Israel" For the theological concept of "remnant" see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (three senses).

For "Israel" see SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name). One wonders if it means

  1. the northern ten tribes (exiled in 722 B.C.)
  2. the collective name for Abraham's seed from Jacob. The two nations, Israel and Judah, will be unified again, but by judgment!

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:10 "their ears are closed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:10 "their ears are closed" In Jer. 6:10 Jeremiah responds to YHWH's charge to keep proclaiming his message. Israel's ears are "uncircumcised" (BDB 790, cf. Jer. 4:4; 9:25-26). They will not/cannot respond (i.e. "listen," BDB 904, KB 1151, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT). This is very similar to Isa. 6:9-13.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CIRCUMCISION, IV. C.

▣ "They have no delight in it" God's word (Scripture or the prophetic word or both) was meant to be a joyous thing (cf. Ps. 19:7-10). They have made it a "reproach" (BDB 357).

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:11 Notice how YHWH is described.

  1. full of wrath
  2. weary with holding it in (cf. Jer. 15:6)
  3. will pour it out (cf. Jer. 7:20) on
    1. children
    2. young men
    3. husband and wife
    4. the very old

This means YHWH's judgment has arrived and it will affect the whole of society (i.e. reverse Holy War, cf. Jer. 6:13,21).

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:12 This verse (Jer. 6:12-15 are repeated in Jer. 8:10-12) describes the consequences of resisting both the Assyrian and Neo-Babylonian armies. They moved conquered people hundreds of miles and relocated others in their homes and on their fields (i.e. Deut. 28:30,38-40; Amos 5:11; Micah 6:15).

Notice also that it is not the power of the gods of the invaders/exilers, but the judgment of YHWH on His own people for their sin and idolatry.

For "I will stretch out My hand," see SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND.

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:13 Every segment of society is sinful (cf. Jer. 8:10; 16:6; 31:34; 42:1). All are sinful, all will be judged (cf. Jer. 6:11, cf. Rom. 3:10-18).

▣ "greedy for gain" This phrase is from the NOUN and VERB of the same root (BDB130, KB 147, cf. Jer. 8:10; 22:17). It characterizes the wealthy and powerful of Judah's society.

▣ "from the prophet even to the priest" All of Judah's leadership are corrupt. They lie (BDB 1055). There was no one to trust (cf. Jer. 9:1)!

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:14 "They have healed the brokenness of My people superficially"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:14 "They have healed the brokenness of My people superficially" The false prophets (cf. Jer. 8:10-11; 14:14; 23:10-22) and priests denied the problem and tried to cover up the consequences of invasion and exile (cf. Jer. 8:11; Ezek. 13:10; Micah 3:5).

▣ "Peace" This is the Hebrew Shalom (BDB 1022, KB 1532), which means the absence of bad and the presence of good. However, it was a false message!

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (shalom)

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:15 God's people were not ashamed (BDB 101, KB 116, Hiphil PERFECT, cf. Jer. 3:3; 8:12). They will be!

This same VERB root is repeated in line 2 in an intensified grammatical form (i.e. INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT VERB). Jeremiah uses this root many times.

▣ "they shall fall among those who fall" There is a word play on

  1. Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 656, KB 709)
  2. Qal PARTICIPLE (BDB 656, KB 709)

What happened to other rebels will happen to them. This is possibly an allusion to the previous fall of Israel by Assyria in 722 B.C.

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:16 YHWH uses five IMPERATIVES to call His people back to His covenant with them but they refused (see Contextual Insights).

God's truths and guidelines were pictured as a clearly marked path (cf. Jer. 18:15; 31:21; Psalm 119; 105; 139:24; Prov. 6:23). This godly path brought rest and peace but they would not!

Lifestyle faith is characterized by the VERB "walk" in both the OT and NT (cf. Eph. 2:10; 4:1,17; 5:2,15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WAY. . .THE PATH

▣ "you will find rest for your souls" Jesus quotes this in Matt. 11:29. His teachings fulfill the "ancient paths" (i.e. Moses, cf. Jer. 18:15) and surpasses them (cf. Matt. 5:17-19,21-48; the book of Hebrews).

For "souls" (nephesh) see notes online at Gen. 35:18; Lev. 17:11; Ezek. 18:4.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:17 "watchmen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:17 "watchmen" This imagery refers to the prophets (cf. Ezek. 3:16-21; 33:7).

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:18-19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:18-19 There is a parallelism between

  1. O nations (BDB 156)
  2. O congregation (BDB 417 II). This line of Jer. 6:18 is left untranslated by AB because of its difficulty and uncertainty, the UBS Handbook on Jeremiah suggests that "O congregation" be revocalized to an INFINITIVE of "know," thereby intensifying the VERB "know" (BDB 393, KB 390; see SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW), p. 196
  3. O earth (BDB 75)

These seem to be imagery for witnesses to court testimony and judgment (similar to "O heavens. . . O earth"). Each is matched with an IMPERATIVE.

For "earth" see SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH (ארץ)

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:19 "The fruit of their plans"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:19 "The fruit of their plans" They are reaping what they sowed. This is a recurrent biblical theme (cf. Jer. 17:10). See full list of texts on this biblical truth in Gal. 6:7-10.

▣ "My words. . .My law" YHWH's people were His in name only! They rejected both the Torah/Law of Moses (i.e. the ancient paths, cf. Ps. 16:11; 139:24), as well as the word of the true prophets (cf. Isa. 1:10; 5:24). Their lack of spiritual discernment is exemplified by their devotion to

  1. idolatry
  2. false prophets (cf. Isa. 29:13)
  3. greed and exploitation of the poor

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:20 This is sacrificial terminology.

  1. frankincense, BDB 526 I, cf. Exod. 30:34-38; Lev. 2:1, this was used for temple incense; it comes from Sheba (i.e. modern Yemen)
  2. sweet cane, BDB 373 II and 889, cf. Exod. 30:23-25, this was one term for the holy anointing oil, possibly from India
  3. burnt offerings, BDB 750, these were wholly burnt offerings symbolizing total dedication (see SPECIAL TOPIC: BURNT OFFERINGS)
  4. sacrifices, BDB 257, cf. Lev. 7:15-18; 19:5-8, the offerer retained part for a fellowship meal to eat with friends and YHWH (see SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE OFFERING)

▣ "your sacrifices are not pleasing to Me" This is a shocking phrase (cf. Jer. 7:21-23; Isa. 1:11-14; Hosea 6:6; Amos 5:21-23; Micah 6:6-7). It was not the sacrificial system (which YHWH instigated), but the attitude and faithless lifestyle of the worshipers that He rejected (i.e. Cain, Gen. 4, also note Jer. 7:23; Isa. 1:16-17; Amos 5:24; Micah 6:8).

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:21 The imagery of this verse refers to the "ancient paths" of Jer. 6:16. As walking on the path of God (i.e. Scripture, or the prophetic word) was a source of life, peace, and joy, anything that blocked that path (cf. Isa. 8:14-15) caused pain, trouble, and confusion. The path God's people were on was not His path! They refused to listen and repent, so there were societal and individual consequences! YHWH disciplines His people for their ultimate good!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:22-26
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:22-26 This strophe describes the Mesopotamian invaders (cf. Jer. 50:41-43).

  1. they come from the north
  2. they are a great nation
  3. they are aroused by God
  4. they seize bow and spear (BDB 475 I, "javelin" in 1 Sam. 17:6 or "sword" in DSS)
  5. they are cruel and have no mercy (cf. Isa. 13:18)
  6. their voices roar (cf. Isa. 5:30; 17:12)
  7. they ride horses (cf. Jer. 4:13,19)

It also describes Zion's response.

  1. they have heard the report
  2. their hands are limp (from fear, cf. Isa. 13:7; Zeph. 3:16)
  3. anguish seizes them (like childbirth)
  4. they (Qere) are afraid to travel
  5. they grieve (see SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES)
    1. put on sackcloth
    2. roll in ashes (cf. Jer. 25:34)
    3. mourn as for an only son (cf. Amos 8:10; Zech. 12:10)
    4. lament bitterly

The destroyer will come suddenly!

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:23 "O daughter of Zion"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:23 "O daughter of Zion" See full notes at Jer. 46:11.

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:25 "Terror is on every side"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 6:25 "Terror is on every side" This is a recurrent phrase in Jeremiah (cf. Jer. 20:3-4,10; 46:5; 49:29).

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:27-30
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:27-30 This strophe is directed towards Jeremiah (cf. Jer. 1:18). YHWH has made him

  1. an assayer (BDB 103)
  2. a tester (NASB, LXX, REB)
  3. a fortification (BDB 131, NKJV)
  4. a refiner (NJB, JPSOA)

These are rare usages of these roots, which usually denote towers and fortifications, but the context of Jer. 6:27-30 demands it.

The strophe continues by YHWH's description of His people.

  1. stubborn (BDB 711)
  2. rebellious (BDB 710, KB 779, Qal PARTICIPLE)
  3. talebearers (BDB 940)
  4. bronze and iron (cf. Ezek. 22:18)
  5. corrupt (BDB 1007, KB 1469, Hiphil PARTICIPLE)

YHWH tries to purify them as silver (BDB 549, KB 540, Niphal PARTICIPLE) but they would not, therefore, He has "rejected them" (BDB 549, KB 540, Qal PERFECT).

entries.title: Jeremiah 6:29 "fire"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:29 "fire" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

▣ "the refining goes on" This is a Qal PERFECT VERB used to show intensity.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Is there any hope?
  2. Why is God so upset with Judah?

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:1 Notice the titles for God in this chapter.

  1. "the Lord" (YHWH), Jer. 7:1,2,13,19,29,30; see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.
  2. "the Lord of hosts," Jer. 7:3,21; see SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS
  3. "the God (Elohim) of Israel," Jer. 7:3,21 (LXX, Jer. 7:1); see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.
  4. "the Lord (Adon) God (YHWH)," Jer. 7:20; see SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (Adon and Kurios)
  5. "I will be your God (Elohim), Jer. 7:23 (note the covenant language)
  6. "the Lord their God," Jer. 7:28

The tragedy of this sermon is that it is directed to the covenant people who had YHWH's revelation (promises, covenants, cultus, prophets, cf. Rom. 9:4-5), but were not loyal to Him.

Notice how specific YHWH's message is to Jeremiah. These are not Jeremiah's thoughts and opinions. These are God's words, directed to His people, about their cavalier treatment of His name and worship!

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION, I. A. #1, a.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

BRIEF HISTORY

  1. Judah alone is left as God's covenant people. The Northern Ten Tribes have been in exile since 722 B.C. (i.e. Fall of Samaria to Assyria).

    SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF ASSYRIA

  2. Assyrian power has been completely broken by Neo-Babylon (605 B.C.; the battle of Carchemish). The remnant of the Assyrian army attempted to join forces with the Egyptian army. Josiah, Judah's godly king, tried to intervene and was killed by Egypt's army at Meggido. His son, Jehoahaz, reigned only three months before Pharaoh Necho II of Egypt placed his brother, Jehoiakim (609-597 B.C.), on the throne of Judah as his vassal.

    SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF NEO-BABYLON

  3. Jeremiah 7:1-15 and Jer. 26 ("in the beginning of Jehoiakim's reign") recount the same sermon and its effect.

  4. This is one of the most powerful sermons in the OT. Jeremiah attacks faithless ritual and liturgy (cf. Jer. 7:16; 8:3; Isa. 29:13). Religion without personal faith in YHWH is a disaster!

  5. The NASB Study Bible (p. 1065) asserts that Jer. 7:1-10:25 is a series of temple sermons over several years.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:2 "Stand in the gate. . .gates"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:2 "Stand in the gate. . .gates" This is a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 763, KB 840). Kimchi (Jewish commentator of the Middle Ages) says Jeremiah preached this sermon seven times (SINGULAR vs. PLURAL), once at each gate of the temple. The gates were the focal point of temple traffic. The temple itself was the place of the people's legalistic, liturgical, sacramental religion.

▣ "Hear the word of the Lord" This is another Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033, KB 1570), which means "to hear so as to do" (cf. Deut. 4:1; 5:1; 6:3,4; 9:1; 20:3; 27:10; 33:7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ "all you of Judah" Every male above the age of thirteen assembled regularly at the temple.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:3 "Lord of hosts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:3 "Lord of hosts" This refers to

  1. the captain of the army of heaven
  2. the leader of the heavenly council

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

▣ "Amend" The VERB "amend" (BDB 405, KB 408, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, cf. vv. 3,5,6) is normally translated "do good" (cf. Jer. 10:5). In this context it denotes changing from evil to good (cf. Jer. 7:5). It was another literary way to call for repentance (cf. Jer. 4:1). This VERB in the Hiphil denotes ethical behavior in Gen. 4:7; Lev. 5:4; Isa. 1:17; Jer. 4:22; 13:23. The covenant is both conditional ("if. . .then," Jer. 7:5,6) and unconditional (YHWH's character and promises) to every generation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "let you dwell in this place" The VERB (BDB 1014, KB 1490) is a Piel COHORTATIVE. The Vulgate and Aquilla's version have "I will dwell with you" (cf. 1 Kgs. 6:12-13; NJB). This involves only a revocalization of the Masoretic Text (as it does in Jer. 7:7). The UBS Text Project, p. 195, gives the first option a C rating (considerable doubt).

The second option is theologically attractive because biblical faith is a trusting relationship with YHWH before it is a land promise! The greatest blessing is YHWH's personal presence (i.e. Immanuel, cf. Isa. 7:14; see SPECIAL TOPIC: IMMANUEL'S PERSON AND REIGN).

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:4 "Do not trust in deceptive words"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:4 "Do not trust in deceptive words" The VERB "trust" (BDB 105, KB 120, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) is an important theological concept, repeated in Jer. 7:8 (Qal PARTICIPLE). The words of the priests and prophets (cf. Jer. 7:13) who served in Jerusalem in the temple were false (cf. Jer. 6:14; 8:11). They probably used 2 Sam. 7:11-14; 1 Kgs. 8:13; and Isaiah's message (i.e. Isaiah 36-39) as proof texts to back up their false optimism. They had forgotten the conditional nature of the covenant (cf. Jer. 7:5).

▣ "This is the temple of the Lord" This phrase possibly refers to a chorus the temple choir regularly sang. In Hebrew a three form repetition expresses a superlative degree (cf. Isa. 6:3, e.g. Holy, Holy, Holy = the most holy; as note Jer. 22:29; Ezek. 21:27). They were trusting in the place of worship not the person to be worshiped! Form without faith (cf. Isa. 29:13; 2 Tim. 3:5)!

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:5 "if"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:5 "if" The "if" (conditional element) of this context is crucial (note the four "if" clauses).

▣ The MT has two intensified grammatical structures in v. 5.

  1. a Hiphil INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a Hiphil IMPERFECT VERB of the same root (BDB 405, KB 408), "if you truly amend your ways"
  2. a Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Qal IMPERFECT VERB of the same root (BDB 793, KB 889), "if you truly practice justice"

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:6 Notice the observable conditional activities which reveal a true faith lifestyle.

  1. practice justice between a man and his neighbor, Jer. 7:5
  2. do not oppress, Jer. 7:6
    1. the alien (foreigner living in Judah)
    2. the orphan
    3. the widow
  3. do not shed innocent blood in this place, Jer. 7:6
  4. do not walk after other gods to your own ruin, Jer. 7:6

▣ "alien, the orphan, or the widow" God loves and protects the helpless and weak. This is a recurrent theme of Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 10:18; 24:17; 26:12-13; 27:19; Jer. 10:18; 14:29; 16:11,14; 22:3; 24:17,19,20,21; 26:12,13; 27:19).

▣ "walk after other gods" This is a Hebraic expression of lifestyle idolatry (cf. Jer. 13:10; Deut. 6:14-15; 8:19; 11:28; 1 Kgs. 8:25).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:7 "forever and ever"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:7 "forever and ever" This Hebrew phrase must be interpreted in light of the context of the conditional and unconditional aspects of the Mosaic covenant. To prooftext this phrase as a promise to depend on is a false message!

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:8 See note at Jer. 7:4.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:9 This is a summary of the Sinai revelation (i.e. Ten Commantments).

  1. steal ‒ BDB 170, KB 198, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
  2. murder ‒ BDB 953, KB 1283, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
  3. commit adultery ‒ BDB 610, KB 658, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
  4. swear falsely ‒ BDB 989, KB 1396, Niphal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
  5. offer sacrifices to Ba'al ‒ BDB 882, KB 1094, Piel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
  6. walk after other gods ‒ BDB 229, IB 246, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE

SPECIAL TOPIC: NOTES ON EXODUS 20

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:10 "then come and stand before Me in this house"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:10 "then come and stand before Me in this house" Both VERBS are Qal PERFECTS with waw (settled condition). This shows the hypocrisy of formal religion apart from personal lifestyle faith and obedience (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:23; Ezek. 23:36-45; Luke 6:46).

▣ "in this house, which is called by My name" This is a recurrent title for Solomon's temple in Jerusalem (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:43; 2 Chr. 6:33; 20:9; Jer. 7:10,11,14,30; 25:29; 32:34; 34:15). It is thus titled because YHWH, symbolically dwells there between the wings of the cherubim over the ark of the covenant.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

▣ "We are delivered" This is a Niphal PERFECT (BDB 664, KB 717). They thought that religious acts in a religious place would bring deliverance (i.e. no defeat and exile by Neo-Babylon, cf. Jer. 39:17).

▣ "that you may do all these abominations" The covenant people turned their faith into a license to sin! Ritual replaced lifestyle faithfulness! Our life reveals our true self (cf. Matthew 7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:11 "den of robbers"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:11 "den of robbers" What a shocking phrase to describe Solomon's temple in light of 1 Kgs. 8:41-43,60. Jesus uses this same phrase in Matt. 21:13; Mark 11:17; Luke 19:46 to describe the temple procedures occurring in the court of the Gentiles in His day.

▣
NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "I, even I, have seen it"
NRSV  "I, at any rate, can see straight"
TEV  "I have seen what you are doing"
NJB  "You know, I too am watching"
LXX  "And I, behold, I have seen it"
JPSOA  "As for Me, I have been watching"
REB  "I warn you, I myself have seen all this"

The Hebrew is ambiguous but the sense is clear. YHWH knows and is involved in what happens on earth and especially with His covenant people (i.e. Exod. 3:7-9).

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:12 "Shiloh"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:12 "Shiloh" "Go" (BDB 229, KB 246) and "see" (BDB 906, KB 1157) are both Qal IMPERATIVES. Shiloh was the first sanctuary in the Promised Land where the tabernacle and the Ark dwelt. It was destroyed by the Philistines and the Ark captured in 1050 B.C. (the event is not recorded in the OT but alluded to in Jer. 26:6; Ps. 78:60). This should have shown the covenant people their theology of God's covenant protection without conditions was not correct.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:13 "I spoke to you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:13 "I spoke to you" This refers to the prophets (cf. Jer. 7:25).

▣ "rising up early" This is imagery for the often and repeated attempts by YHWH to address His people through the prophets (cf. Jer. 7:25; 11:7; 25:3-4; 26:5; 29:19; 32:33; 35:14-15; 44:4)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:14 "the house. . .in which you trust"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:14 "the house. . .in which you trust" There are no special places or things to those who truly know God (cf. Jer. 26:6; John 4:23-24). All places, things, and especially people are holy and sacred because of God's presence and creation. They turned faith into a place and ritual instead of a daily, godly faith relationship (cf. 1 Kgs. 6:12-13). This is also true of the church building and Sunday services in modern western countries!

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:15 "all the offspring of Ephraim"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:15 "all the offspring of Ephraim" This is a reference to the exile of the Northern Ten Tribes in 722 B.C. by Assyria. What happened to them should have been a warning to Judah but it was not (cf. Jer. 3:11; Ezek. 16:51-52; 23:11). Judah also will be "cast out" (two Hiphil PEFECTS, BDB 1020, KB 1527).

The northern tribes came to be known by three titles.

  1. Israel (a collective term)
  2. Ephraim (the largest tribe and the tribe of the person who instigated the split, Jeroboam I)
  3. Samaria (the fortified capital; it fell in 722 B.C. to Assyria

Just a note about "the northern ten tribes." This was not a numerically accurate title. Judah was made up of the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Simeon, and most of the Levites. Remember, there were 13 sons of Jacob/Joseph, only twelve who inherited land.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:16 Because of Judah's reluctance to repent, YHWH tells Jeremiah not to

  1. pray for them ‒ BDB 813, KB 933, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  2. lift up cry or prayer for them ‒ BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  3. intercede ‒ BDB 803, KB 910, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

This is repeated in Jer. 11:14! He will not hear (cf. Jer. 11:11; Ps. 18:41; Prov. 1:28; Isa. 1:15; Hosea 5:6). There are consequences to repeated, hardened unrepentant people!

Westerners must be cognizant of the hyperbolic nature of eastern literature. Often they say things to arrest people's attention. Here are some examples.

  1. Jer. 7:16; 11:14; 14:11 ‒ do not pray for them
  2. Jer. 7:20 ‒ YHWH's anger on the temple and Judah will be like a fire that will never be quenched
  3. Jer. 11:11 ‒ YHWH will not hear their prayers for help
  4. Jer. 23:40 ‒ YHWH sends everlasting reproach and humiliation that will not be forgotten
  5. Hosea 9:15 ‒ YHWH hates them, does not love them, will drive them out of His temple

For a good brief discussion of hyperbole, see G. B. Caird, The Language and Imagery of the Bible, pp. 110-117.

SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:18 The entire family was caught up in and taught idolatry, but especially the wife. Parent do influence and stamp their children with their own lifestyles and priorities (cf. Exod. 20:5-6).

▣ "cakes" This refers to the sacrificial raisin cakes made in Astarte's image which was given to worshipers. This was family worship, but of idols (cf. Jer. 44:19; Hosea 3:1).

▣ "queen of heaven" This was possibly the fertility goddess of Babylon, Ishtar (who is called "the Queen of heaven" [Venus], cf. Jer. 44:17-19,25). Worship of her (Venus) involved giving worshipers "sweet cakes," cf. Jer. 44:19. Other examples of idol worship are 19:13; 32:29; 44:17-19; 2 Kgs. 23:4-14.

The LXX has "host of heaven," which would make it Babylonian astrology.

However, it is possible that this was an Assyrian goddess which came into Judah through political alliance ceremonies or even Asherah, the Canaanite goddess.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

▣ "they pour out drink offerings to other gods" This was part of the worship (cf. Jer. 19:13; 44:18; Ezek. 20:28).

▣ "in order to spite Me" The VERB (BDB 494, KB 491, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Deut. 31:29) is repeated in Jer. 7:19 (Hiphil PARTICIPLE). YHWH is a jealous God! He wants faithful worship. Idolatry is an affront to Him (i.e. spiritual adultery, cf. Jer. 11:17; 32:29; Deut. 32:16,21; 1 Kgs. 14:9; 16:2; Ezek. 8:7-18).

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUS. . .ZEALOUS

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:20 YHWH's anger (BDB 60 I) and wrath (BDB 404) "will be poured out" (BDB 677, KB 732, Niphal PARTICIPLE), which is a different word from "poured out" in Jer. 7:18 (BDB 659, KB 703). The one in Jer. 7:18 is used of a sacrifice, but this one is used of poured out wrath.

▣ Notice how God's judgment affects God's Promised Land. The curses of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28 are coming to reality.

  1. on man
  2. on beast
  3. on trees of the field (cf. Jer. 8:13)
  4. on the fruit of the ground

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:21 The rejection of sacrifices by YHWH is a recurrent theme (see full note at Jer. 6:20 and note 14:12; Isa. 1:11; Amos 5:21). That which was designed to bring sinful mankind back to YHWH (i.e. Leviticus 1-7) had been completely perverted into ritual and liturgy only!

▣ "burnt offerings" These were sacrifices that were totally consumed on the altar (BDB 750).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BURNT OFFERINGS

▣ "sacrifices and eat flesh" In some sacrifices only part was burnt and the rest was eaten by priests or the offerer (BDB 257). The Jews did not eat meat regularly. They were offering sacrifices to God just so they could have the meat to eat!

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE OFFERING

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:22 "For I did not speak. . .concerning burnt offerings and sacrifices"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:22 "For I did not speak. . .concerning burnt offerings and sacrifices" This is not a total rejection of ritual sacrifices, but an emphasis on the motive behind the sacrifice and the offerer's faith relationship with YHWH (cf. 1 Sam. 15:22; Ps. 51:16-17; Isa. 1:11-14; Hosea 6:6; Amos 5:21-24; Micah 6:6-8).

It is surprising that in Exodus 19-20, which describes God's teachings revealed at Sinai, no mention of the sacrificial cultus is made.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:23 "this is what I commanded them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:23 "this is what I commanded them" Exodus 19-20 shows that the covenant was primarily ethical living, not ritual acts of devotion. Obedience is crucial (cf. Exod. 19:5-6; Deut. 6:3; Isa. 1:19), but so is attitude (cf. Deut. 30:15-20)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "I will be your God, and you will be My people" This is covenant language (cf. Jer. 11:4; Exod. 6:7; Lev. 26:12; Deut. 26:17-18). Notice the conditional connotation (i.e. obedience [lit. "hear" Qal IMPERATIVE] to the covenant).

For the concept of "covenant" see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "that it may be well with you" God wants to give us joy and abundance (cf. Deuteronomy 27-28), but it is conditional (cf. Jer. 26:13; 38:20; 42:6).

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:24 This verse expressed the reality of His covenant people's condition (cf. Ezek. 20:8,13,16,21), as Jer. 7:23 expresses the hope.

  1. they did not obey
  2. they did not incline their ear
  3. they walked in their own counsels (or by revocalization, "their disobedience")
  4. they walked in the stubbornness of their evil heart
  5. they went backward and not forward

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:25 "My servants the prophets"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:25 "My servants the prophets" YHWH sent His people prophets again and again, but they would not listen. Israel/Judah was His vineyard (cf. Isa. 5:1-7; Jer. 12:10). He planted in her His best vines (cf. Jer. 2:21), but they produced only bad/wild grapes (i.e. sin and rebellion). Because of this, He will send judgment on His vineyard (i.e. foreign armies, cf. Jer. 5:17; 8:13).

One wonders how much of this repeated story Jesus picks up on in His parable of the wicked tenant farmers (cf. Matt. 21:33-46; Mark 12:1-12; Luke 20:9-19). He saw Himself as the vineyard owner's "son" and the covenant people as the wicked tenant farmers! Jesus' parable closes with a quote from Ps. 118:22-23.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:25-26
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:25-26 These verses express the rebellious acts of YHWH's people. From the very beginning they were repeatedly unresponsive to Him (cf. Neh. 9:16-19; see SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS). He tried and tried (cf. Jer. 7:13; 25:3-4; 29:19; 35:14-15; 44:4) to communicate with them, but they would not hear and respond (cf. Jer. 17:23; 19:15).

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:27
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:27 This verse is theologically parallel to Isa. 6:9-10! However, Jeremiah must speak YHWH's message (cf. Jer. 26:2; Ezek. 2:7).

The message is Jer. 7:28-34.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:28
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:28 Notice again (cf. Jer. 7:24) how YHWH characterizes His people.

  1. they did not obey
  2. they did not accept correction
  3. they allowed truth to
    1. perish
    2. be cut off from their mouth

▣ "truth" This is literally "faithfulness" and refers both to their faith relationship with YHWH and obedience to His covenant.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:29 Verse 29 is a poem amidst prose. It has three IMPERATIVES.

  1. cut off your hair ‒ BDB 159, KB 186, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. cast it away ‒ BDB 1020, KB 1527, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  3. take up lamentation ‒ BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERATIVE

These acts are grieving rites (cf. Jer. 41:5; Isa. 22:12). See SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

The reason for the grieving is that YHWH has

  1. rejected ‒ BDB 549, KB 540, Qal PERFECT
  2. forsaken ‒ BDB 643, KB 695, Qal IMPERFECT (with waw)

Because of Jer. 16:6; 48:37 (Isa. 15:2) it could refer to idolatrous rites (cf. Lev. 21:5; Deut. 14:1).

▣ "lamentation on the bare heights" This possibly refers to the very high places of Canaanite fertility worship.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:30
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:30 This refers to the idols the covenant people put in YHWH's temple (cf. Jer. 32:34; 2 Kgs. 21:4-5,7; 23:4-14; 2 Chr. 33:4,5,7; Ezek. 8:3,5). What a shocking sin. They were probably related to political alliances and Canaanite fertility cults.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:31 "Topheth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:31 "Topheth" The root of this term (BDB 1075, KB 1781 II) is either from Aramaic, "hearth" or Hebrew, "to speak." This is a reference to the worship of Molech (cf. Lev. 18:21; 20:2-5; see SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH), the Phoenician fire god to whom children were sacrificed (cf. Jer. 19:6,11-12; Lev. 18:21; 2 Kgs. 16:3; 17:17; 21:6; 23:10; 2 Chr. 28:3; 33:6; Ps. 106:37,38). This type of worship possibly developed from a misunderstanding of Exod. 13:2.

▣ "the valley of the son of Hinnom" See Gehenna in SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DEAD, WHERE ARE THEY? (Sheol/Hades, Gehenna, Tartarus), II. D.

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:32 See Jeremiah 19:6-7! A Terrible judgment is coming!

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:33 "food for the birds of the sky"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:33 "food for the birds of the sky" This is a common imagery of "the last days" (cf. Jer. 12:9; Isa. 18:4; Ezek. 29:5; 32:4; 39:4). This is one of the specific judgments of Deuteronomy 28 (cf. Deut. 28:26).

entries.title: Jeremiah 7:34
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:34 YHWH wanted to give peace and joy (cf. Jer. 7:13), but because of their idolatrous rebellion He will give judgment (cf. Jer. 16:9; 25:10).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. How does this sermon relate to our day?
  2. Is ritual or form bad? Can it become evil? What is the difference?
  3. Was Jeremiah condemning the sacrificial system?
  4. What was Judah's major sin?

entries.title: Jeremiah 8:1 "they will bring out the bones. . ."
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:1 "they will bring out the bones. . ." Notice how the entire population is mentioned by a series of different groups.

  1. kings of Judah
  2. its princes
  3. priests
  4. the prophets
  5. the inhabitants of Jerusalem

This act of bringing out the bones of buried Judeans has the following symbolic meaning:

  1. the invaders were looking for buried valuables
  2. it is connected with the astral worship of Neo-Babylon (cf. Jer. 8:2)
  3. it was a cultural act of hatred and contempt for conquered Judah (cf. Amos 2:1)
