READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. Jeremiah 14 and 15 are a literary unit concerning a divinely sent drought that is coming to the land of Palestine.

  2. Jeremiah 14:1 may be an introduction to the entire literary unit.

  3. Again the method of arrangement of the strophe and prose sections seems to be sound plays. Jeremiah, like Isaiah, is an anthology and is not structured chronologically.

  4. The UBS Handbook For Translators of Jeremiah outlines the unit as follows (pp. 344-345).
    1. Jer. 14:2-6 ‒ Jeremiah bemoans the drought
    2. Jer. 14:7-9 ‒ the people of Judah confess their sin and ask for help
    3. Jer. 14:10-12 ‒ YHWH replies with a threat instead of mercy
    4. Jer. 14:13 ‒ Jeremiah blames the situation on the false prophets
    5. Jer. 14:14-16 ‒ YHWH will judge both the fake prophets and those who hear and believe them
    6. Jer. 14:17-18 ‒ Jeremiah's vision of the coming destruction
    7. Jer. 14:19-22 ‒ the people pray as they did in Jer. 14:7-9 but with more intensity
    8. Jer. 15:1-9 ‒ YHWH responds to their prayer. No intercessor can remove the guilt which began with King Manasseh. Slaughter will come.
    9. Jer. 15:10-21 ‒ Jeremiah honestly speaks to YHWH about his life
      1. Jeremiah, Jer. 14:10-12
      2. YHWH, Jer. 14:13-14
      3. Jeremiah, Jer. 14:15-18
      4. YHWH, Jer. 14:19-21

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:2 This verse contains a series of mourning VERBS.

  1. Judah mourns ‒ BDB 5, KB 6, Qal PERFECT
  2. her gates languish ‒ BDB 51, KB 63 Pulal PERFECT, cf. Jer. 15:9)
  3. they sit on the ground in mourning (lit. "in black") ‒ BDB 871, KB 1072, Qal PERFECT, cf. Jer. 8:21; Job 5:11; 30:28
  4. the cry of Jerusalem has ascended ‒ BDB 748, KB 828, Qal PERFECT

The drought caused the Judeans to pray (cf. Jer. 14:7-9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

▣ "her gates" This is the place where the life of the city was centralized. It was a place of social and civic justice (i.e. Deut. 16:18; Ruth 4). Here, they are personified and are imagery for all the people of the city.

▣ "the cry of Jerusalem has ascended" The prayers of these unrepentant idolaters will not be heard (cf. Jer. 11:11; Isa. 1:15; Zech. 7:13).

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:3 This verse describes the wealthy seeking water.

  1. sent their servants (lit. "little ones," cf. Jer. 48:4)
  2. came to the cisterns (cf. Jer. 2:13)
  3. returned with vessels empty

Therefore, the wealthy

  1. have been put to shame (BDB 101, KB 116, Qal PERFECT)
  2. have been humiliated (BDB 483, KB 480, Hophal PERFECT)
  3. cover their heads (BDB 341, KB 339, Qal PERFECT)

▣ As Jer. 14:3 describes the wealthy, Jer. 14:4 describes the farmer's problem (i.e. no water).

  1. the ground is cracked
  2. there has been no rain

Therefore, the farmers

  1. have been put to shame (BDB 101, KB 116, Qal PERFECT)
  2. have covered their heads (BDB 341, KB 339, Qal PERFECT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:5-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:5-6 The results of the drought on the wildlife is described.

  1. v. 5, the doe abandons her young
  2. v. 6, the donkeys pant for air like jackals (i.e. stress caused by high temperatures)

All creation is affected by human sin (cf. Genesis 3; Rom. 8:18-23), note Jer. 12:4,11!  YHWH's covenant was targeted to agricultural blessings of the ANE. Its violation resulted in agricultural failures (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-28).

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:7 Verse 7 should begin a new paragraph (cf. NKJV, NRSV, NJB). Notice the thrust of the verse is a corporate intercession ("our," "we"). Jeremiah basically confesses the following sins of the people.

  1. our iniquities
  2. our apostasies have been many
  3. we have sinned against You

Here, Jeremiah collectively confesses the sins of Israel, like Abraham, Moses (see note at Jer. 15:1), the high priest (i.e. Leviticus 16), or like the father of a family (i.e. Job 1:5).

It is also possible that Jer. 14:7-9 were temple liturgy, said on specific feast or fast days.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

▣ "O Lord, act for Your name's sake" Jeremiah does not plead for God's forgiveness based on the people's worthiness, but on God's character (cf. Ezek. 20:9,14,22,24; 36:22,23). He is the God who acts (BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERATIVE). The hope of Israel is in the character of God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

▣ Notice how Judah is described.

  1. apostasies have been many (cf. Jer. 5:6; 7:24; 8:5)
  2. we have sinned against You (all sin is against YHWH, cf. Ps. 51:4)

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:8 YHWH (specified in the LXX of Jer. 14:8) is described by two covenant titles.

  1. O Hope of Israel ‒ this refers to YHWH as the God of the Patriarchs (cf. Jer. 17:13; 50:7)
  2. Savior ‒ this is a common characterization or title in Isaiah (cf. Jer. 19:20; 43:3,11; 45:15,21; 49:26; 60:16; 63:8)

SPECIAL TOPIC: OUR SAVIOR

▣  "Why are You like a stranger in the land

 Or like a traveler who has pitched his tent for the night" This is very similar to Jer. 9:2. Verses 8c-9e are the people's response to Jeremiah's message. They suggest a shocking picture of YHWH as someone who is incapable and doesn't care, when in reality, He cared deeply as we have seen in Jer. 8:18-9:16. It was not YHWH's weakness but the people's sin that forced Him to act. The problem was not YHWH but idolatry (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-28).

14:9
NASB  "dismayed"
NKJV  "astonished"
NRSV  "bemused"
TEV  "taken by surprise"
NJB  "confused"
JPSOA  "who is stunned"
REB  "suddenly overcome"
LXX  "asleep"
NET Bible  "helpless"

This is the only time this word appears in the OT. The Hebrew term (BDB 187, KB 214, Niphal PARTICIPLE), according to BDB, means "astonish," but KB alludes to a seventh century B.C. inscription where it contextually means "helpless." Hapax Legomenon (words used only once) are so hard to translate. The proper procedure is to look at

  1. the basic meaning of the root
  2. the root in cognate languages
  3. the context (strophe)
  4. the parallelism (poetic lines)
  5. possible parallel passages in Scripture
  6. usage outside Scripture

The LXX's meaning comes from a one consonant change in the MT.

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:9c-e
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:9c-e This is theologically similar to Jer. 14:7b. It magnifies YHWH.

  1. You are in our midst ‒ this could refer to
    1. the temple (cf. Jer. 8:19)
    2. the promise of His personal presence with His people (i.e. the Cloud, the Ark, the promise of Immanuel)
      SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH
      SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT
  2. we are called by Your name (cf. Jer. 15:16; Isa. 63:19)
    SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

Because of these two truths, these lines ask YHWH not to forsake them (BDB 628, KB 679, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense). This is an unusual meaning for this VERB. It is found only here and Ps. 119:121, in the sense of "abandon." Its basic meaning is "rest," but it is used in the sense of "remain" in Jer. 27:11.

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:10-12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:10-12 This is God's response to Jeremiah's intercessory prayer. It is shocking in its harsh statements. He characterizes Judah.

  1. they have loved to wander
  2. they have not stayed on the clearly marked path of His word
    SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

Therefore, YHWH will

  1. not accept them (this term, BDB 953, is used for YHWH being pleased to accept a sacrifice when brought in an appropriate manner and an appropriate heart, cf. vv. 10,12)
  2. remember their iniquity (#2 and #3 are prophetic idioms, cf. Hosea 8:13; 9:9)
  3. call their sins to account
  4. instructed Jeremiah:
    1. not pray for them (BDB 813, KB 933, Hithpael IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense, cf. Jer. 7:16; 11:14)
    2. not listen to their cry (cf. Jer. 6:20)
      (1) when they fast (see SPECIAL TOPIC: FASTING)
      (2) when they sacrifice
  5. not accept them (cf. Jer. 14:10)
  6. make an end of them (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-28)
    1. sword
    2. famine
    3. pestilence (cf. Jer. 21:7,9; 24:10; 27:8,13; 28:8; 29:17-18; 32:24,36; 34:17; 38:2; 42:17,22; 44:13)

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:12 "burnt offering and grain offering"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:12 "burnt offering and grain offering" These are two of the types of offerings discussed in Leviticus 1-7 (burnt ‒ BDB 750; grain ‒ BDB 585).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SACRIFICIAL SYSTEMS OF THE ANE , V. A., B.

▣ "sword, famine and pestilence" These three form the triad of the terrible results of invasion (cf. Jer. 5:12; 14:15; 27:8; 29:18). They are the predicted consequences of covenant disobedience (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28).

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:13 This is the prophet's attempt to blame the people's religious apostasy on the religious leaders. Although there is some truth to this, the leaders were certainly far from God, the people were still responsible for their own acts (cf. Ezekiel 18). They should have recognized a false teacher (cf. Deut. 13:1-5; 18:22).

▣ "but I will give you lasting peace in this place" This was the promise of YHWH that the false prophets kept alluding to. It was surely a covenant promise. Isaiah uses it in encouraging Hezekiah not to surrender to the Assyrians (cf. Isaiah 36-37). But Jeremiah makes it very plain that this promise had conditions, covenant conditions that Judah had hopelessly violated! Invasion and exile were coming!

See D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks, pp. 44-47, "Conditional or Unconditional." This is crucial in understanding the relationship between the OT and the NT.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:14-18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:14-18 This is God's response to the prophet's prayer to forgive the people because of the false teachers (cf. Jer. 23; 28; Deut. 18:9-22). YHWH admits that the leaders had been idolatrous, but also that the people are responsible. The prophets will bear the burden of their sin as will the people (cf. Ezekiel 18).

Notice how YHWH characterizes the false prophets (cf. Deut. 13:1-5; 18:9-22).

  1. prophesying falsehood in My name (cf. Jer. 5:31; 23:25)
    1. I did not send them
    2. I did not command them
    3. I did not speak to them
  2. their message comes from
    1. a false vision (cf. Jer. 23:25,28,32)
    2. divination (cf. Jer. 27:9; 29:8; see SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINER)
    3. futility (cf. Jer. 23:16)
    4. the deception of their own minds (cf. Jer. 23:26)
  3. all of these false prophets will die (cf. Jer. 14:15; 28:17; Deut. 13:1-2; 18:20)
  4. those who have heard and believed them will also die in the invasion and siege (cf. Jer. 14:16)

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:17d-e
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:17d-e These last two poetic lines describe the covenant people (i.e. the virgin daughter, cf. Jer. 8:21; 18:13; 31:4,21; 46:11; see full note at Jer. 46:11).

  1. has been crushed with a mighty blow (BDB 990, KB 1402, Niphal PERFECT)
  2. has a sorely infected wound (BDB 317, KB 316, Niphal PARTICIPLE)
14:18
NASB  "have gone roving about in the land that
  they do not know"
NKJV  "go about. . ."
NRSV  "roam the country at their wit's end"
TEV (footnote)  "have been dragged away to a land they
  know nothing about"
NJB  "ply their trade throughout the land, and
  have no knowledge"
JPSOA  "roam the land, they know not where"
REB  "wander without rest in the land"
Peshitta  "begging in the land unrecognized"

The NJB is closest to the MT. The NASB, NKJV, JPSOA follow the LXX. The options are

  1. these leaders do not know how to handle the results of the invasion
  2. these leaders are exiled (NRSV, TEV footnote; this has no Hebrew or Greek or versional support)
  3. the leaders wander about looking for work (i.e. a livelihood) because the temple is destroyed

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:17-18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:17-18 In this poetic strophe we again see, not only the grief of the prophet, but the grief of YHWH (cf. Jer. 8:18-9:9). It is such an important truth that God does not rejoice in judgment but rejoices in blessing. Fallen humans force Him to discipline them because of their flagrant, continuing rebellion and willful idolatry. The discipline is an act of parental love and desire to use Israel to inform the nations about Himself.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:19 There are three questions here which are emphatic in the Hebrew.

  1. "Have You completely rejected Judah?" (emphatic by grammatical feature ‒ the use of the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a VERB of the same root [BDB 549, KB 540])
  2. "Have You loathed Zion?" (emphatic by word choice [BDB 171, KB 199, Qal PERFECT] cf. Lev. 26:30,43)
  3. "Why have You stricken us so that we are beyond healing?" (cf. Jer. 8:15)

This third question is the central issue — Has the conditional covenant with Abraham been totally abrogated by Israel and Judah's continual disobedience? Well, yes and no!

  1. yes ‒ and this sets the stage for the "new covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34 (cf. Rom. 3:21-31; Galatians 3)
  2. no ‒ see Lev. 26:43, YHWH still has a purpose for His OT people (cf. Romans 9-11)

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:19-22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 14:19-22 These verses contain the prophet's questions and prayers for God's mercy. One wonders if these may also be liturgical pieces quoted regularly at the temple (cf. Jer. 14:7-9).

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:20 All three Hebrew words for sin are found in this verse, which shows the waywardness of the people of God.

  1. wickedness (BDB 957, cf. Jer. 5:26; 12:1; 23:19; 25:31; 30:23)
  2. iniquity (BDB 730, cf. Jer. 2:22; 3:13; 5:25; 11:10; 13:22; 14:7,10,20; 16:10,17,18; 18:23, etc.)
  3. sin (BDB 306, cf. Jer. 3:25; 5:25; 14:10; 15:13; 16:10,18; 17:1,3; 18:23, etc.)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Jeremiah 14:20-22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:20-22 The prophet attempts a corporate prayer (see SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER) again.

  1. we know our wickedness (cf. Jer. 3:25)
  2. we know the iniquity of our fathers (cf. Jer. 2:5-6; 7:25-26)
  3. we know we have sinned against You

In light of these confessions Jeremiah pleads for YHWH to act because of His own character and purposes (cf. Jer. 14:7; Ezek. 36:22-38).

  1. do not despise (BDB 610, KB 658, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) for You own name's sake
  2. do not disgrace (BDB 614, KB 663, Piel IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) the throne of Your glory (i.e. the ark of the covenant in the holy of holies, cf. Jer. 3:17; 17:12)
  3. remember (BDB 269, KB 269, Qal IMPERATIVE) and do not annul (BDB 830, KB 974, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) Your covenant with us
  4. same as #3
  5. we know You are the only giver of rain (not Ba'al, cf. Jer. 5:24; see SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS)
  6. therefore, we hope in You

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:1 YHWH answers Jeremiah's intercession. The few spiritual leaders in Israel/Judah's history cannot avert the unbelief and rebellion of the current generation (cf. Ezekiel 18). Corporate prayers are effective only if the people share the faith and repentant attitude of the intercessor!

For the intercessory ministry (cf. Ps. 99:6-8) of

  1. Moses ‒ see Exod. 32:11-14,30-32; Num. 14:13-25; Deut. 9:18-20,25-29
  2. Samuel ‒ see 1 Sam. 7:9; 12:23

Notice YHWH's directives about Judah.

  1. My heart (lit. nephesh, BDB 659, KB 711; see SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH) would not be with this people
  2. send them away from My presence ‒ BDB 1018, KB 1511, Piel IMPERATIVE
  3. let them go ‒ BDB 422, KB 425, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

Judah had rejected YHWH ("Me," "My," "My," cf. Jer. 15:6). They were no longer in a covenant relationship with Him. Oh my, what a tragedy for all humanity!

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY (aphistēmi)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

15:2
NASB, NRSV, JPSOA  "those destined for. . ."
NKJV  "such as are for. . ."
TEV  "some are doomed to. . ."
NJB  "those for. . ."
LXX  "as many as for. . ."
REB  "those who are for. . ."
Peshitta  "those numbered for"

The people respond to YHWH's message through Jeremiah ("where should we go"). They are not seeking knowledge but flippantly responding! Therefore, YHWH tells them exactly where they will go (cf. Jer. 14:12).

  1. some to death by death (disease)
  2. some to death by the sword (warfare)
  3. some to death by famine (siege)
  4. some to captivity (exile)

The normal triad of judgment is the sword, famine, and pestilence (cf. Ezek. 14:21; 33:27), but here "captivity" or exile is added.

The MT has "those who are for. . ." You can tell by the variety in the translations that the logical issue is, "Who chooses which one for which judgment?" Some believers believe every detail of a person's life is predestined (i.e. Calvinists). I, however, lean toward some human freedom. I think our choices in life often affect the outcome, not fate, not chance, and not God. Life is not a pre-written puppet show!

This thought in no way is meant to depreciate in any way the recurrent biblical emphasis on the sovereignty of God. It is meant to highlight the magnitude of humans, being made in the image and likeness of God, are given some freedom of choice (i.e. Adam and Eve, Cain, etc.)

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. This chapter seems to be made up of disjointed poems.
    1. Jer. 15:1-4 (or possibly Jer. 15:1-9) goes with Jer. 14
    2. Jer. 15:5-9 is YHWH's lament over Judah's destruction (using the imagery of widows and mothers)
    3. Jer. 15:10-11 is another poem involving birth and a mother (the MT of Jer. 15:11 is very difficult)
    4. Jer. 15:12-14 is a seemingly unrelated poem of destruction, possibly related to Jer. 1:18-19 and 15:20
    5. Jer. 15:15-18 is the second (or third) of Jeremiah's laments (i.e. confessions)
    6. Jer. 15:19-21 has YHWH's response to Jeremiah's prayer. In a sense this is like a second call to prophetic service.

  2. The time for repentance has passed, even intercession by great leaders cannot stop the coming invasion from the north (cf. Jer. 15:12-14).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:3 "I shall appoint"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:3 "I shall appoint" The VERB (BDB 823, KB 955, Qal PERFECT with waw) can mean

  1. visit upon
    1. in punishment ‒ Isa. 10:12; Jer. 9:25; 11:22; 13:21; 21:14
    2. in mercy ‒ Gen. 21:1; 50:24,25; Isa. 23:17-18; Jer. 15:15; 27:22; 29:10; 32:5
  2. appoint to, cf. Num. 27:16; Jer. 15:3; 49:15; 50:44; 51:27

This VERB is where several translations get the idea of "destined" in v. 2.

▣ "four kinds of doom" There are four Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS.

  1. the sword to slay
  2. the dogs to drag off (i.e. the horror of improper burial)
  3. the birds of the sky to devour and destroy (cf. Deut. 28:26; Jer. 7:33; 16:4; 19:7; 34:20)
  4. the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy (cf. Deut. 28:26; Jer. 7:33; 16:4; 19:7; 34:20)

Notice numbers 3 and 4 are specifically mentined in Deut. 28, which is a litany of curses and blessings for covenant obedience!

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:4 "I will make them an object of horror among all the kingdoms of the earth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:4 "I will make them an object of horror among all the kingdoms of the earth" This Hebrew idiom is explained in Jer. 24:9; 29:18 (cf. Deut. 28:25). Israel was meant to reveal YHWH's loving character to the nations, but they did not see the mercy of YHWH because only His judgment was manifested in the life of Israel (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "because of Manasseh" YHWH gives the specific origin of Judah's current idolatry—King Manasseh. He was Hezekiah's son who reigned longer than any other Judean king. He was by far the most evil king in Judah's history (cf. 2 Kgs. 21:1-18; 23:26-27; 24:3-4; 2 Chr. 33:1-17). He was saved and forgiven at the very end of his life, but the consequences of his idolatry remained in the people of Judah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED KINGDOM

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:5-9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:5-9 Verses 5-9 are YHWH's lament! This poetic strophe (characterized by PERFECT VERBS) describes the coming judgment of Judah's incalcitrant rebellion and idolatry.

Verse 5 is a series of questions.

  1. who will have pity on you 
  2. who will mourn you
  3. who will turn aside to ask about your welfare

The theological implication is that without YHWH's help, there is no one else who cares, protects, and provides for them. But they have rejected Him.

  1. you have forsaken Me
  2. you keep going backward

Because of this YHWH will act as judge. He is tired of relenting (cf. Jer. 6:11; 7:6).

  1. stretch out His hand against them (cf. Jer. 6:12)
  2. destroy them (cf. Jer. 15:8)
  3. winnow them (cf. Jer. 51:2)
  4. bereave them of children
  5. give them numerous widows
  6. bring the destroyer at noonday
  7. anguish and dismay
  8. bring shame (BDB 101, KB 116) and humiliation (BDB 344, KB 340)
  9. give the survivors to the sword

Wow! Idolatry has consequences! Lack of repentance (cf. Jer. 15:7, line 3) has consequences! If this were true then, why not now?

I do like the NET Bible's understanding of an outline of this poem based on who is speaking to whom (p. 1333).

  1. Jer. 15:1-4 ‒ YHWH addresses Jeremiah
  2. Jer. 15:5-6 ‒ YHWH addresses Jerusalem
  3. Jer. 15:7-9 ‒ YHWH addresses Jeremiah

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:6 "I will stretch out My hand against you and destroy you"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:6 "I will stretch out My hand against you and destroy you" This is an idiom from the exodus (cf. Exod. 7:5; Isa. 31:3) of YHWH's power in judgment (cf. Jer. 6:12). In Exod. 7:5 it is against the Egyptians on behalf of His covenant people, but now YHWH acts against His own people (cf. Isa. 5:25; 10:4; 14:27; Jer. 6:12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣
NASB, JPSOA  "You keep going backward"
NKJV, NJB, Peshitta  "You have gone backwards"
NRSV, TEV, REB, NET  "You have turned your back to me"
LXX  "you will go backward"
NIV  "you keep on backsliding"

Hebrew VERBS do not have a time element; that must be determined from context. Notice how the translations of Jer. 15:6 differ.

The best parallel use of "backward" (BDB 229) is Jer. 7:24.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW GRAMMAR, II.

▣ "I am tired of relenting" The VERB (BDB 521, KB 512, Niphal PERFECT) is used of exhausted patience. The Niphal PERFECT can be used in a good sense.

  1. Jer. 6:11, in relation to YHWH's wrath
  2. Jer. 20:9, in relation to YHWH's word
  3. Isa. 1:14, in relation to YHWH's feasts

It can be used in a bad sense.

  1. Jer. 9:5, in relation to iniquity
  2. Isa. 47:13, in relation to occult practices

The second VERBAL (BDB 636, KB 688, Niphal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) means to be moved with pity. Here it is negated. YHWH will not be moved with pity (cf. Isa. 7:16). Judgment is coming! He has waited and waited but Judah would not repent and return to Him.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:7 "At the gates of the land"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:7 "At the gates of the land" This would refer to the

  1. walled cities near the borders where invading armies would travel (i.e. coastal plain)
  2. fortresses on the invasion routes (i.e. caravan routes)

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:8 This verse is difficult to understand.

  1. Does it refer to the dead children of the widows who were strong young soldiers but now dead? (i.e. little children)
  2. Does it refer to the death of the remaining widows by young invaders because their own children/warriors cannot defend them?

The "widows" described as "the sand of the sea" is an allusion to YHWH's promise to Abraham about his numerous descendants (cf. Gen. 22:17; 32:12). But now his many descendants will be destroyed! The fathers/husbands and their young men/soldiers are already dead, and now their mothers also (i.e. no hope for a next generation).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

▣ "A destroyer at noonday" This seems to refer to the personification of an invading army that attacks at the time when the defenders could see best (cf. Jer. 6:4). This would then be a symbol of the invulnerability of the invaders.

▣ "Anguish" This word (BDB 735 I, KB 822 II) is found only here and in Hosea 11:9. It denotes "shock" and "agitation" (KB).

▣ "dismay" This word (BDB 96, KB 111) basically means "sudden fear" (cf. Ps. 78:33). It is used in the "cursing and blessing" section of Leviticus (cf. Lev. 26:16). In Isa. 65:23 it is used of what will not happen to a restored, repentant people of God.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:9 There have been several ways to understand Jer. 15:9, line 2.

  1. "her breathing is labored," NASB
  2. "she has breathed her last," NKJV, NIV, NAB
  3. "gasps for breath," NRSV
  4. "she has swooned away," NJB

The numerous widows and mothers of Jer. 15:7-8 are again used as imagery of Judah invaded, defeated, and taken into exile.

▣ "seven" This is a symbolic number, going back to Genesis 1-2, for perfection. A woman with seven sons would be considered uniquely blessed by God (cf. 1 Sam. 2:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #4

▣ "Her sun has set while it was yet day" This imagery speaks of sudden hopelessness. It may

  1. relate to v. 1, line 4
  2. relate to Jer. 6:4
  3. relate to the prophetic imagery of Amos 8:9

▣ "She has been shamed and humiliated" This blessed mother (i.e. seven sons) has lost all her sons (which gave her renown) to invasion. Now childless, she is shamed and humiliated.

▣ "So I will give over their survivors to the sword" This phrase appears to denote a complete destruction of Judah by the sword. This is prophetic hyperbole because we know many thousands were exiled. Poetry is meant to function on an emotional level, not a literal, historical level.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:10-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:10-11 Verse 10 is obviously a lament from Jeremiah. He expresses how he feels about the way his ministry is being accepted.

  1. expresses sorrow for his birth (cf. Jer. 20:14-18, i.e. imagery of his life)
  2. he has become a man of strife (BDB 936) and contention (BDB 193 I) instead of a servant of YHWH
    1. he has no honor
    2. is always in a lawsuit against Judah
  3. he is rejected by his own (i.e. imagery of lending money as causing problems)

Verse 11 is difficult to understand in the MT. It could mean

  1. YHWH is answering (LXX) Jeremiah (NJB) by reminding him of his call (i.e. Jer. 1:4-10). His birth (#1 above) was the will of YHWH (i.e. Jer. 1:5).
  2. Jeremiah continues to talk to YHWH of his faithfulness (NRSV, TEV)
  3. YHWH speaks to Judah of the hope for a remnant (NKJV, JPSOA; this is reminiscent of Isa. 4:2-6; 6:1-13; 10:20-27; 37:30-32)

The Hebrew of Jer. 15:11 is uncertain. The diversity of the versions and the Kethiv and Qere of the Masoretes show this.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (three senses)

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:10-18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 15:10-18 This is known as the second "Confession of Jeremiah," but it may be better characterized as his "complaint." He prays in Jer. 15:15-18. YHWH responds and reassures him in Jer. 15:19-21.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:12-14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:12-14 The NASB strophe describes the judgment of Judah by YHWH (notice the "I will. . .," vv. 13,14). He is addressing Judah in Jer. 15:12-14 (cf. Jer. 17:3-4).

  1. invasion from the north by a strong invader (iron)
  2. wealth confiscated (i.e. because of their sin)
  3. wealth taken out of the country (NASB, i.e. the temple treasures)

There is a problem with the first VERB of Jer. 15:14 (see further note there).

  1. "cause to pass" ‒ BDB 716, KB 778, Hiphil PERFECT with waw
    1. NASB ‒ "then I will cause your enemies to bring it"
    2. NKJV ‒ "and I will make you cross over with your enemies"
  2. "cause to serve" ‒ BDB 712, KB 773 (LXX, NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB, Net Bible, Peshitta, UBS's Text Project, p. 224, gives this a "C" rating)
  3. "bring your enemies by way of a land you have not known" (JPSOA)

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:13 "without cost"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 15:13 "without cost" This phrase is difficult to interpret in this context. The LXX omits it, which makes the verse much easier to understand in the strophe. This is followed by TEV. The "without cost" refers to the invaders confiscating Judah's wealth easily, without great loss to the invaders' military.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:14 The threat of exile was initially stated in the "cursing and blessing" section of Deuteronomy (i.e. Deut. 28:36,64).

Lines 3 and 4 are related to Deut. 33:22. Remember the prophets are "covenant mediators" (see Fee and Stuart, How To Read the Bible For All Its Worth, pp.181-204). They hold Israel and Judah to the Mosaic legislation! If they obey—abundance; if they disobey—judgment (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-28).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

▣
NASB  "I will cause your enemies to bring it"
NKJV  "I will make you cross over with your
  enemies"
NRSV, TEV, REB  "I will make you serve your enemies"
LXX, NJB, Peshitta  "I will enslave you to your enemies"
JPSOA  "I will bring your enemies by way of
  a land you have not known"

The MT has "I will make you pass over your enemies in a land which you do not know." Though the MT is ambiguous, it still makes sense. Judah, by God's will, will be taken as slaves into a foreign land.

▣ "fire" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:15 Notice the prayer requests (i.e. IMPERATIVES) in this verse.

  1. remember me ‒ BDB 269, KB 269, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. take notice of me (lit. "visit me," see note at Jer. 15:3) ‒ BDB 823, KB 955, Qal IMPERATIVE
  3. take vengeance for me ‒ BDB 667, KB 721, Niphal IMPERATIVE
  4. do not take me away ‒ BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  5. know that for Your sake I endure reproach ‒ BDB 383, KB 390, Qal IMPERATIVE

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:15-18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:15-18 This is Jeremiah's prayer for YHWH to take notice of his faithfulness and service. Notice the names for Deity.

  1. "Thou who knowest" (BDB393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT)
  2. "O YHWH" (i.e. YHWH; see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.)
  3. "Thy name" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: "The Name" of YHWH)
  4. "O Lord of hosts" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS)

These are all covenant names (cf. Jer. 15:16). If Judah has not been faithful, Jeremiah has and he has suffered for it.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DESCRIPTIVE TITLES FOR GOD

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:16 Jeremiah is expressing, even in the midst of persecution (i.e. Jer. 15:15), the joy (BDB 965) and delight (BDB 970) of being YHWH's prophet. The idiom "I ate them" refers to God's message being imparted to the prophet (cf. Ezek. 3:3).

Some commentators have suggested that the phrase "Your words were found" refers to the discovery of the Law found in the remodeling of the temple during Josiah's reign (cf. 2 Kings 22; 2 Chr. 34; i.e. 621 B.C.).

▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, Peshitta  "For I have been called
  by Your name"
TEV, NET  "For I belong to you"
REB  "you. . .have named me
  yours"
LXX  "Your name has been
  called on Me"
JPSOA  "Your name is attached
  to me"

The phrase is used in

  1. Jer. 7:10,11,14,30; 32:34 to refer to the temple
  2. Jer. 14:9 to refer to the covenant people of God (i.e. collectively)
  3. Isa. 63:19 to refer to Gentiles (phrase negated)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON THE NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALLED

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:17-18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:17-18 Jeremiah describes how being God's prophet affected his life.

  1. I did not sit in the circle of merrymakers
  2. I did not exult
  3. I sat alone

He states that this is a result of YHWH's call.

  1. Your hand was upon me
  2. You filled me with indignation
  3. I have perpetual pain
  4. I have an incurable wound

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:18c-d
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:18c-d This is one of the most shocking assertions about YHWH in the OT. Jeremiah feels so comfortable with YHWH that he can express himself in hyperbolic imagery (exactly the opposite of Jer. 2:13).

  1. YHWH is like a deceptive stream (BDB 469). This phrase is intensified by the presence of an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT VERB of "to be" (BDB 224, KB 243).
  2. The parallel line is like water that is unreliable (BDB 52, KB 63, Niphal PERFECT, see SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN; and SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:19 "And if you extract the precious from the worthless"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 15:19 "And if you extract the precious from the worthless" I like what UBS Handbook for Translators on Jeremiah (p. 379) says about line 4, "the precious is YHWH's message (Jer. 15:16) and the worthless is Jeremiah's evaluation" (cf. Jer. 15:18, lines 3-4).

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:19-21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:19-21 YHWH answers Jeremiah's complaints and requests. YHWH is apparently offended by Jeremiah's characterization in 18c-d. Jeremiah himself must repent (BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal IMPERFECT; see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)).

If Jeremiah "turns back" to YHWH, then YHWH will restore (VERB) him. The covenant always has two parties (see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT).

The play on the word "return" (used four times in Jer. 15:19) continues in Jer. 15:19f-g. Jeremiah, as YHWH's spokesman, would hopefully have the Judeans come to him to hear God's word, but he must be careful not to be influenced by their apparent response.

One wonders how much Jeremiah's sense of rejection and prayer for protection and vengeance is meant to reflect the feelings of the godly remnant of Judah/Jerusalem. Often the prophet feels for YHWH. Is it possible he now feels for the repentant remnant?

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:20 This alludes to Jer. 1:18-19. Jeremiah must be strong to face the opposition that will surely come for speaking the true word of God.

▣ "save. . .deliver" These are in a parallel relationship. They both refer to physical deliverance (BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT; BDB 664, KB 717, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT).

The second VERB is repeated in Jer. 15:21 (Hiphil PERFECT), parallel to "ransom" (BDB 804, KB 911, Qal PERFECT).

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:21 "deliver. . .redeem"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
15:21 "deliver. . .redeem" These are also in a parallel relationship. For "redeem" (BDB 804, KB 911, Qal PERFECT).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:2 Jeremiah is restricted by YHWH from taking a wife (very unusual for a Jewish man) or having children (cf. Gen. 1:28; Lev. 26:22). The reason given is

  1. that families will soon die in YHWH's judgment (cf. Jer. 15:2-3; 16:3-4) for their idolatry (cf. Lev. 19:4; 26:1)
    1. deadly diseases (cf. Lev. 26:16,21; Deut. 28:21,22,27,59,60,61)
    2. sword (cf. Lev. 26:25; Jer. 50:28; 51:11)
    3. famine (Lev. 26:26; Deut. 28:17)

      Their bodies will be unburied (no one left to bury them, cf. Deut. 28:26; Ps. 79:2-3) and will be food for birds and animals (cf. Jer. 7:33; 16:4; 19:7; 34:20).

  2. This lact of a spouse symbolizes YHWH's lack of a covenant people (i.e. wife).
  3. YHWH surprisingly restricts Jeremiah from all societal comforts. He must be comforted by his service to YHWH, who would be his hope, comfort, and peace (cf. Jer. 16:19)!

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:3 Notice the three uses of the root for having children.

  1. born ‒ BDB 409, KB 411, ADJECTIVE
  2. bore ‒ BDB 408, KB 411, Qal PARTICIPLE
  3. begot ‒ BDB 408, KB 411, Hiphil PARTICIPLE

The next generation, along with the current generation of Judeans, will be destroyed!

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:4 Notice the IMPERFECT VERBS.

  1. "die" ‒ BDB 559, KB 562, Qal IMPERFECT
  2. "lamented" ‒ BDB 704, KB 763, Niphal IMPERFECT (negated)
  3. "buried" ‒ BDB 868, IB 1064, Niphal IMPERFECT (negated)
  4. "will be as dung" ‒ BDB 224, KB 243, Qal IMPERFECT
  5. "come to an end" ‒ BDB 477, KB 476, Qal IMPERFECT

Being unmourned, unburied, and devoured by animals was a great fear and curse for ANE people (cf. Jer. 7:33; 8:2; 9:22; 15:3-4; 19:7; 34:20; Deut. 28:26; 1 Kgs. 14:11). It affected one's afterlife in Sheol.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

▣
NASB, NRSV, NJB, NIV  "deadly diseases"
NRSV, JPSOA  "gruesome deaths"
LXX  "a sickly death"
REB  "a horrible death"
Peshitta  "famine"

This is a CONSTRUCT of BDB 560 (i.e. "deadly," cf Ezek. 28:8) and BDB 316 (i.e. "diseases," cf. Jer. 14:18; 2 Chr. 21:19; Ps. 103:3). These were the result of covenant disobedience (cf. Lev. 26:16,21; Deut. 28:21,22,27,59-61; 29:14-21,22-28, esp. Jer. 16:22).

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:5 Notice the commands of Jer. 16:5.

  1. do not enter a house of mourning (or "feasting," i.e. special meal for the family of the dead) ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  2. do not lament ‒ BDB 229, KB 240, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  3. do not console them ‒ BDB 626, KB 678, Qal JUSSIVE

Their plight was YHWH's judgment of their covenant disobedience. Mourning would send the wrong message (much like Lev. 10:1-3). It is possible there is no one left to mourn!

▣ "I have withdrawn" (BDB 62, KB 74, Qal PERFECT)

  1. My peace, BDB 1022, cf. Jer. 12:12; 30:5; see SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (shalom, OT)
  2. My lovingkindness, BDB 338 I, see an example of what happens when lovingkindness is removed at Jer. 13:14, see SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (Hesed)
  3. My compassion, BDB 933, cf. Deut. 13:17; Neh. 9:19,27,31; Ps. 25:6; 40:11; 77:9; 79:8; 103:4; Isa. 63:7,15; hosea 2:19 (this term is found only here and in Jer. 42:12)

The eternal covenant is negated, broken, cancelled! Shocking! A new covenant must come now (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36).

It is shocking that YHWH has annulled His "eternal" covenant with Abraham's descendants (cf. Lev. 26; Deut. 27-30)! This seems to violate 2 Sam. 7; 1 Chr. 17. However, Jeremiah realized the covenant of Moses was a "conditional covenant."

Israel had been unfaithful from the Exodus onward, except for brief periods of godly kings and, even then, the population did not follow!

I have come to believe that the promised restoration from Neo-Babylonian exile by Cyrus II's decree in 538 B.C. was only a temporary reprieve. By Jesus' day the people of Israel were again hopelessly lost in ritual, tradition, and poilitical alliances (i.e. Rome). The prophecy of Dan. 9:24-27 came into reality, as did the curses of Lev. 26; Deut. 28 in the Assyrian and Neo-Babylonian exiles.

Israel was a stubborn, rebellious people. YHWH divorces HIs unfaithful wife (Israel) and takes a new faithful bride, the Church. This means that Jesus' Olivet Discourse (Matt. 24; Mark 13; Luke 17; 21) and the book of Revelation relate to the destruction of Jerusalem and the temple in A.D. 70 (Partial Preterism). These texts are now fulfilled and past. They do not refer to al future historical event. I know for many of you, this is a new thought. Please look at my verse-by-verse commentary on these passages free online at www.freebiblecommentary.org

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SUPERIORITY OF THE NEW COVENANT OVER THE MOSAIC COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEWS OF THE MOSAIC LAW

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:5-9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:5-9 The first strophe (Jer. 16:1-4) denotes the death of families with no lamentation or burial (cf. Jer. 16:6). This second strophe picks up on

  1. "mourning" ‒ BDB 931 or "feasting" (cf. Amos 6:7)
  2. "lament" ‒ BDB 704
  3. "console" ‒ BDB 626
  4. "mourner" ‒ BDB 5
  5. "consolation" ‒ BDB 637

The book of Jeremiah is structured/edited/compiled by

  1. theological themes
  2. word plays
  3. genre (i.e. laments, court scenes, promise/salvation oracles)

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:6 As all of the family dies in Jer. 16:1-4, in Jer. 16:6 all levels of society die (cf. Jer. 6:13; 8:10)!

▣ "nor will anyone gash himself or shave his head for them" These are pagan mourning rites (cf. Lev. 19:28; 21:5; Deut. 14:1; 1 Kgs. 18:28; Isa. 22:12; Jer. 41:5; 47:5; 48:37; see SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES). This shows how far the Judeans had progressed in idolatry (i.e. possibly ancestral worship and necromancy, cf. Deut. 26:14; Isa. 8:19-20)!

16:7
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA  "break bread"
TEV  "no one will eat or drink"
REB  "a portion of bread"
NJB  "no bread will be broken"
JPSOA (footnote)  "to them"
NRSV (footnote)  "break for them"
LXX  "bread shall not be broken"
Peshitta  "tear themselves for them"

The MT has "no one shall break for them." The word "for them" is (BDB 241, plus PREPOSITION, להם). Notice the similarity to the word for "bread" is לחם (BDB 536). The UBS Text Project, p. 225, gives "bread" a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

The LXX revocalized the Hebrew word "for them" to get the translation "bread." The KJV, following the Peshitta, translates the phrase as "neither shall men tear themselves," which would relate to Jer. 16:6 (i.e. "gash").

Because of the mention of a cup later in the verse, probably "bread" or "food" (NIV) makes more sense. However, the Jerome Bible Commentary (p. 316) reminds us of food being offered to the dead (cf. Deut. 26:14; Ezek. 24:17,22; Tobit 4:17), which would make this another idolatrous practice, so perhaps KJV is a valid way of understanding this verse.

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:8 This may relate to Jer. 15:17. Apparently these dinners were connected to burial rites (i.e. breaking the fast of the mourning period). The word "mourning" (BDB 931) can denote a banquet in Aramaic. Also, the phrase "the cup of consolation" is found only here and may refer to a meal after the funeral.

Some commentators relate this verse to a marriage feast (cf. Jer. 16:9, UBS, Handbook for Translators on Jeremiah, p. 382).

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:9 Beginning in Jer. 16:9 several covenant titles for Israel's covenant Deity are used in this chapter (cf. Ps. 18:2).

  1. the Lord of hosts, Jer. 16:9 (SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS)
  2. the God of Israel, Jer. 16:9 (Eloah; see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.)
  3. the Lord our God, Jer. 16:10 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.)
  4. as the Lord lives, Jer. 16:14,15 (cf. Jer. 4:2)
  5. my strength, Jer. 16:19
  6. my stronghold, Jer. 16:19
  7. my refuge, Jer. 16:19 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE)
  8. My name is the Lord , Jer. 16:21 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH)
    SPECIAL TOPIC: DESCRIPTIVE TITLES FOR GOD

▣ "I am going to eliminate" The first list is YHWH telling "where," "who," and "when."

  1. from this place (i.e. Judah)
  2. before your eyes
  3. in your time

He will cause all normal social activities to cease.

  1. voice of rejoicing
  2. voice of gladness
  3. voice of the groom
  4. voice of the bride

This phrase ( unique to Jeremiah) is repeated in Jer. 7:34; 25:10; 33:11. It is surprising that the text jumps from an occasion of grief to an occasion of joy (i.e. possibly the ambiguity of the term "house of mourning" or "house of feasting" at v. 5). Possibly this is meant to highlight that all social life and events will cease because all are dead!

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:10-13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:10-13 The question "why us, why now" is addressed (cf. Deut. 29:24-26; Jer. 5:18-19; 9:12-16).

  1. the people's (cf. Jer. 16:12; see SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT)
    1. iniquity
    2. sin
  2. their forefathers
    1. had forsaken YHWH (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SEEK THE LORD)
    2. had not kept His law (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)
    3. followed after other gods (see SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY)
    4. served other gods (i.e. sacrifices)
    5. bowed down to other gods (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)

Because of their multi-generational idolatry, YHWH will

  1. exile ("cast," BDB 376, KB 373, Hiphil PERFECT with waw, Jer. 16:13; 22:26) them from the Promised Land
  2. cause them to serve the pagan gods of that land (cf. Jer. 5:19)
  3. cause them not to have the favor (BDB 337, this form of the root found only here in the OT) of YHWH

Notice the number of personal PRONOUNS used of YHWH. His special, covenant people have rejected Him. It is personal!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

▣ 16:11 This verse clearly illustrates the generational covenant disobedience that led to the curses of Lev. 26 and Deut. 28 becoming a reality. The current generation followed the disobedience of their ancestors (i.e. v. 12).

The Mosaic covenant is a "conditional covenant," as it relates to nations and individuals. YHWH's promise of forgiveness, restoration, and fellowship is "unconditional"!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:12 The people's lifestyle actions are characterized.

  1. walk according to the stubbornness of his own evil heart (cf. Jer. 7:24; 9:14; 11:8; 13:10; SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)
  2. without listening (Shema, BDB 1033; see SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR) to YHWH (cf. Jer. 11:8)

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:14 "days are coming"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:14 "days are coming" Usually phrases like this refer to Judgment Day (cf. Jer. 7:32), but here it refers to restoration (i.e. a new exodus) day. The same "living" God (in contrast to the lifeless idols) who fulfilled His promise to Abraham (cf. Gen. 15:12-21) will do it again, but instead of an exodus from Egypt, it will be out of Mesopotamia.

The reason for the restoration is not stated. YHWH chooses to act based on His character, will, and actions and not on His fallen, disabled, covenant people (cf. Jer. 16:17-18). A new covenant is present (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-38).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE LAST DAYS

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:14 "As the Lord lives"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:14 "As the Lord lives" This is a word play on the covenant name for Israel's God, YHWH. It is from the Hebrew VERB "to be" (cf. Exod. 3:13-15). He is the great "I am"! He is the Only One who possesses immortality. He is the ever-living, only-living One!

This phrase was used as

  1. an oath formula in worship settings ‒ Deut. 6:13; 10:20; Jer. 4:2; 12:16; Hosea 4:15
  2. an oath formula for speaking truth ‒ Jdgs. 8:19; Ruth 3:13; 1 Sam. 14:39,45; 20:3,21; 2 Sam. 4:9; 12:5; 1 Kgs. 1:29; 2:24; 22:14; Jer. 5:2; 38:16

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (NT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:14-15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:14-15 This is the first of four brief strophes that deal with YHWH's promise of restoration! It is so common in the prophetic literature for "judgment" oracles to be matched with "promise" oracles.

These verses reappear in Jer. 23:7-8. The book of Jeremiah is an anthology of his poems! They are not in chronological order and they do not always specify the historical setting.

It is interesting that the terms for "land" (i.e. adamah and erets) are used in distinct ways.

  1. adamah (BDB 9) is used of the land of Canaan that YHWH gave to the descendants of the Patriarchs.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS
  2. erets (BDB 75, KB 90) is used of the land occupied by other people groups

This is illustrated in Deut. 29:28; 2 Kgs. 25:21; Jer. 16:15 repeated in 23:7-8.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH (erets)

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:16-18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:16-18 YHWH (emphatic in Jer. 16:16) uses food-gathering imagery to describe the return of all His exiled people.

  1. fishermen (opposite of Amos 4:2)
  2. hunters (opposite of Isa. 2:21)

It is surely possible that Jer. 16:16-18 refers to judgment, while Jer. 16:14-15 and Jer. 16:19-20,21 refer to restoration. It seems to me that Jer. 16:17 is saying YHWH has not overlooked their sin. He has fairly and proportionally punished them, but now He is bringing them back (i.e. a new exodus)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "abominations" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:18 Before YHWH restores, He punishes them for their sin, especially idolatry. The phrase "doubly repay" is an idiom used in the sense of "fully" (cf. Isa. 40:2; Rev. 18:6) or complete judgment.

▣ "My inheritance" The NET Bible (p. 1337) has a good note on how this word is used in Jeremiah.

  1. the Promised Land (Palestine), Jer. 2:7
  2. the covenant people themselves, Jer. 10:16; 12:8-9
  3. the temple in Jerusalem, Jer. 12:7

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:19a,b
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:19a,b There is a beautiful series of descriptive titles for YHWH so reminiscent of Ps. 18:1, but with different words.

  1. my strength ‒ BDB 738, KB 806 II, cf. Exod. 15:2; Ps. 28:7; 62:7; 118:14; Isa. 12:2
  2. my stronghold ‒ BDB 731, #2a, KB 806 II, cf. Ps. 28:8; 43:2; Isa. 25:4
  3. my refuge ‒ BDB 631, KB 600, cf. Nah. 1:7

Notice the personal element (i.e. "my"). Biblical faith is a personal faith relationship of repentance, faith, faithfulness, obedience, worship, and service.

All three of these NOUNS have a similoar connotation ‒ YHWH's protection.

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:19c,d
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:19c,d This is a wonderful universal promise that all humans will come to YHWH (cf. Jer. 3:17; 4:2; 12:15,16). These universal, inclusive statements are more common in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 56:6-8; 60:1-3; 66:23), but surely present in Jeremiah. The hope of Gen. 3:15 and 12:3; 22:18 will be fulfilled!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:19e,f
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:19e,f The last two lines and Jer. 16:20 are clearly a turning from helpless, man-made idols to YHWH, from falsehood to truth! Superstition characterizes pagan humanity (cf. Isa. 44:9-20; Jer. 10:2-5)! Biblical faith is a "turning from" and a "turning to"!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEEK YHWH

entries.title: Jeremiah 16:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
16:20 Notice YHWH will make the nations

  1. know His power
  2. know His might
  3. know His name

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:1-2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:1-2 This is an idiomatic way of asserting the unrepentant nature of Judah's idolatry.

The three images used are

  1. engraved with an iron stylus with a "diamond" (BDB 1038, KB 1562 II) point (i.e. sharp point like a thorn); no way to erase the message (cf. Job 19:24)
  2. on the tablet of the heart ‒ the innermost thoughts and personality (cf. Prov. 3:3; 7:3); this was the place that the new covenant would abide (cf. Jer. 31:31-34)
  3. on the horns of their altars ‒ in Hebrew rituals this is an allusion to the altar of sacrifice (cf. Exod. 27:2) and/or incense altar (cf. Exod. 30:2) in the temple. "Horns" were a symbol of power. They lifted the sacrifice to YHWH. This was where the innocent, sacrificial blood was smeared (cf. Lev. 16:18).

Verse 2 shows that Jeremiah is using "altars" in an idolatrous sense. The fertility gods of Canaan were worshiped on hills, under trees, (cf. Jer. 3:6), or on specially built stone platforms. The intensity of Judah's devotion to Ba'al and Asherah is seen in the phrase "as they remember their children."

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

SPECIAL TOPIC: ALTAR OF SACRIFICE

SPECIAL TOPIC: ALTAR OF INCENSE

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:1-4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:1-4 These verses are missing in the Septuagint.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:3 "O mountain of Mine in the countryside"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:3 "O mountain of Mine in the countryside" This could refer to the temple. But it was not in the countryside, rather in the capital of Jerusalem. Jeremiah must be alluding to the future, complete destruction of the capital and temple (cf. Jer. 9:11; 26:18; Micah 3:12). What a shocking statement to these Judeans! Even the temple treasures will be taken (cf. Jer. 15:13; 20:5).

The alternate interpretation is that this refers to Ba'al worship on the high hills throughout Judah. Both interpretations are possible. However, Ba'al/Asherah platforms did not have horned altars, nor did their worshipers keep "treasures" at the rural sites.

The terms "wealth" and "treasure" may refer to their children either

  1. killed in invasion
  2. offered to Molech

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:3-4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 17:3-4 These verses are similar to Jer. 15:13-14.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:4 Exile is surely coming (cf. Jer. 15:14; 27:12-13) because of Judah's idolatry. YHWH is furious, jealous, and committed to judgment.

For "fire" (cf. Jer. 15:14) see SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE.

The last line of Jer. 17:4 is hyperbolic. Jeremiah's hearers/readers understood this genre; moderns do not! See D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUS. . .ZEALOUS

▣ "forever" This term must be interpreted in context. Here, it is hyperbole.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:5 "Thus says the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:5 "Thus says the Lord" There are several aspects to this phrase.

  1. Jeremiah is speaking YHWH's message, not his own.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION
    SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION
  2. It is Israel's covenant God, YHWH, who speaks.
    1. YHWH is first used in Gen. 2:4.
    2. YHWH is the God of Abraham (cf. Gen. 12:8), though the Patriarchs called Him El Shaddai (cf. Exod. 6:3).
      SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.
      SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADDAI
  3. YHWH chooses to reveal Himself and His will through both words and actions/events. This revelation was meant to be carried to the whole of mankind through Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "Cursed is the man who trusts in mankind" The word "curse" (BDB 76, KB 91, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE) is used in an exclamatory sense in Jer. 11:3; 17:5; 20:14,15; 48:10 [twice]; Deut. 27:15-26. It denotes the opposite of YHWH's blessing.

The term "trust" (BDB 105, KB 120, Qal IMPERFECT) means "a sense of security." Judah trusted in political alliances and national armies (cf. Jer. 46:25) instead of their covenant God (i.e. Ps. 118:8-9; 146:3).

This VERB "trusts" is common in Jeremiah, used of Judah trusting in different things (cf. Jer. 5:17; 7:14; 12:5; 13:25; 48:7; 49:4), but not in YHWH Himself (cf. Ps. 62:8; 115:9-11; Isa. 26:3-4; 30:15). To trust YHWH brings security and rest.

▣ "heart" See SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART.

▣ "whose heart turns away from the Lord" Remember these were covenant people who worshiped regularly at the temple in Jerusalem. Yet, they also worshiped at the local altars of the Canaanite fertility gods (cf. Deut. 11:16; 17:11,17; 29:18-20; 30:17). This was not ignorance but purposeful rebellion by means of religious amalgamation!

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:5-8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 17:5-8 This strophe is theologically and idiomatically related to Psalm 1. Here "bless" is BDB 138 (to kneel), but in Psalm 1 it is BDB 80 (to be happy).

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:6 "bush"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:6 "bush" This word (BDB 792, KB 887) is found only twice in the OT, both in Jeremiah (cf. Jer. 48:6). A similar root is found in Ps. 102:17 and is translated "destitute" (NASB margin, "naked"). The NASB translates it "juniper" in Jer. 48:6. KB translates it as "tamarisk." The UBS Fauna and Flora of the Bible sees it as juniper (p. 131, REB) and does not even list it with the ARTICLE on tamarisk (p. 182).

▣
NASB  "prosperity"
NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA, REB, Peshitta, LXX  "good"
NJB  "relief"

The word (BDB 375 III) means "a good thing," "benefit," or "welfare." In Deut. 28:12 the same root (BDB 373 II) refers to "rain," which makes sense in this context.

▣ "a land of salt" See Deut. 29:23 where this phrase is used of YHWH's judgment on disobedient covenant Israel.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:7 "Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:7 "Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord" This proverb (BDB 138, KB 159, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE) is a recurrent theme of the Psalms (i.e. Ps. 34:8; 40:4; 84:12). It is the theological opposite of "cursed." Both are exclamatory! There are only two kinds of people.

  1. those who trust in YHWH (not just the things He gives) ‒ Jer. 17:7
  2. those who trust in humanity (humanism, nationalism) ‒ Jer. 17:5

The results of each are very different (cf. Deuteronomy 27-28; Psalm 1; Matthew 5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING (OT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:9-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:9-11 This is the recurrent message of Scripture after the Fall of Genesis 3 (cf. Gen. 6:5,11,12,13; Rom. 3:9-18). See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND.

The imagery of "sinfulness" as "sickness" (BDB 60, cf. Jer. 30:12; Isa. 1:5-6; 17:11; Micah 1:9) is found in the Hebrew concept of abundance/health vs. poverty/sickness (cf. Jer. 17:14; 14:19; Deuteronomy 27-28; Job; Ps. 103:1-5; Isa. 1:5-6; 53:4-6). The booklet that has helped me in this area, written by a charismatic author is Gordon Fee, The Disease of the Health and Wealth Gospel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEALING

17:9
NASB, NKJV, TEV, REB  "deceitful"
NRSV, NJB, JPSOA  "devious"
Peshitta  "stubborn"
LXX  "deep"

This word (BDB 784 I) comes from "heel" or "footprint." It is used of Jacob's birth (cf. Gen. 25:26; 27:36). It is used in Jer. 9:4 and translated "craftily" or "supplanter" (another reference to Jacob's treatment of Esau).

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:10 "I, the Lord, search the heart
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:10 "I, the Lord, search the heart

 I test the mind" See full note at Jer. 11:20.

▣ "Even to give to each man according to his ways" YHWH is an ethical god. He created a moral universe. There are consequences to choices! We reap what we sow (cf. Job 34:11,25; Ps. 28:4; 62:12; Prov. 12:14; 24:12; Eccl. 12:14; Jer. 32:19; Ezek. 33:20; Matt. 16:27; 25:31-46; Rom. 2:6; 14:12; 1 Cor. 3:8; 2 Cor. 5:10; Gal. 6:7-10; 2 Tim. 4:14; 1 Pet. 1:17; Rev. 2:23; 20:12; 22:12).

Our lifestyle choices clearly reveal who our Father is (cf. Matt. 7).

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:11 As the rabbinical proverb goes, "a partridge sits on other birds' eggs" (cf. NIV). This may have developed from the large number of eggs that partridges lay. However, when the young hatch and develop, they leave the false parent. Those who succeed by unrighteous means will also be abandoned by their gathered wealth.

The bird "partridge" (BDB 896) is discussed in UBS', Fauna and Flora of the Bible, p. 64. Colors, gems, trees, flowers, and animals of the ANE are often difficult to specify with certainty. Usually, however, the contexts that use the allusions, idioms, and imagery are understandable.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

▣ "fools" This is the only occurrence of this NOUN (BDB 614) in Jeremiah, though the VERB occurs in Jer. 14:21. This is a common term in Wisdom Literature, but it does occur some in other genres.

  1. Deut. 32:6,21
  2. 1 Sam. 25:25; 2 Sam. 3:33; 13:13
  3. Isa. 32:5-6
  4. Ezek. 13:3

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR FOOLISH PEOPLE

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:12 This refers to

  1. the temple in Jerusalem. The "Holy of Holies" contained the Ark of the Covenant, where YHWH symbolically dwelt. It symbolized YHWH's covenant presence with Abraham's seed (cf. Jer. 14:21). One day all the earth would come and meet Him here (cf. Jer. 3:17).
  2. This list of three descriptions (MT) could refer to YHWH Himself, which fits the context. From Jer. 7, we know that these Judeans had replaced faith in YHWH with faith in the temple, but the temple would be destroyed by Neo-Babylon in 586 B.C.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:12-18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:12-18 Of all the English translations listed at the beginning of each chapter, only NASB sees Jer. 17:12-18 as a separate strophe. All others start a new strophe at Jer. 17:14.

This is another of Jeremiah's laments/confessions. Verses 12-14 may be an introduction to Jeremiah's prayer. It seems to be another way to express Jer. 17:10.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:13 "O Lord, the hope of Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:13 "O Lord, the hope of Israel" See note at Jer. 14:8.

▣ The Judeans are characterized as:

  1. all who forsake (BDB 736, KB 806, Qal PARTICIPLE) You
  2. those who turn away from Me (BDB 693, KB 747, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, Qere reading; UBS Text Project, p. 231, gives this a "B" rating)

Notice the consequences of their actions.

  1. will be put to shame (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME)
  2. will be written down (cf. Jer. 17:1; i.e. in the book of deeds, see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO BOOKS OF GOD)

These consequences are the result of forsaking (Qal PERFECT, second usage) YHWH, who is described as "the fountain of living water" (cf. Jer. 2:13; Ps. 36:9).

▣
NASB, LXX  ". . .on earth will be written down"
NKJV  "Shall be written in the earth"
NRSV, NJB, NET  "will be registered in the underworld"
TEV, REB  "They will disappear like names
  written in the dust"
TEV (footnote)  "go to the world of the dead"
JPSOA  "Shall be doomed men"
Peshitta  "shall have their names written
  in the dust"

There seem to be two ways to interpret this phrase.

  1. those who reject YHWH will be recorded in the book of deeds
  2. those who reject YHWH will be registered in the lists of the dead in Sheol (lit. "in the earth," ארץ [see SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND COUNTRY, EARTH], seen as coming from Ugaritic root for "underworld," see AB, p. 118)

SPECIAL TOPIC: WORLD (several terms), I.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:14 Jeremiah begins his lists of prayer requests to YHWH.

  1. heal me ‒ BDB 950, KB 1272, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. and I will be healed ‒ Niphal IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense
  3. save me ‒ BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  4. and I will be saved ‒ BDB Niphal COHORTATIVE

"Healing" is imagery for forgiveness, see note at Jer. 17:9. "Saving" is imagery for physical deliverance. Jeremiah felt the need of strength and assurance in both the spiritual and physical realms. Humans are creatures of both (cf. Gen. 2:7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FORGIVENESS IN THE OT

▣ "For You are my praise" Jeremiah's strength and assurance were in YHWH (cf. Deut. 10:21; Ps. 109:1). There is no other source (cf. Jer. 17:17b; 16:19).

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:15 This is the Judeans' response to Jeremiah's message. YHWH's delay was misinterpreted (cf. Isa. 5:19; Rom. 2:4; 2 Pet. 3:3-7). The delay of judgment was so that they might repent and return to YHWH. They accused Jeremiah of being a false prophet (cf. Deut. 13:1-5; 18:20-21), but he was a true prophet (cf. Deut. 18:19)! They will die!

▣ "Let it come now!" This VERB (BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) catches the arrogance and unbelief of these Jerusalemites/Judeans. They do not fear YHWH's spokesperson or YHWH Himself!

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:16 Jeremiah describes his own thoughts, feelings, and actions.

  1. I have not hurried away from being a shepherd after You (see textual note below)
  2. I have not longed for the woeful day (i.e. judgment day, invasion, exile)
  3. my message was Your message (i.e. in/from Your presence)
▣
MT, NASB, NKJV, NJB, JPSOA, NIV  "I have not hurried away
  from being a shepherd
  after You"
Peshitta, NRSV, TEV, REB, NET  "Yet I never urged you
  to send disaster"
LXX  "I have not tired of
 following after you"

The problem is not the first VERBAL "pressed" (BDB 21, KB 23, Qal PERFECT), but the following PARTICIPLE.

  1. MT, רעה, "from a shepherd" ‒ BDB 944, KB 1258, Qal PARTICIPLE (UBS Text Project, p. 237, gives this a "C" rating).
  2. The LXX has "following you," which is related to "shepherd."
  3. suggested, מרעה, "from evil," from root רעע ‒ BDB 949, KB 1269 (Peshitta). JPSOA footnote has "emendation yields 'urged you to [bring] misfortune'."
17:17
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB, Peshitta "Do not be a terror
  to me"
JPSOA, NET "Do not be a cause
  of dismay to me"
LXX "Be not to me a
  stranger"

The NASB reflects the MT. The basic root (BDB 369) can be translated:

  1. dismay
  2. terror
  3. shattered
  4. ruin

The VERB is used twice in v. 18 and is translated "dismayed" by NASB. In Ps. 88:15, it is translated "terror."

Jeremiah was surprised that following YHWH and being His spokesman would cause such internal and external problems! The intimacy that he felt with YHWH is expressed in his questions (i.e. his confessions).

If we are not careful, circumstances can blind our hearts and minds to YHWH's presence and promises. There is a difference bewtween God allowing and God sending. This is not the world that God intended it to be, that it one day will be!

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:18 Jeremiah (in typical Eastern cursing language, i.e. Ps. 139:19-22) lists his request against those of his own people who opposed him and his message.

  1. let those who persecute me be put to shame ‒ BDB 101, KB 116, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  2. let them be dismayed ‒ BDB 369, KB 365, Qal ‒ BDB IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense
  3. bring on them a day of disaster ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  4. crush them with twofold destruction ‒ BDB 990, KB 1402, Qal IMPERATIVE

Jeremiah was in a spiritual/physical struggle for the minds and hearts of the covenant people. YHWH wanted to use them in His eternal redemptive plan for all humans (cf. Jer. 3:17; 4:2; 16:19-21). This type of hyperbolic prophetic poetry seems so violent and aggressive to moderns. But there are falsehoods, spiritual deceptions, satanic alternatives to truth (cf. Eph. 4:14)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "put to shame" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME

▣ "twofold destruction" This is an idiom which denotes "complete and full" destruction (cf. Isa. 40:2; Jer. 16:18; Rev. 18:6).

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:19-27
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:19-27 YHWH responds to Jeremiah's prayer by focusing on covenant obedience, specifically Sabbath observance, see SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH (OT). Judah would be blessed or cursed based on her obedience (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-29). This one command represented all the Mosaic legislation.

The Judeans knew this but YHWH would remind them through Jeremiah's proclamation at a specific gate of the temple used by the king.

Their response is recorded in Jer. 17:23 and 27. Verses 24-27 function as a parallel strophe.

YHWH wanted to bless (cf. Jer. 17:25-26) Judah so that the world might come to know Him (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW), but they would not (cf. Ezek. 26:22-32).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:20 "listen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:20 "listen" The term (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE) means to hear so as to do (i.e. Deut. 4:1; 5:1; 6:3,4, see full note at Deut. 6:4 online)! It is repeated in Jer. 17:23, 24 (intensified), 27. This is similar to James 1:23-27. True faith involved heart, head, and hand!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:21 "take heed for yourselves"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 17:21 "take heed for yourselves" The MT is literally an idiom, "take heed for the sake of your lives." The VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Niphal IMPERATIVE) denotes careful listening (cf. Deut. 4:9,15,23; 6:12; 8:11; Josh. 23:11).

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:23 "stiffened their necks"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:23 "stiffened their necks" See note at Jer. 7:25-26. They were unwilling to hear and respond!

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:24 "if you listen attentively to Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:24 "if you listen attentively to Me" The IMPERFECT VERB is intensified by the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of the same root (BDB 1033, KB 1570). Notice the "if. . .then" structure of a conditional covenant.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:25 "chariots"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
17:25 "chariots" See SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARIOTS

▣ "forever" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios).
