READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. The literary context of Jer. 23 starts in Jer. 21:11-14, which begins YHWH's word to the royal house of Judah.

  2. The basic outline of Jer. 22:1-23:8
    1. Zedekiah, Jer. 22:1-9
    2. Shallum, Jer. 22:10-12 (Jehoahaz)
    3. Jehoiakim, Jer. 22:13-23
    4. Jehoiachim, Jer. 22:24-30 (Coniah)
    5. Zedekiah, Jer. 23:1-8 (although Zedekiah is not mentioned by name in Jer. 23:1-8, if the shepherd series continues, he is the object of the message)

  3. This chapter is a sharp contrast between the false shepherd and YHWH's Righteous Branch (i.e. Messiah; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BRANCH OF THE LORD). The contrast is heightened by the use of
    1. "say" ‒ BDB 55, KB 65, used 16 times
    2. "speak" ‒ BDB 180, KB 210, used 5 times
    3. "prophesy" ‒ BDB 612, KB 659, used 6 times

  4. This chapter has several titles for Judah's Deity.
    1. the Lord God of Israel, Jer. 23:2
    2. a righteous branch, Jer. 23:5
    3. the Lord our righteousness (Davidic Messiah's name), Jer. 23:6
    4. the Lord of hosts, Jer. 23:15,16,36
    5. a God who is near, Jer. 23:23
    6. not a God far off, Jer. 23:23
    7. the living God, Jer. 23:36
    8. our God, Jer. 23:36

  5. In the midst of terrible judgment comes the wonderful promise of YHWH's righteous Branch! There is hope; there will be salvation; there will be justice! A new day will arise from the ashes of judgment.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:3 "I Myself shall gather the remnant of My flock"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:3 "I Myself shall gather the remnant of My flock" Notice that the problem of fallen human's, even covenant humans, inability to follow God is answered by God Himself acting on their behalf. This is the "new covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34 (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36). The new covenant is based on grace, not performance (i.e. Rom. 3:21-31; Galatians 3; the book of Hebrews), but the goal is still a people who reflect YHWH's character.

The term "remnant" has several meanings. However, in this context it carries the dual meaning of

  1. returnee from exile
  2. the faithful followers of YHWH

This chapter makes it hard to distinguish between the return from exile and the future Messianic reign (cf. Jer. 23:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, THREE SENSES

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:5 "I will raise up for David a righteous Branch"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:5 "I will raise up for David a righteous Branch" This is literally "sprout," BDB 855. This was a symbol of life out of death. It was used of the Messiah in Jer. 33:15-16; Zech. 3:8; 6:12; the same concept but different terms in Isa. 11:1 ("twig," BDB 310 and "shoot," BDB 666); 53:2 ("young plant," BDB 413; "a root," BDB 1057). It (BDB 855) apparently refers to Zerubbabel in Zechariah, but foreshadows the Messiah.

In the midst of oracles of judgment, comes hope, promise, and a new leader, a new day! The concept of a Messiah is recurrent in the OT although the term is not. The Aramaic Targums read "Messiah" in this context, paralleling "Branch," which shows the rabbis of that day saw this text as Messianic. See Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 343-344, for the title's four different usages. See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DEITY OF CHRIST IN THE OT

I would like to add my comments from Isaiah 4:2 which includes brief quotes from Zech. 3:8; 6:12, and SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BRANCH OF THE LORD.
SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH
SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

Isa. 4:2 "the Branch of the Lord" To describe this title (BDB 855, Targums interpreted it as the Messiah) let me quote from my commentary on Daniel and Zechariah where the term is also used (but just a note of caution, we must be careful about assigning a technical meaning everywhere a word or phrase is used-context, context, context is crucial). This term may have developed over time from a reference to ideal abundance to God's special Servant who will restore that abundance (i.e. a shoot, a branch).

Let me share notes from my commentary on Zechariah.

Zech. 3:8 "the Branch" This may be "sprout" (BDB 855). This is another Messianic title (cf. Jer. 6:12; Isa. 4:2; 11:1; 53:2; Jer. 23:5; 33:15). See full discussion and SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS THE NAZARENE.

This title is used of Zerubbabel in Jer. 6:12 as a symbol of the royal Davidic line. It is surprising that it is used in this context, which emphasizes the priestly aspect of the Messiah. The twin aspects of redeemer (priestly, cf. Isaiah 53) and administrative leader (kingly, cf. Isa. 9:6-7) are merged in the book of Zechariah (cf. chapter 4).

Zech. 6:12 "Branch" This word (BDB 855) means "sprout" (cf. Jer. 3:8; 6:12; Isa. 4:2; 11:1; 53:2; Jer. 23:5; 33:15). This is a title for the Messiah. In Zechariah it refers to Zerubbabel as a type of the Messiah (cf. Ibn Ezra and Rashi). The name, Zerubbabel, in Akkadian, means "shoot of Babylon." This was possibly a play on his name since he rebuilt the temple in 516 B.C.., but it is really an ultimate reference to Jesus. This title and the matching VERB ("will branch out," Qal IMPERFECT) appear together in this verse.

▣ A description of YHWH's "Branch" (NKJV, NRSV, JB)

  1. beautiful, BDB 840, cf. Jer. 3:19 (often used of Promised Land in Dan. 8:9; 11:16,41)
  2. glorious, BDB 458 means "abundance," "honor," and "glory" ("glory," BDB 802, also in this verse)

These two terms are often used together (cf. Isa. 13:19; 28:1,4,5).

Some versions take this verse as a reference to plant growth in the period of restoration (LXX, Peshitta, TEV, NJB, REB, NET Bible). In a sense the Messiah and the age of restoration are lexically linked.

This is also from my notes on Isaiah 11:1:

11:1 "a shoot" This rare word found only here in the OT ("twig," "branch," or "shoot" translated "rod" in Prov. 14:3, BDB 310, KB 307), obviously refers to a supernatural Davidic descendant (cf. Jer. 6:13; 2 Samuel 7; Rev. 22:16). Out of this seemingly dead stump (i.e. exiled Judah) will come a new king! This imagery (but different Hebrew word) is seen again in the Suffering Servant Song of Isaiah 52:13-53:12 (i.e. Jer. 23:2).

The Jewish Study Bible (p. 807) adds an interesting comment on "stump."

"If the translation 'stump' is correct, then the passage may presume that the Davidic dynasty will (or has) come to an end; this reading would deviate significantly from Isaiah's notion that Davidic kings will reign eternally (cf. 2 Sam. 7:8-16; Ps. 89:20-37). But the Hebrew 'geza' refers not only to a stump of a tree that has been cut down but also to the trunk of a living tree."

I cannot confirm this meaning for "shoot" unless it is Isa. 40:24.

▣ "from the stem of Jesse" Jesse was King David's father. This future descendant is mentioned in Jer. 23:10; 9:7; 16:5.

The OT gives the lineage of the Special Coming One, the Anointed One.

  1. from the tribe of Judah, Gen. 49:8-12, esp. Jer. 23:10 and Rev. 5:5
  2. from the family of Jesse, 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17

The special child of the new age has now been identified as a special ruler. His person will characterize the new age (cf. Jer. 23:5).

▣ "a branch from his roots" The NOUN "branch," "sprout," or "shoot" (BDB 666, cf. Jer. 14:19; 60:21; Dan. 11:7) is a literary parallel to "branch" or "sprout" (BDB 855, cf. Jer. 4:2; 61:11). New growth will come!

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS THE NAZARENE

▣ "will bear fruit" The MT has the VERB "bear fruit" (פרה, BDB 826, KB 963, Qal IMPERFECT, Dead Sea Scrolls, NASB), but most ancient and modern versions assume a similar VERB פרח (BDB 827).

  1. NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta, "shall grow out"
  2. NJB, "will grow"
  3. LXX, Targums, "shall come up"
  4. 4. REB, "will spring from"
  5. JPSOA, "shall sprout"

The second option fits the parallelism best!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

▣ "He will. . ." Notice how the Branch is characterized.

  1. He will reign (cf. Isa. 9:6-7; 11:1-5; Micah 5:2-4).
  2. He will act wisely ‒ BDB 968, Hiphil PERFECT, cf. Dan. 12:3; this root can also be translated "prosper" (cf. Isa. 52:13).
  3. He will do justice ‒ Ps. 72:2; Isa. 32:1
    1. SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE
    2. SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGE, JUDGMENT, JUSTICE IN ISAIAH
  4. He will do righteousness; see SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:6 "Judah. . .Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:6 "Judah. . .Israel" This would predict the reunited kingdom (i.e. Jer. 3:18; 30:3; 31:27,31; Ezek. 37:25-28; Hosea 1:11). The United Monarchy split in 922 B.C. under Solomon's son, Rehoboam, and Jeroboam I, an Ephraimitic labor leader (cf. 1 Kings 12).

▣ "The Lord our righteousness" This may be a play on the name "Zedekiah," which means "the Lord is righteous," the person Nebuchadnezzar II put on the throne to replace Jehoiachin (cf. 2 Kings 24). It is a descriptive Messianic title in Jer. 23:5; 33:16. It is parallel to "a righteous Branch" in Jer. 23:5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:7,8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:7,8 This is a repeated literary piece from Jer. 16:14-15. The same sentiment is found in Isa. 43:18-19. A new day is coming (cf. Jer. 16:14; Hosea 3:4-5)! The new age of the Spirit, the new age of righteousness, the new age of the Messiah is coming!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:7 "As the Lord lives
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 23:7 "As the Lord lives" See note at Jer. 22:24.

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:8 The same truth is found in Jer. 16:14-15, in almost the exact words.

▣ "who brought up and led back" As YHWH's power and grace were seen in the Exodus, so too, in the return from exile!

▣ "from the north land" Assyria and Babylon were to the east of Palestine, but the only land route was from/to the north (i.e. basically following the Euphrates River to the coastal plain). This is due to the large desert between Palestine and the mouth of the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers (i.e. Mesopotamia).

▣
NASB, NKJV  "where I had driven them"
NRSV, NJB, REB  "he had driven them"
TEV  "where I had scattered them"
JPSOA  "to which I have banished them"
Peshitta  "where they had been scattered"

YHWH is in control of history. Assyria and Babylon were merely His tools of judgment (cf. Isa. 10:5, as was later, Rome in A.D. 66-70. See my revised and expanded exegetical notes on Jesus' Olivet Discourse). The UBS Text Project gives the MT "I" a "B" rating (i.e. YHWH speaking).

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:9-32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 23:9-32 Jeremiah addresses the false prophets, as they surely condemned him (cf. Example in chapter 28).

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:9 The prophet is speaking of the physical effects of God's message on him. This is much like what happened to Daniel (i.e. Dan. 7:15,28; 8:27; 10:8,16).

  1. broken heart (i.e. the center of the intellect, not emotions, cf. Jer. 8:18)
  2. bones tremble
  3. like an intoxicated person (i.e. with YHWH's revelation)

▣ "drunken man. . .a man overcome with wine" Drunkenness here is a sign of confusion, but in Jer. 25:15 it is a sign of judgment.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL ATTITUDES TOWARD ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOLISM

▣ There are two words for human beings used in this verse.

  1. ish (BDB 35) ‒ This is the term used in Gen. 2:23 to distinguish man from the newly formed woman. See Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT, pp. 48-50
  2. gever (BDB 149) ‒ This is the same root as "strong" or "mighty." See Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT, pp. 52-54.

In this context, they are in a poetic parallel relationship.

▣ Lines 6 and 7 give the reason for Jeremiah's distress. He believed God's revelation! He knew it was true. I so wish modern believers would tremble at God's word (cf. Isa. 66:5). Do we grieve over our own sinful societies and the sure wrath of God that will come (i.e. Romans 1-2; Gal. 6:7)?

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:10 "adulterers"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:10 "adulterers" In this context this (BDB 610) could refer to

  1. fertility worship (literal adultery), Jer. 3:2,6,8-9; 5:7-8
  2. foreign alliances (spiritual adultery), i.e. "lovers" (cf. Jer. 2:25; 3:1; 22:20,22, which involved the idols of these pagan nations)

▣ "land mourns" This is parallel to 10c, "dries up." This is part of the curses of Lev. 26:4,19-20; Deut. 28:23-24; 29:20-21; and Rom. 8:18-22!

▣
NASB, NRSV  "because of the curse"
NKJV, NJB  "because of a curse"
TEV  "the Lord's curse"
REB  "because of them"
LXX  "because due to these"
Peshitta  "because of these men"

the MT has "because of the curse," but the same consonants revocalized is "because of these."

  1. curse ‒ אלה (BDB 46, MT)
  2. of these ‒ אלה (LXX)

The UBS Text Project, p. 244, gives the MT a "B" rating.

▣
NASB, MT  "Their course also is evil"
  And their might is not right"
NKJV  "Their course of life is evil"
  And their might is not right"
TEV  "they live wicked lives and misuse their power"
NJB  "They are prompt to do wrong"
  Make no effort to do right"
JPSOA  "For they run to do evil"
  They strain to do wrong"
LXX  "And their course became evil"
Peshitta  "Their course of life is evil"
  And their yield has been poor"

There is no VERB in these last two poetic lines of Jer. 23:10. It seems that Jeremiah has changed imagery from nature disrupted to humans disrupted! Neither is what YHWH intended in Gen. 1:31!

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:11 It is a common theme in Jeremiah to condemn both prophet and priest (cf. Jer. 2:8). What a terrible situation! The people only hear the false words.

The prophets of Israel are described in Jer. 23:12 and the prophets of Judah in Jer. 23:14. YHWH's judgment falls on both in Jer. 23:15.

One wonders about the historical setting of this strophe. It seems to assume Israel was still in the land. The time element of Hebrew VERBS is totally related to the context (see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW GRAMMAR, II). Jeremiah had his ministry soon after Josiah became king (+/- 626 B.C.). The northern kingdom of Israel was exiled earlier in 722 B.C. by Assyria. This reference is not a "history thing" (western mindset), but a "theme thing" (eastern mindset).

Possibly the reason for mentioning the prophets of Israel is that the prophets of Judah should have learned from other's judgment (cf. Jer. 3:6-10; Ezek. 23:4-49).

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:12 "slippery paths"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:12 "slippery paths" This is a Hebrew idiom of sinful living (cf. Jer. 13:16; Ps. 35:6; 73:18; Prov. 4:19). It is the opposite of "faith," which is "to be firm" or "to be sure" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS [OT]). God's word was like a clearly marked path (cf. Ps. 119:105; Prov. 6:23). The problem with Judah's sin was not ignorance, but willful covenant disobedience!
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WAY. . .THE PATH

Notice the results of willful unfaithfulness.

  1. slippery paths
  2. driven away into the gloom (lit. "darkness," BDB 66)
  3. fall into gloom
  4. YHWH brings calamity (lit. "evil," BDB 949)

Some commentators try to link this poetic strophe to eternal punishment (which is surely biblical; choices in time affect eternity). Be careful of turning hyperbolic Hebrew poetry into doctrine. Look for clear passages from the NT.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL PUNISHMENT

SPECIAL TOPIC: GEHENNA, II. D.

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:13 "Samaria"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:13 "Samaria" This was the capital of the northern kingdom and used as a symbol for the nation as a whole.

The Northern Kingdom, formed in the split of the United Monarchy in 922 B.C., was known by three terms.

  1. Israel (a collective term)
  2. Ephraim (the largest tribe)
  3. Samaria (the nation's capital)

Jeremiah prophesied during the Neo-Babylonian period. Samaria fell during the Assyrian period (i.e. Isaiah).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF NEO-BABYLON

Timeline (Old Testament)

▣
NASB  "an offensive thing"
NKJV  "folly"
NRSV, NET  "a disgusting thing"
TEV  "the sin"
REB  "a lack of sense"
NJB  "insanity"
Peshitta  "falsehood"
LXX  "lawless deeds"
JPSOA  "repulsive thing"

The MT has the FEMININE NOUN (BDB 1074, KB 1776, cf. Job 1:22; 24:12), which refers to that which is morally inappropriate. In this context, Ba'al worship is specified. Ba'al worship was the major cause of this fall of Israel and now had become common in Judah!

▣ "They prophesied by Baal" This refers to Canaanite fertility worship (cf. Jer. 2:8). Ba'al was the male god who controlled fertility and was called "Lord."

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

▣ "astray" This VERB (BDB 1073, KB 1766, Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw) denoted mental and moral confusion and the resulting poor choices (cf. 2 Kgs. 21:9; Isa. 3:12; 9:16; Jer. 23:13,32; 42:20; Amos 2:4; Micah 3:5). The people of Judah were morally responsible for their choices, but they also had been led astray by people they trusted! Be careful who you listen to! There are still false prophets among us!

SPECIAL TOPIC: FALSE TEACHERS

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:14 Apparently, KIng Jehoiakim remodeled and expanded the royal residences. From v. 13, these building projects were done by forced labor from the tribes.

Notice lthe description of the oplulence.

  1. "spacious (BDB 926) upper (BDB 751) rooms" ‒ possibly structures built on an existing flat roof
  2. special "windows" (BDB 319)
  3. "cedar (BDB 72) paneling" (BDB 706, cf. 1 Kgs. 7:7), very expensive
  4. painted with vermillion (BDB 1059); this was a bright reddish orange dye made originally from insects, but later from the mineral cinnabar

Jehoiakim tried to match the greatness of his father, Josiah, in buildings but not in righteousness (cf. v. 15).

22:16
NASB, NJB  "Is not that what it means to know Me?"
NKJV  "Was not this knowing Me?"
NRSV  "Is not this to know me?"
TEV  "That is what it means to know the Lord"
JPSOA  "That is truly heeding Me"
JPSOA (footnote)  "That is the reward for heeding Me"
LXX  "Is not this so, because you do not know
 me?"
REB  "Did not this show he knew me?"

The MT has "not this to know me?" Knowing YHWH involves several aspects (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW).

  1. personal faith relationship (i.e. prayer and worship; see SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord)
  2. cognitive belief (i.e. Scripture truly reveals God; see SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION)
  3. volition (i.e. acting on the truth you know; lifestyle faith)

All are crucial! All reflect biblical faith (cf. Deut. 10:12-13; Hosea 6:6; Micah 6:8).

  1. a personal relationship (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)
  2. truths about that person to believe
  3. a life like that person's to live (i.e. covenant faithfulness)

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:14 This verse describes the prophets of Judah who were involved in Ba'al worship like Israel.

  1. They committed adultery (see note at Jer. 23:10)
  2. They walked in falsehood (lit. lies, referring to false prophecies, cf. v. 32)
  3. They strengthened the hand of evildoers
  4. No one repented (people or prophet or priest or shepherd)

Notice how often Jeremiah addresses the false prophets (cf. Jer. 2:8; 4:9; 5:30-31; 6:13-15; 8:10-12; 14:13-15; 18:18-23; 26:8,11,16; 27:1-22; 28:1-17).

Every generation of believers must decide to whom they will listen and respond. There are charlatans, deceivers, crooks; how does a believer know who to believe! Here are some Scriptural guidelines.

  1. the accuracy of their predictions, cf. Deut. 13:1-5; 18:18-22 (this does not relate to conditional prophecies like Jonah's)
  2. lifestyle, cf. Jer. 23:13-22; Matt. 7:15-23
  3. content of the message (for NT), cf. 1 Cor. 12:3; 15:3-4; 1 John 4:1-3

See Grant Osborne, The Hermeneutical Spiral, pp. 210-211, "The Characteristics of False Prophets."

▣ "like Sodom. . .like Gomorrah" These were the wicked cities of the Plain which YHWH destroyed in Genesis 19 (cf. Isa. 1:9,10; 3:9; 13:19; Jer. 23:14; 49:18; 50:40; Amos 4:11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOMOSEXUALITY

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:15 This verse describes what YHWH will do to these false prophets (cf. Jer. 9:15).

  1. feed them wormwood
  2. make them drink poisonous water

He gives them a taste of their own actions. They taught poison, now they must drink it themselves (cf. Jer. 17:10; Gal. 6:7). False teaching spreads like gangrene!

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:16 "the Lord of hosts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:16 "the Lord of hosts" See SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

▣ "They speak a vision of their own imagination" They speak in God's name but the message is their own (cf. Jer. 23:25; 5:31; 14:14; Ezek. 13:2,17). Whether they

  1. are sincere or purposely manipulative
  2. are self-deceived or demonically influenced
  3. proclaim half truths
  4. seek influence, power, fame, or wealth

they must be recognized and rejected by biblically influenced believers led by the Spirit. YHWH has spoken and is speaking. He wants us to understand and respond appropriately to Him and His revelation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

▣ "futility" This VERBAL (BDB 211, KB 236, Hiphil PARTICIPLE) occurs only here. The Qal form occurs in Jer. 2:5. The NOUN form (BDB 210) is used of the nothingness of idols (i.e. 2 Kgs. 17:15; Isa. 57:13; Jer. 10:15; 16:19; 51:18).

▣ Judeans are not to "listen" (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) to their prophets, because they are prophesying (BDB 612, KB 659, Niphal PARTICIPLE) falsehoods. This is recorded in Jer. 23:17b (cf. Jer. 6:14; 8:11; 14:13-14). Jeremiah has predicted that the Babylonians

  1. will invade
  2. will capture Judah and her leaders
  3. will destroy Jerusalem and the temple
  4. will exile most of the population
  5. will take the temple treasures to the temple of Marduk in Babylon as spoils

▣ "They speak a vision of their own imagination" "Imagination" is literally "heart." One wonders if they knew it was a false vision. Were they self-duped or intentionally lying? Verse 17 implies they knew it was a false message of hope (cf. Jer. 23:21,26).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:17 "They keep saying"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:17 "They keep saying" This is the Qal PARTICIPLE and INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of the same root ("to say," BDB 55, KB 65), denoting intensity.

▣
NASB, NKJV, NJB, JPSOA  "to those who despise Me,"
  The Lord has said
LXX, NRSV, REB  "to those who despise the word of the Lord"

The UBS Text Project, p. 244, gives the first option (NASB) a "C" rating (considerable doubt). The difference is a matter of vowel choice, not a consonantal change. The NET Bible prefers option #2 (LXX, RSV, NEB).

▣ "You will have peace" This was the basic message of the false prophets (cf. Jer. 5:12; 6:14; 8:11; 14:13; 28:8-9; Ezek. 13:10). God's word to the wicked is not "peace" but a "fire" and a "hammer" (cf. Jer. 23:29).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:18
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:18 Jeremiah is describing his own situation. He did "see" (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) in the council of YHWH (cf. Amos 3:7). He heard YHWH's word (i.e. from Him directly, or a literary way of referring to the "heavenly council" of YHWH and those angels who serve Him, cf. 1 Kgs. 22:19-23; Job 2:1-6) and performed it/spoke it! YHWH honors those who hear/heed/live His word and will (cf. Jer. 23:22).

▣ "in the council of the Lord" This may refer to the heavenly council of YHWH and those angels who surround Him.

  1. for praise ‒ Isa. 6:2-3; Rev. 4:8
  2. for protection ‒ Gen. 3:24
  3. for action ‒ Gen. 1:26; 3:22; 11:7; 1 Kgs. 22:19-22; Job 1:6; 2:1; 29:4; Ps. 89:7
  4. for judgment ‒ Dan. 7:10,22,26

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS

SPECIAL TOPIC: GODLY ONES, HOLY ONES

▣
NASB, NJB, REB  "and listened"
NKJV  "and heard it"
NRSV  "so as to proclaim it"
JPSOA, LXX  "must obey"
Peshitta  "and heard him"

The JPSOA footnote suggests a revocalization that yields "approve it," a VERB which occurs in vv. 22 and 28.

  1. "listened," BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERFECT with waw
  2. "announce," BDB 1033, KB 1570, Hiphil IMPERFECT (vv. 22,28)

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:19-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 23:19-20 This is similar to Jer. 30:23-24. The repetition occurs often in Jeremiah, which shows his various sermons and poems were collected and edited after his death or towards the end of his life (cf. Jer. 23:7-8, repeated in Jer. 16:14-15; Jer. 23:15 repeated in Jer. 9:15).

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:20 YHWH's judgment will come (cf. Jer. 30:24; Isa. 45:23; 55:11). The time for repentance has passed. Judah cannot repent (cf. Jer. 13:23). YHWH's only choice for His larger redemptive purpose of using Israel was to destroy and exile the current idolatrous generation. Only radical surgery can save the patient (cf. Isa. 1:5-6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ The last line of Jer. 23:20 seems to be a promise of a future time when God's people will, one day, understand

  1. His actions and greater purpose (i.e. eschatological, see chapter 17, "God's Plan" in Millard Erickson, Christian Theology, second ed., pp. 371-390)
  2. that they were duped by their false leadership (i.e. concerning the Neo-Babylonian invasion and exile, cf. Jer. 30:23)

The NET Bible (p. 1357) has a good comment about "clearly understand." This is "a Hebrew construction where a noun functions as the object of a verb from the same word root (the Hebrew cognate accusative)." See BDB 106, KB 122, Hithpolel IMPERFECT and the NOUN, BDB 108, cf. Jer. 30:24. Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT, pp. 94-95, also discusses this root and feels it denotes that which is clear or complete; here, it refers to a message of divine judgment.

▣ "in the last days" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE LAST DAYS

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:21 YHWH rejects these proclaimers of "peace" (cf. Jer. 29:9,23).

These false prophets are characterized as:

  1. "they ran" ‒ This may reflect a messenger coming to a king with haste.
  2. YHWH
    1. did not send them
    2. did not speak to them
  3. They spoke as if they knew YHWH's will, but they did not.

Notice the sarcasm of vv. 30-32!

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:21-22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:21-22 YHWH speaks again, as in Jer. 23:16-18 and also Jer. 23:23-24, 25-32. It is difficult to know how the OT writers received YHWH's revelation. Either they speak in His name and then comment on it or there is a more direct verbal reception of the message. See Hard Sayings of the Bible, chapter 8, pp. 66-69.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: ILLUMINATION

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 23:22 YHWH's spokespersons can effect change and help His people turn from evil and walk in His word and ways!

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:23-24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:23-24 Notice the three rhetorical questions. The first and third expect a "yes" answer and the second a "no" answer.

This brief strophe is a self-affirmation of YHWH's immanence

  1. personal presence with His people
  2. desire for fellowship
  3. active participation in His people's lives
  4. His presence throughout creation (i.e. His transcendence, cf. 1 Kgs. 8:27; Ps. 139:7-16; Isa. 66:1)

This expresses YHWH's immanence/omnipresence! He is the Holy One of Israel, but He is also "Father" (cf. Isa. 57:15). For a good discussion of the theological relationship between immanence and transcendence, see Millard J. Erickson, Christian Theology, 2nd ed., pp. 327-345.

Some see this brief strophe as YHWH's way of denying that He is just one of many local deities. See chapter 15, "God's Nearness and Distance. . ." in Millard Erickson, Christian Theology, second ed., pp. 327-345.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:25 "I had a dream, I had a dream"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:25 "I had a dream, I had a dream" This was a claim to divine revelation. Dreams were common ways for God to communicate (cf. Gen. 20:3; 28:12; 31:11,24; 37:5; Deut. 13:1-5). Joseph had dream interpretation as a gift from God (cf. Genesis 40-41), as did Daniel (cf. Daniel 2).

▣
NASB  "is there anything in the hearts of the prophets"
NKJV  "How long will this be in the heart of the prophets"

Other suggestions by scholars is to supply the missing SUBJECT (cf. JPSOA)

  1. my word
  2. lies (LXX, RSV, JSPOA)
  3. My name

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:25-32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:25-32 YHWH describes the false prophets. They claim revelation but have none! They even get their message from one another (Jer. 23:30). Their message (in dreams) is their own message and it will destroy Judah.

For "dreams" as a method of revelation in the ANE, see John Walton, ANE Thought and the OT, p. 243.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:27 "forgot My name"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:27 "forgot My name" This is that special use of the name to refer to God's covenant relationship and eternal character. Judah was attributing God's acts to Ba'al!

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:29 In this verse YHWH describes His word as

  1. a fire (cf. Jer. 5:14; 20:9)
  2. a hammer which shatters a rock

God's word has results (cf. Isa. 49:2)! The false prophets bring no benefit (cf. Jer. 23:32; this is the Hiphil INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT VERB of the same root [BDB 418, KB 420] which denotes intensity). The imagery in the NT of Jesus with a two edged sword coming out of His mouth is the same type of figurative language (cf. Rev. 1:16; 2:12,16; 19:15; Heb. 4:12).

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:30-32
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 23:30-32 the UBS Handbook for Translators on Jeremiah says these verses are a summary of YHWH's message against the false, self-deceived prophets (p. 513, this is such a helpful grammatical and syntactical resource for translators and interpreters).

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:33 "oracle"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:33 "oracle" The term (BDB 672) meant "to lift up a burden." It is a play on the two uses of this term (see full note at Isa. 13:1).

  1. a heavy word from God
  2. a load that an animal carried

The AB suggests that the Hebrew text be divided in a different way from the MT. If so it could read, "What is the massa" (that is, the utterance of Yahweh? say to them, "you are the massa [that is, the burden], and I will cast you off‒Yahweh's word," p. 150). The LXX and Vulgate, followed by NRSV, REB, NET, have, "You are the burden." Hereby the word play on "burden" (BDB 672 I) is made clear.

The Hebrew root, םשׂא, can mean

  1. burden ‒ BDB 672 II
  2. utterance ‒ BDB 672 III, cf. Isa. 13:1; 15:1; Jer. 23:33,34,36,38 (thrice)

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:33-40
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:33-40 This strophe presents its message by a series of questions that Judeans ask each other about YHWH's revelation (i.e. what is the oracle of the Lord).

  1. prophets
  2. priests
  3. people

Jeremiah's answer is that there are no more messages to be received, only judgment (i.e. "I shall abandon you," cf. Jer. 12:7; 23:39). The religious leaders were making up their own message in YHWH's name (cf. Jer. 23:36). They did not really want to hear from Him.

Because of this false message supposedly from God, YHWH says

  1. I will forget you (this is a PERFECT VERB and an INFINITIVE ABSOSLUTE from the same root, which denotes intensity)
  2. I will cast you away from My presence
  3. I will cast away the Jerusalem/temple
  4. I will give you an everlasting reproach
  5. I will give you an everlasting humiliation, either of which will never be forgotten

Wow! These idolatrous Judeans and their leaders will be permanently cut off. The faithful remnant, though not specifically mentioned, will be restored.

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:35-36
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 23:35-36 This is exactly the opposite of the "new covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34 (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36). Knowledge of the Lord is the exception, not the rule!

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:36 "every man's own word will become the oracle"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:36 "every man's own word will become the oracle" This very phrase is the reality of a post-modern, western, twenty-first century culture. There are no absolutes! Everyone's opinion has weight and authority! This is a lie since there is an inspired revelation from the one true God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

▣ "you have perverted the words of the living God, the Lord of hosts, our God" The VERB (BDB 245, KB 253, Qal PERFECT with waw) means "to turn" or "to overturn." To put this in modern idiom, these false religionists put a "spin" on their words, their interest, their presuppositions, their historical setting, their personal preferences, claiming it was God's words.

The same occurs today by denominations and secularists! Only a commitment to revelation and a knowledge of it can protect a believer.

This verse ends with three titles for Israel's Deity.

  1. Elohim (BDB 43, lit. "the Loving God")
  2. YHWH of Hosts (BDB 217 and BDB 838; see SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS)
  3. our God (Eloah, BDB 43, see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.)
23:39
NASB  "I shall surely forget you and cast you away"
NKJV  "I, even I, will utterly forget you and forsake you"
NRSV  "I will surely lift you up and cast you away"
TEV  "I will certainly pick them up and throw them far
  away"
JPSOA  "I will utterly forget you and I will cast you away"
REB  "I Myself shall carry you like a burden and throw
  you away out of my sight"
Peshitta  "I will surely remove you, and cast you away"

There are several grammatical elements.

  1. the first VERB, "forget" (נשׁה, BDB 674 III, KB 728, Qal PERFECT with waw) is followed by its INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of the same root in the MT, which denotes intensity
  2. some Hebrew MSS and the Septuagint change the VERB to "lift up" (נשׁא, BDB 669, KB 724), which is the same root as "burden," used in Jer. 23:33 (twice),34,36 (twice), 38 (thrice)
  3. the parallel VERB in Jer. 23:33, "cast off" (BDB 643, KB 695, Qal PERFECT with waw) is repeated in Jer. 23:39
  4. the change made by the LXX makes sense in the context of Jer. 23:33-40 (i.e. word play)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

SPECIAL TOPIC: MASORETIC TEXT

entries.title: Jeremiah 23:40 "everlasting"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
23:40 "everlasting" This Hebrew term, 'olam (BDB 761), must always be interpreted theologically in light of

  1. the context where it is used
  2. the conditional nature of God's covenant with humans (i.e. mercy and repentance are always possible)

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "everlasting reproach" The first NOUN is 'olam (BDB 761). It must be interpreted in specific context because of its wide semantic field.

The second NOUN (BDB 357) means "reproach" or "scorn." The root is used several times in Jeremiah (cf. Jer. 6:10; 15:15; 20:8; 23:40; 24:9; 25:18; 31:19; 42:18; 44:8,12; 49:13 (of Edom); 51:51.

▣ "everlasting humiliation" The first NOUN is the same as above. The second NOUN (BDB 484) is found in this form only here in the OT and means "ignominy." A related root is found in Jer. 20:11, where it is translated "eternal dishonor" or "eternal disgrace."

Verse 40 is obviously hyperbolic. See D. Brent Sandy. Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic.

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Jeremiah 24:1 "Nebuchadnezzar"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
24:1 "Nebuchadnezzar" See SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF NEO-BABYLON

▣ The "captivity" of this Judean King Jehoiachin specifically dates this strophe as 597 B.C. (cf. 2 Kgs. 24:10-16; 2 Chr. 36:9-10). This king goes by three names.

  1. Jeconiah, 24:1; 27:20; 28:4; 29:2
  2. Coniah, 22:24,28; 37:1
  3. Jehoiachin, 52:31; 2 Kings 24-25

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED KINGDOM

▣ "craftsmen" This term (BDB 360, cf. Jer. 29:2) refers to an engraver of

  1. gems (cf. Exod. 28:11)
  2. stone (cf. 2 Sam. 5:11)
  3. wood (cf. Jer. 10:3)
  4. metal (cf. Jer. 10:9)

It can also denote an "idol-maker" (cf. 2 Kgs. 24:14,16; Isa. 44:11; 45:16).

▣ "smith" This ambiguous term (BDB 688, KB 604 II) may refer to

  1. a metal worker (NJB, NET)
  2. possibly "builders" or "engineers"
  3. "harem" (REB textual marginal note)

▣ "two baskets of figs" This is another visual image to communicate God's message vividly to the people of Judah who were left in Jerusalem.

Amos used the same type of imagery in Amos 8:1-3.

▣ "set before the temple of the Lord" These baskets of figs represented two groups of people. They were seen as offerings to YHWH (cf. Deut. 26:2-11), to use for His purposes.

  1. good figs ‒ those Judeans already exiled
  2. bad figs ‒ those Judeans left in Palestine

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Jeremiah 24:2 "very bad figs"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
24:2 "very bad figs" These figs are characterized in two ways.

  1. very good figs
    1. NOUN, BDB 1061, "figs"
    2. ADJECTIVE, BDB 373 II, "good"
    3. ADVERB, BDB 547, "very"
  2. very bad figs
    1. NOUN, BDB 1061, "figs"
    2. ADJECTIVE, BDB 948, "bad"
    3. ADVERB, BDB 547, "very"
  3. bad
    1. PREPOSITION, "so"
    2. NOUN, BDB 947, "bad"

These same inedible, rotten figs are mentioned in Jer. 29:17.

entries.title: Jeremiah 24:5 "Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
24:5 "Lord" This is the title for the Covenant God (cf. Gen. 2:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "God" This is the SINGULAR form of the title for Deity in Gen. 1:1 (Elohim).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

▣ "of Israel" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name).

▣ The good figs are, surprisingly, the Judeans taken into exile. One would have thought the ones left in Palestine were the favored ones, but not so. YHWH will work with the exiles

  1. to whom Ezekiel ministered in Babylon
  2. that YHWH Himself left the temple and traveled east (cf. Ezek. 1; 10)

▣ "Chaldeans" See SPECIAL TOPIC: CHALDEANS

entries.title: Jeremiah 24:6 "for good"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 24:6 "for good" This common ADJECTIVE (BDB 373 II, III; NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 353-356) is also used to describe "one basket of figs" (i.e. those Judeans taken into exile by Neo-Babylon). This root has a wide semantic field (i.e. BDB 373-376). In this context, it denotes that the welfare and happiness will be with the exiles and not those Judeans who remain (i.e. Jer. 21:10; Amos 9:4).

entries.title: Jeremiah 24:6-7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
24:6-7 List the promises YHWH makes to the Judeans in exile.

  1. He will regard them as "good" (BDB 373 II, III)
  2. He will set His eyes on them for good (see SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN)
  3. He will bring them back to Judah
  4. He will build them up and not overthrow them
  5. He will plant them and not pluck them up
  6. He will give them a heart to know Him

Jer. 24:7 has several covenant terms. It speaks of a new day of faithfulness and devotion (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36; Jer. 31:31-34). YHWH will give them a "new heart" and a "new mind."

The phrases "build them up" (BDB 124, KB 139); "not overthrow them" (BDB 248, KB 256); "plant them" (BDB 642, KB 694); and "not pluck them up" (BDB 684, KB 737) are also used in Jeremiah's call in Jer. 1:10. Here these VERBS are preceded by a vision, but there they are preceded by two visions (an almond rod and a boiling pot).

entries.title: Jeremiah 24:7 "I will give them a heart to know Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
24:7 "I will give them a heart to know Me" Notice the new faith necessary to be YHWH's covenant people is not based in human covenant performance, but is a gift from YHWH. This is the essence of the New Covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; 32:40; Ezek. 36:22-36). This new way of fellowship and intimacy with the Creator is often called "a personal faith relationship." It is more lthan ritual and liturgy.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Heart

SPECIAL TOPIC: Know

SPECIAL TOPIC: Call On HIs Name

SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord

▣ "they will return to Me" This VERB (BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal IMPERFECT) is used to express true repentance. This involves the mystery of foreknowledge, human free will and predestination.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PREDESTINATION [CALVINISM] vs HUMAN FREE WILL [ARMINIANISM]

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION AND THE NEED FOR A THEOLOGICAL BALANCE)

▣ "with a whole heart" This is a Hebrew idiom of complete devotion (cf. Jer. 3:10; 1 Sam. 7:3; 1 Chr. 22:19; 2 Chr. 22:9; Joel 2:12-14). It was used of David's devotion to YHWH but not Solomon who, in his old age, became involved in idolatry (cf. 1 Kings 11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

entries.title: Jeremiah 24:8-10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 24:8-10 The royal family of Zedekiah and all his helpers will be abandoned (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal IMPERFECT). This VERB has a wide semantic field. The context requires "give over" (cf. Num. 21:3,29; Deut. 7:2,23; 31:5; Jdg. 20:13; etc.). This is so shocking in light of 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17!

entries.title: Jeremiah 24:8 "the remnant of Jerusalem"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
24:8 "the remnant of Jerusalem" Here, the phrase is negative and refers to those left in Jerusalem.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses).

▣ "the ones who dwell in the land of Egypt" Who these are depends on to whom verses 8-10 refer. It probably refers to those in Zedekiah's day, after the exile of 597 B.C. If so, then who are "the ones"?

  1. those taken into exile by Pharaoh Necho II along with Jehoahaz (609 B.C.; cf. 2 Kgs. 23:31-34)
  2. pro-Egypt supporters who fled when they saw Babylon invading
  3. a future reference to those who fled to Egypt after the murder of Gedaliah (cf. Jeremiah 40-41)

entries.title: Jeremiah 24:9-10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
24:9-10 These two verses describe what YHWH will do to those who remain in Judah and those who fled to Egypt.

  1. make them a terror (lit. "horror," BDB 266, cf. Jer. 15:4; 29:18; 34:17)
  2. make them an evil (BDB 949, cf. Deut. 31:17,21; Jer. 4:6; 5:12; 19:3; 36:31)
  3. make them a reproach (BDB 357, cf. Deut. 28:37; 1 Kgs. 9:7; Ps. 44:13-14)
  4. make them a proverb (BDB 605)
  5. make them a taunt (BDB 1042)
  6. make them a curse (BDB 887, cf. Jer. 25:18; Isa. 65:15; Ezeh. 8:13)
  7. send the sword
  8. send the famine
  9. send the pestilence

This was because of their continuing, unrepentant covenant disobedience. YHWH revoked the covenant promises made to their forefathers (cf. Jer. 24:10). Instead of the "nations" seeing YHWH's mercy, grace, and justice in the covenant people, they saw His judgment (cf. Deut. 28:25,37; Ezek. 36:22-23). This very purpose in YHWH's calling Abraham (cf. Gen. 12:3) has been compromised!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:1 This is obviously an attempt to date the prophecy historically (cf. Jer. 25:3).

  1. the fourth year of Jehoiakim (i.e. 605 B.C., same year as the defeat of the Egyptian army of Necho II at Carchemish, cf. Jer. 46:2)
  2. the first year of Nebuchadnezzar II (possibly both, 604 B.C.)

The poems of Jeremiah have been organized by themes, key words, word plays (sound plays, semantic field). They are not chronological (although the earlier chapters may be).

One tenet in hermeneutical theory is to establish the historical setting and try to identify the reason for the poem/prophecy. When there is no historical item mentioned it becomes theological speculation (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar").

Notice the king of Neo-Babylon is spelled here Nebuchadnezzar. There are always differences when transliterating names. The Babylonian name is Nabu-kudurri-osur, but it is transliterated two different ways in the OT (with an "n" and an "r").

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF NEO-BABYLON

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:1-3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:1-3 Jeremiah had presented YHWH's revelation to Judah for 23 years, but they would not respond in repentance and obedience. In Jer. 36:1-2, he is told to write down his revelations. One of my favorite resources on how to interpret the genre of prophecy is D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic. He discusses the movement from oral to a written document using Jeremiah, pp. 50-54.

Moderns do not know "who," "when," or "how" the Old Testament/Hebrew Bible was formed. The Septuagint is our earliest version, but it is not an autograph.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:2 Jeremiah identifies his audience as

  1. all the people of Judah, Jer. 25:1,2
  2. all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, Jer. 25:2

The first designation would relate to the common people of Judah and the second to her leadership and the elite of society.

Notice that in Jer. 25:4 he calls them "His servants." YHWH's people are meant to be servants and priests (i.e. Exod. 19:5-6). Yet, Jeremiah's twenty-three years of delivering YHWH's revelations had not affected these sin-hardened people.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:3 "the thirteenth year of Josiah"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:3 "the thirteenth year of Josiah" This would be 627 B.C.., the year of Jeremiah's call (cf. Jer. 1:1-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED MONARCHY

▣ "even to this day" This phrase (and variations) occurs many times in the OT. For most scholars it shows the presence of a later editor/compiler, but here it is used by an author to refer to his previous ministry. We must always be careful of our assumptions. They are just that! Moderns do not understand ancient literature as well as they think they do!!

SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

▣ "the word of the Lord has come to me" As a modern preacher/teacher, how do I know the Lord has spoken to me, directed me? It is obvious the OT prophets and NT Apostles had a unique revelation (see SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY [OT]). For those of us who live and serve in the post-apostolic age, our message must be linked to inspired authors and their message. Every text has only one meaning (i.e. the intent of the original author) but many applications. We cannot just say, "God told me!" We must point people to texts that they can evaluate for themselves! Texts have priority!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

▣
NASB, REB  "again and again"
NKJV  "rising early and speaking"
NRSV, JPSOA  "I have spoken persistently to you"
NJB  "I have never tired of speaking to you"
LXX  "being early and speaking"
Peshitta  "sending them in advance"

The NKJV is the Hebrew idiom (two INFINITIVE ABSOLUTES; BDB 1014, KB 1492 and BDB 1018, KB 1511). It occurs in Jer. 25:4; 7:25; 11:7; 26:5. This idiomatic language represents one of the greatest challenges to interpreters because idioms, by their very nature, are not literal. The words have a special meaning. An idiom such as this can be understood because it is repeated and contextually obvious, but others are very difficult.

  1. to identify as an idiom
  2. to ascertain its meaning in context

I am sure when we get to heaven and get to visit with these original authors, we and they, will be shocked by what we thought they meant! For a good book dealing with this, see G. B. Caird, The Language and Imagery of the Bible.

▣ "but you have not listened" This VERB (BDB 1033, KB 1570) is a Qal PERFECT which denoted a settled opposition to hearing and obeying YHWH! These are His people. They have His revelation but they seem not to recognize the choice of "life" or "death" (cf. Deut. 30:15,19; Psalm 1) connected to YHWH's words (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-28).

For further insights to this VERB, see notes in my commentary on Deuteronomy 4:1; 5:1; and 6:5. It is online free in several languages at www.freebiblecommentary.org.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:4 Notice the parallelism between

  1. you have not listened ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal PERFECT
  2. inclined your ear to hear ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

Hebrew poetry must be interpreted through (1) purposeful poetic parallelism, (2) parallel biblical passages, and (3) word plays.

Also notice the number of Hebrew words that begin with שׁ in Jer. 25:3-5 (i.e. word/sound play).

  1. hear (thrice), שׁמע, BDB 1033, KB 1570
  2. send (twice), שׁלח, BDB 1018, KB 1511
  3. rise (twice), שׁכס, BDB 1014, KB 1492
  4. turn, שׁוב, BDB 996, KB 1427

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:4-7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:4-7 YHWH lists why He is angry with His covenant people, Judah.

  1. they have not listened and obeyed, Jer. 25:4,7
  2. they have not responded (see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [OT]), Jer. 25:5
  3. they have committed flagrant idolatry, Jer. 25:6,7 (i.e. "the work of your hands," cf. Jer. 25:14; 1:16; 10:3-5; Isa. 2:8; 17:8; 37:19)

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:5 "turn"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:5 "turn" The Qal IMPERATIVE is a call for repentance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

▣ "from his evil way" Biblical faith involves:

  1. a faith relationship with God
  2. an acceptance of this revelatory message
  3. a lifestyle of worship and obedience (i.e., evil way. . .evil deeds)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "dwell in the land which the Lord has given to you and your forefathers forever and ever" This reflects Jer. 7:7, which reflects Deut. 4:40. The land was part of the Abrahamic Covenant (cf. Gen. 12:1-3; 15:12-21). It was meant to be a permanent gracious gift, but there were conditions (i.e. covenant obedience, cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-28,30).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:6 "other gods"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:6 "other gods" The Hebrew title Elohim is used of God as Creartor, Provider, and Sustainer of all life on the planet (i.e. Gen. 1-2). It is also used of the gods (i.e. demonic influence) of the nations. When the title refers to YHWH, it uses a SINGULAR VERB.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

▣ "worship" See SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP.

▣ "do not provoke Me" This VERB (BDB 494, KB 491, Hiphil IMPERFECT) is often used of YHWH's reaction to idolatry (i.e. Deut. 32:21; 1 Kgs. 15:30; 16:13; 22:53; 2 Kgs. 23:26; 2 Chr. 28:25). YHWH is a jealous God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUSY

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 25:7 Verse 7 is parallel to v. 6. "The work of your hands" surely denotes the creation of idols (i.e. Jer. 25:14; 32:30; Isa. 2:8; 17:8; 40:19; 41:24,29; 44:17; Ps. 115:4-8).

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:8-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:8-11 YHWH lists the results of their disobedience (Jer. 25:8).

  1. I will send and take all the families of the north (cf. Jer. 1:14,15; 4:6; 6:1,22; 10:22; 13:20). YHWH controls both Assyria (i.e. Isa. 10:5) and Babylon (cf. v. 9), as well as Persia (Isa. 44:28; 45:1), for His purposes!
  2. They will invade, destroy, and exile the people of Palestine.
  3. Society will be radically changed from peace to panic.
    1. I will take the voice of joy (BDB 965)
    2. I will take the voice of gladness (BDB 970)
    3. I will take the voice of the bridegroom (BDB 368)
    4. I will take the voice of the bride (BDB 483)
    5. I will take the sound of the millstone (BDB 932)
    6. I will take the light of the lamp (BDB 21 CONSTRUCT BDb 632)

This social imagery denotes utter destruction (cf. Jer. 25:9). The land of promise and abundance will be the land of

  1. horror, Jer. 25:9,11
  2. hissing, Jer. 25:9
  3. everlasting desolation, Jer. 25:9,11

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:8 "Lord of hosts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:8 "Lord of hosts" see SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord of Hosts.

▣ "because you have not obeyed My words" Obedience is crucial because the Mosaic Covenant, like prophecy, is conditional. Judah did not respond to Moses or the Prophets!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:9 "My servant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:9 "My servant" This is the same title (BDB 712, 713) used of the Messiah in Servant Songs of Isaiah 40-66. Here it is not used in a Messianic sense, but is a way of denoting one who fulfills YHWH's purpose (i.e. "Nebuchadnezzar King of Babylon," cf. Jer. 27:6; 43:10; Isa. 13:3).

Cyrus is called "My shepherd" (Isa. 44:28) and "His anointed" (Isa. 45:1) in the same sense. As YHWH used Pharaoh in the Exodus (see SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD HARDENED), He uses these kings to accomplish His wider purposes!

The one true God is actively involved in all of human history. The Bible records that aspect of this involvement that relates to redemption through Israel and the Messiah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

▣ "utterly destroy" This is the Hebrew VERB herem (BDB 355 I, KB 353), Hiphil PERFECT with waw. It is used of things devoted to God and, thereby they become too holy for common use (BDB 356, cf. Lev. 27:21,28,29; Num. 18:14; Deut. 7:26; 13:17; Josh. 6:17-18; 7:1,11,12,13,15).

The same root (BDB 355) means "to completely destroy" (cf. Jer. 25:9; 50:21,26; 51:3; Exod. 22:20; Lev. 27:28,29; Num. 21:2,3; Deut. 2:34; 3:6; 7:2; 13:15; 20:17). This second sense is how the word is used in Jeremiah.

This is "holy war" terminology. The God who fought for Israel in the conquest of Joshua now fights against Judah and Jerusalem (i.e. the very place "He caused His name to dwell," which is repeated often in Deuteronomy).

SPECIAL TOPIC: UTTERLY DESTROY

▣
NASB  "horror"
NKJV, Peshitta  "astonishment"
NRSV, NJB, REB  "object of horror"
JPSOA  "desolation"
LXX  "an annihilation"

This Hebrew word (BDB 1031, KB 1566) means "waste" or "devastation." It is used numerous times by Jeremiah (cf. Jer. 4:27; 6:8; 9:11; 10:22; 12:10,11; 25:12; 32:43; 34:22; 44:6; 49:2,33; 50:13; 51:26,62).

▣ "hissing" This Hebrew word (BDB 1057, KB 1657) means "to hiss" (cf. Jer. 18:16; 19:8; 25:18) or "to whistle." The Jewish Study Bible, at Jer. 18:16, has the footnote, "These actions were performed at the sight of ruin to ward off a like fate from the observer" (p. 964).

▣
NASB, Peshitta  "an everlasting desolation"
NKJV  "perpetual desolations"
NRSV, LXX  "an everlasting disgrace"
NJB, REB  "ruin them for ever"
JPSOA  "ruins for all time"

The MT has "everlasting ruins" (BDB 352 CONSTRUCT BDB 761). BDB 352 means "waste," "desolation," or "ruin" (ח רבה) However, the LXX changes the root to "reproach" (BDB 357, חרפה). The UBS Text Project, p. 248, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

The word translated "everlasting" (BDB 352) must be interpreted in context. It has a wide semantic field (see Special Topic below).

For a good discussion of the use of hyperbole, see D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks, chapter 2, "What Makes Prophecy Problematic?" (pp. 31-57).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:11 "seventy years"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:11 "seventy years" This time prediction is also mentioned in Jer. 29:10; 2 Chr. 36:21-23; Dan. 9:2; and Zech. 7:5. Seventy is a round number which denotes

  1. multiple generations
  2. a complete life (cf. Ps. 90:10; Isa. 23:15)

It is interesting that the date of the destruction of the temple by Nebuchadnezzar II (i.e. 586 B.C.) is exactly seventy years from the rebuilding of the second temple by Zerubbabel (i.e. 516 B.C., cf. Zech. 1:12).

Remember, the ancients thought of numbers differently than moderns.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #4

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEVENTY YEARS

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:12-14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:12-14 Jeremiah records YHWH's commitment to judging Neo-Babylon. The same phrase, "an everlasting desolation" from Jer. 25:9 is now used of the ones who made Palestine desolate.

Notice that Jeremiah alludes to his own book (i.e. "this book"), but notice Jeremiah is mentioned by name, which implies Baruch (cf. Jer. 36:4,29,32) or another editor (i.e. Ezra). The destruction and judgment of Neo-Babylon is predicted and described in Jer. 51 and Isa. 13.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:13 "against all the nations"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:13 "against all the nations" Several of the Prophets have chapters about YHWH's judgment of the nations. These nations probably never heard these messages. They are written to show the universal nature of Israel's God (cf. LXX, Deut. 32:8). All history is before Him. He is not like the dead, blind, deaf idols; He acts in His world.

The NJB entitles Jer. 25:13c-38 "Introduction to the Prophecies Against the Nations." The LXX moves these prophecies from chapters 46-51 in the MT to begin at chapter 25 in the Septuagint.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MASORETIC TEXT

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:14 This verse is in parentheses in the NASB, NKJV, which denotes the comments of an editor or an aside from Baruch (i.e. Jeremiah's scribe, cf. Jer. 32; 36).

▣ "I will recompense them according to their deeds" See full notes at Jer. 17:10 and full list of texts at Gal. 6:7-10. We reap what we sow, often in kind!

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:15 "this cup of the wine"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:15 "this cup of the wine" This is a Hebrew idiom for judgment (cf. Jer. 13:13; 51:7; Ps. 75:8; Isa. 51:17,22). Notice it again asserts that YHWH, not the gods of the nations, controls the outcome of wars and international treaties, etc. (cf. Jer. 25:28; 1:10; LXX of Deut. 32:8).

Notice the number of times in this context the VERBS related to drinking/drunkenness are used.

  1. give to drink ‒ BDB 1052, KB 1639, Hiphil PERFECT with waw, Jer. 25:15,17
  2. drink ‒ BDB 1059, KB 1667, Qal PERFECT, Jer. 25:16,26,28 (thrice)
  3. be drunk ‒ BDB 1016, KB 1500, Qal IMPERATIVE, Jer. 25:27
  4. surely drink ‒ BDB 1059, KB 1667, INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and Qal IMPERFECT of the same root for intensity, Jer. 25:28
  5. stagger ‒ BDB 172, KB 200, Hithpoel PERFECT with waw
  6. go mad ‒ BDB 237, KB 248, Hithpoel PERFECT with waw

SPECIAL TOPIC: ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOL ABUSE

▣ "wrath. . .My hand" The only vocabulary that humans have to speak of God is analogy and negation (i.e. what God is not). God is an eternal, spiritual Being with no corporal aspect.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:17 "cup"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:17 "cup" This is imagery of judgment.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CUP

▣ "all the nations" The list of nations in Jer. 25:18-26 is

  1. mostly listed in Jeremiah 46-51
  2. listed as part of the Persian Empire

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:18 "a ruin, a horror, a hissing and a curse"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:18 "a ruin, a horror, a hissing and a curse" These very words of judgment are mentioned in v. 9.

▣ "as it is this day" This repeated phrase seems to denote a later editorial note, possibly from Baruch (cf. v. 14).

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:20-24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 25:20-24 These nations are located in the same general geographical area as Judah (as well as Zimri in v. 25).

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:23 "all who cut the corners of their hair"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:23 "all who cut the corners of their hair" This pagan practice is mentioned two other times in Jeremiah (cf. Jer. 9:26; 49:32) and may relate to Lev. 19:27-28 or 21:5 (cf. Deut. 14:1-2). Its exact nature is uncertain.

  1. pagan rite
  2. mourning rite (i.e. ancestor worship)

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:25
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:25 There are several names that refer to Mesopotamia.

  1. Elam
  2. Media
  3. "Kings of the north"
  4. Sheshach (possibly Babylon)

All of these nations mentioned in vv. 20-25 were part of Neo-Babylon's mercenary army or they took advantage of the invasion.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:26 "all the kings of the north, near and far"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:26 "all the kings of the north, near and far" This phrase is used of those nations directly north of Palestine and those of the Fertile Crescent/Mesopotamia.

▣ "Sheshach" This (BDB 1058) is an "atbash" (Jewish Study Bible) cryptogram for Babel.

  1. JPSOA footnote, c
  2. footnote on p. 1001 from the New Oxford Annotated Bible, NRSV
  3. AB says in a footnote, "a cipher by which letters of one name, counted from the beginning of the alphabet, are exchanged for corresponding letters counted from the end" (p. 161). This is from Jerome. The method is called atbash (also note Jer. 51:1).

▣ "all the kingdoms of the earth which are upon the face of the ground" This is hyperbolic (cf. Jer. 25:29)! This refers to the nations of which Israel/Judah had knowledge (i.e. the ANE). It would not include China, the Americas, etc., but theologically it would! God loves all the nations and wants all of them to know Him (i.e. Gen. 1:26,27; 3:15; 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH (erets)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:27
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:27 There is a string of commands related to drunkenness as imagery for judgment.

  1. drink ‒ BDB 1059, KB 1667, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. be drunk ‒ BDB 1016, KB 1500, Qal IMPERATIVE
  3. vomit ‒ BDB 883, KB 1096, Qal IMPERATIVE
  4. fall ‒ BDB 656, KB 709, Qal IMPERATIVE
  5. notice the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT VERB of #1 in Jer. 25:28 for intensity

▣ "Lord of hosts" See SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord of Hosts

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:28 "You shall surely drink!"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 25:28 "You shall surely drink!" This is an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and an IMPERFECT VERB of the same root used to show certainty (BDB 1059, KB 1667).

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:29
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:29 Jerusalem, who had such privileges, will be judged along with the rest of mankind!

▣ "in this city which is called by My name" This is a recurrent phrase from Deuteronomy, which denotes God's special choice of Jerusalem as the site of His temple (i.e., Deut. 12:5,11,13,14,18,21,26; 14:23-25; 15:20; 16:2,6,11,15; 17:8,10; 18:6; 26:2; 31:11; Exod. 20:24; 1 Kgs. 8:43).

This special city will also be punished for its covenant disobedience.

▣ "completely free" This is the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT VERB from the same root (BDB 667, KB 720) for dramatic emphasis. The city which was called by YHWH's name was surely responsible for her

  1. covenant breaking
  2. refusal to repent
  3. continued idolatry

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:30 "roar"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:30 "roar" The imagery of YHWH's judgment changes in Jer. 25:30-38 to YHWH as a lion (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LIONS IN THE OT).

"Roar" is the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT VERB from the same root (BDB 980, KB 1367) for intensity. For this same imagery see Joel 2:11 and Amos 1:2.

Notice all the auditory terms used in vv. 30-31 (also note Isa. 66:6).

  1. prophet speaking (i.e. "prophesy against them all these words"), v. 30a
  2. YHWH roaring (BDB 980), v. 30b,c
  3. YHWH roaring mightily, v. 30d
  4. a harvest shout (BDB 212), v. 30e
  5. a clamor (BDB 981, possible battle shout), v. 31a
  6. YHWH gives His verdict (i.e. court imagery, cf. Jer. 2:9), v. 31c
  7. later in v. 34 the leaders of Judah "wail" (BDB 410) and "cry" (BDB 277); also note v. 36

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:30-31
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:30-31 This strophe characterizes YHWH and His purposes. He wanted to bless mankind but they would not, so judgment came on all (hyperbole). Notice the one true God judges (cf. Jer. 25:38)

  1. His own flock, Jer. 25:30, line 4
  2. the world (i.e. "the nations," "all flesh"), Jer. 25:31

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:32-38
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:32-38 Again a poem of YHWH's universal judgment is appended to the similar poem of Jer. 25:30-31. Were they spoken together at the same time? Probably not. The reason the prophet seems so repetitive is the organization of these poems by theme or key words.

Notice the phrases that speak of universal judgment.

  1. Jer. 25:15 ‒ "caused all the nations to drink it" (cup of judgment)
  2. Jer. 25:17 ‒ "made all the nations to drink it"
  3. Jer. 25:19 ‒ "all his (i.e. Pharaoh) people"
  4. Jer. 25:20 ‒ "all the foreign people"
  5. Jer. 25:20 ‒ "all the kings" (Jer. 25:20 [twice], 22 [thrice],24,26)
  6. Jer. 25:26 ‒ "all the kingdoms of the earth which are upon the face of the ground"
  7. Jer. 25:29 ‒ "all the inhabitants of the earth"
  8. Jer. 25:30 ‒ "against all the inhabitants of the earth"
  9. Jer. 25:31 ‒ "to the ends of the earth"
  10. Jer. 25:31 ‒ "with the nations"
  11. Jer. 25:31 ‒ "with all flesh"
  12. Jer. 25:32 ‒ "from nation to nation"
  13. Jer. 25:32 ‒ "from the remotest part of the earth"
  14. Jer. 25:33 ‒ "from one end of the earth to the other"

One God created the earth. One God wanted fellowship with humans made in His image and likeness (cf. Gen. 1:26,27). All humans rebelled (i.e. in Adam, Genesis 3, and in personal choices, Gen. 6:5,11,12; 8:21; Rom. 3:9-18,23). The consequences are universal, but so too, the love of God in the Messiah (cf. John 3:16; 1 Tim. 2:4; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:2). Judgment is not the last word but it is a necessary word (i.e. Rom. 1:18-3:8)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:33
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:33 Improper burial was a terrible end of life. In the ANE it even affected the afterlife (cf. Jer. 14:6; 16:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BURIAL PRACTICES

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:34 "shepherds"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:34 "shepherds" This refers to both the religious and civil leadership of Judah.

▣ There are two difficulties in this verse.

  1. "dispersions" (NASB, NKJV, NRSV, KB 1775)
    "shattered" (NJB, NIV, BDB 1074; also note KB 1775, "and you will be dispersed")
    "break you in pieces" (JPSOA; BDB 1074)
    The Hebrew word (BDB 807) is found only here and its root is uncertain.
  2. "vessel" (כלי, MT, NASB, NKJV, NJB, JPSOA, BDB 479)
    "rams" (איל, LXX, TEV, RSV, NEB, AB, BDB 17)
    The Hebrew word is uncertain. The UBS Text Project gives "vessel" (SINGULAR) a "B" rating.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:38 "His fierce anger"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
25:38 "His fierce anger" See SPECIAL TOPIC: PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE.

entries.title: Jeremiah 26:1 "In the beginning of the reign"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
26:1 "In the beginning of the reign" This CONSTRUCT (BDB 912 and BDB 575) is a technical phrase for the ascension year of a new king. The reigns of kings were figured differently from country to country. Judah counted the first partial year as one year of a king's reign, while Israel did not. See Edwin R. Thiele, The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings.

▣ "Jehoiakim" He was a son of Josiah and reigned from 609-597 B.C.. He was put on the throne by Pharaoh Necho II of Egypt as a puppet king. His original name was Eliakim (cf. 2 Kgs. 23:34; 2 Chr. 36:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED KINGDOM

entries.content:
