READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. The concept of "covenant" is discussed in the SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT. Basically in this theological context it is an agreement between two unequal partners. Both have obligations and privileges. YHWH sets the conditions and makes the initiative. In my opinion, "covenant" explains the tension-filled, paradoxical relationship between God's sovereignty and human free will.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION AND THE NEED FOR A THEOLOGIVCAL BALANCE

  2. God made a covenant with Israel to represent Him before the world (see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN). They failed to uphold their obligations and God terminated the covenant (see my exegetical notes on Jesus' Olivet Discourse and John's book of Revelation). However, He established an even more significant agreement with mankind (i.e. "new covenant," Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36).

  3. Israel's covenant was meant to help the world see YHWH's love and justice. The Old Testament, Old Covenant, laid the foundation for the understanding and implementation of the New Covenant in Christ.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SUPERIORITY OF THE NEW COVENANT OVER THE MOSAIC COVENANT

  4. Jeremiah 30-33 forms a literary unit of hope and promised restoration which scholars call the "Book of Consolation." When Jerusalem was about to fall, Jeremiah gave his most encouraging revelations! The city and temple would be destroyed but YHWH will restore them and His people!

  5. Jeremiah 31:22 refers to the northern ten tribes, while Jer. 30:23-26 refer to the southern tribes and Jer. 30:27-40 refer to the reunited, restored nation.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:2 "Write all the words I have spoken to you in a book"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:2 "Write all the words I have spoken to you in a book" Jeremiah 30:1-3 forms an introduction to the entire literary unit of Jeremiah 30-33. They deal with hope amidst judgment.

▣ "in a book" This refers to a scroll (BDB 706, #3). Obviously Jeremiah was involved in writing down YHWH's words, as well as speaking them. However, does this refer to

  1. the book of Jeremiah as we know it today
  2. the book that the king burned
  3. the book that Jeremiah dictated to Baruch after the destruction of the first scroll

These are the kinds of modern questions that cannot be answered. We do not know

  1. when the OT was compiled
  2. how/by what criteria
  3. by whom
  4. when

The main truth is "YHWH has revealed Himself!" By faith we believe the Spirit authored and preserved the essential message!

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:3 "days are coming"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:3 "days are coming" This could refer to

  1. the end of the 70 year Babylon exile (i.e. Ezra, Nehemiah, cf. Jer. 16:14; 29:10)
  2. an eschatological setting (cf. Jer. 3:16; 23:5; 31:27,31-34; Zech. 12:10-13:1)

The question arises, "How do these promises to national Israel relate to the NT?" Please look carefully at the Special Topic below.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

▣ "Israel and Judah" Israel was taken captive by Assyria in 722 B.C. Judah was taken captive by Neo-Babylon in 605, 597, 586, 582 B.C. This speaks of their reunification that is based on their repentance and God's restoration of the covenant.

The normal VERB used of repentance (BDB 996, KB 1427) is used in two senses in this verse.

  1. I will restore (i.e. turn back, Qal PERFECT with waw), Jer. 30:18
  2. I will bring them back (Hiphil PERFECT with waw), Jer. 30:10

When His people turn back to Him, He will restore them.
SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

The question that affects so much of western eschatology is, "Is the modern state of Israel fulfilled in prophecy?"

I have come to believe that it does not! If this is a new thought for you, let me recommend some video resources.

  1. Steve Gregg ‒ "The Modern State of Israel" (YouTube)
  2. my videos on the book of Revelation (YouTube, "Free Bible Commentary," "playlists," "Revelation Decoded," 17 video lessons)
  3. my exegetical commentaries on
    1. Jesus' Olivet Discourse (Matt. 24; Mark 13; Luke 17; 21)
    2. Paul's discussion on "the man of lawlessness" (2 Thess. 2)
    3. John's book of Revelation

All of these are free online at www.freebiblecommentary.org

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 30:4 Verse 4 is an introductory literary phrase.

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:5 "I have heard"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:5 "I have heard" The MT has the PLURAL. This may reflect the "Us" of Gen. 1:26; 3:22; 11:7; Isa. 6:8. This could reflect

  1. YHWH and His angelic council (cf. 1 Kgs. 22:19-23; Job 2:1-6; see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS)
  2. a rare and late Hebrew grammatical form for emphasis called "the PLURAL OF MAJESTY"
  3. a precursor of the concept of a Triune God (i.e. Trinity, see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY)

The UBS Text Project, p. 262, gives "we" (MT) a "B" rating (some doubt) and suggests it may reflect a quotation from the community. This is also the opinion of the NET Bible, p. 1375, #22.

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:6 "if a male can give birth"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:6 "if a male can give birth" Ancient women gave birth by kneeling at a birthing stone. The men of Judah were so frightened they looked as if they were giving birth (cf. Jer. 6:24; 22:23). This imagery of birthing is used in the NT to describe the birth pain of the New Age (cf. Rom. 8:22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIRTH PAINS

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:7 "Alas"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 30:7 "Alas" See note at Jer. 22:13.

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:7-8 "that day is. . . on that day"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:7-8 "that day is. . . on that day" Notice that to one group (Israel and Judah) it is a day of restoration, and to the other (i.e. Neo-Babylon) it is a day of judgment.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DAY OF THE LORD

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:8 "I will break his yoke"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:8 "I will break his yoke" This picks up on the imagery of a "yoke" (BDB 760, cf. Lev. 26:13) used by Jeremiah in Jer. 2:20 and Jeremiah 27 and 28.

▣ "bonds" This NOUN (BDB 64) is used literally and figuratively.

  1. literally
    1. Job 39:5 ‒ bonds for a wild donkey
    2. Jer. 27:2 ‒ leather straps to hold yoke in place on work animals
  2. figuratively
    1. of the rule of foreign kings ‒ Job 12:18; Ps. 2:3; 107:14; Isa. 28:22; 52:5; Jer. 30:8; Nah. 1:13
    2. of God's law ‒ Jer. 2:20; 5:5
    3. of death ‒ Ps. 116:16

Ever since Genesis 3, mankind's freedom has been affected by outside forces.

▣ "and strangers shall no longer make them their slaves" Why does this not accurately describe restored Judah's future experience (i.e. domination by Persia, Seleucids, Rome)? Either the covenant people broke the covenant again and are punished again or the reference is to an end-time period (i.e. Dan. 9:24-27).

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:9 "David"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:9 "David" This relates to the Davidic promises given in 2 Sam. 7:12-16. We know that there was not a restoration of a king immediately after the return from Babylon (Sheshbazzar and Zerubbabel were "princes of Judah"), therefore, many believe it refers to an eschatological setting (i.e. Jesus, cf. Ezek. 34:23-24; 37:24-25; Hosea 3:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT PREDICTIONS OF THE FUTURE vs. NT PREDICTIONS

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:10 "Fear not. . .do not be dismayed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:10 "Fear not. . .do not be dismayed" These are both Qal IMPERFECTS used in a JUSSIVE sense. This is YHWH's word of hope for future restoration of His people to Palestine. Their punishment is over! See D. Brent Sandy, Cracking OT Codes: a Guide to Interpreting the Literary Genres of the OT, chapter 7, and Oracles of Salvation, by William A. VanGemeren, pp. 139-155

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

▣ "O Jacob. . .O Israel" This refers to the Patriarch's descendants (Israel and Judah are reunited). Remember that Jacob's name was changed to Israel at the brook Jabbok after he wrestled with an angel (cf. Gen. 32:22-32).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

▣ "My sevant" This honorary designation (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT) is a key in understanding Israel/Judah as YHWH's method for reaching all humans (see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

In Isaiah it is clearly a reference to two things.

  1. the covenant people (i.e. Isa. 42:1-9; 49:1-6; 50:4-9)
  2. the coming Davidic Messiah (i.e. Isa. 52:13-53:12)

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

▣ "I will save you" This refers to the covenant people's restoration to the Promised Land. YHWH sent them into exile; He will restore them (i.e. Cyrus II's edict in 538 B.C.).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

▣ "shall be quiet and at ease" These two descriptions of restoration and peace are used several times in Jeremiah.

  1. quiet (BDB 1052, KB 1641), cf. Jer. 46:27; 47:6,7
  2. ease (BDB 983, KB 1374), cf. Jer. 46:27; 48:11

This had always been YHWH's will for His covenant people (as was "joy" of Jer. 30:19).

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:10-11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:10-11 Notice what YHWH promises to do for them (Jer. 30:10-11, this is repeated in Jer. 46:27-28).

  1. save them ‒ BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil PARTICIPLE
  2. they will be quiet ‒ BDB 1052, KB 1641, Qal PERFECT with waw
  3. they will be at ease ‒ BDB 983, KB 1374, Palel PERFECT with waw
  4. no one shall make them afraid ‒ BDB 353, KB 350, Hiphil PARTICIPLE
  5. I am with you to save you (first spoken to Jeremiah, cf. Jer. 1:8,19; 15:20; 20:11, but now to all of Abraham's seed)

But also notice that covenant disobedience has consequences as well as benefits (i.e. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28).

  1. I will not destroy you completely (hyperbole; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT)
  2. I will chasten you justly
  3. I will by no means leave you unpunished (this is an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and an IMPERFECT VERB from the same root [BDB 667, KB 729] which denotes intensity, cf. Jer. 25:29; 49:12)

There are consequences both spiritual and physical for disobedience, both in time and in eternity!

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:12 "Your wound is incurable"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 30:12 "Your wound is incurable" This word, "curable" (BDB 60 I) is from the same consonants as "enosh" (BDB 60), which speaks of man's frailty, weakness, and fallenness (see Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT, pp. 50-52). The paradox (see SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE [biblical paradoxes]) of this incurable wound (idolatry of which they will not repent, cf. Jer. 15:18; 30:15; Micah 1:9) is found in Jer. 30:17, where God freely heals His people. The horror of Jer. 8:18-22 is now reversed!

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:12-17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:12-17 YHWH used foreign pagan nations to discipline His people. His people surely deserved it (cf. Jer. 30:12,14e,f, 15c,d). His people were

  1. worshiping the fertility gods
  2. making foreign alliances involving other gods

However, YHWH will act on their behalf after He judges them.

  1. those who God used to judge Judah/Israel will also be judged in the same manner (note vv. 11 and 16, see note at Jer. 17:10)
  2. He will restore their health (sickness was imagery for sin, cf. Isa. 1:5-6; Ps. 103:3)
  3. He will heal their wounds
  4. by implication from Jer. 30:13 (in the MT), He will also be their advocate (BDB 192, #3, cf. Jer. 5:28; 22:16)

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEALING

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:17 "Zion"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:17 "Zion" The city of Jerusalem was built on seven hills. Mt. Zion was the site of the old Jebusite fortress. David built his palace there. It came to be an idiom for the entire city of Jerusalem (i.e. Jer. 3:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:18 "the tents of Jacob"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:18 "the tents of Jacob" This is a Hebrew idiom for family units.

▣ "shall be rebuilt on its ruin" This is the Hebrew term tel (BDB 1068, cf. Josh. 11:13), which is used by modern archaeology for the destroyed mound of an ancient city. This implies that Jerusalem (i.e. the destroyed city and the temple) will be rebuilt on the same site.

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:18-22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:18-22 In a sense this reflects the "new covenant" (Jer. 31:31-34) described in Ezek. 36:27-36. YHWH will act on behalf of His people. Notice the covenant language of Jer. 30:22. This poem is functioning as the blessing section, similar to Deuteronomy 27-28. YHWH acts for His name sake, for His purposes (see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

  1. I will restore the fortunes, Jer. 30:18b
  2. I will have compassion
    1. dwelling places, Jer. 30:18c
    2. the city, Jer. 30:18d
    3. the palace, Jer. 30:18e
  3. I will multiply them (i.e. one of the promises to Abraham, cf. Gen. 15:2-5), Jer. 30:19c
  4. I will honor them, Jer. 30:19d
  5. I will punish all their oppressors (cf. Jer. 30:12-17)
  6. I will bring their leader near (priestly language), Jer. 30:21
  7. covenant language, Jer. 30:22 (cf. Jer. 31:1)

A new day has come! The benefits of the covenant are reestablished based on YHWH's mercy, not His people's covenant obedience (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; esp. Ezek. 36:22-36).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:19 "the voice of those who make merry"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 30:19 "the voice of those who make merry" God wants His people to rejoice in creation and in Himself (cf. Jer. 7:34; 31:12-13; 33:11). This may refer to a temple choir or liturgy at a worship setting.

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:20 "their (lit. "His") congregation shall be established before Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:20 "their (lit. "His") congregation shall be established before Me" This terminology is priestly (i.e. approach YHWH in the temple). The covenant people (OT, Exod. 19:5-6; NT, 1 Pet. 2:5,9; Rev. 1:6; 20:6) were meant to be "a kingdom of priests," as the Messiah is

  1. an ideal Israelite in Isaiah 53
  2. also an ideal priest in Jer. 30:21; Ps. 110:1-3; Zech. 3:8; 4:11-14; 6:13

This section may be a "multi-fulfillment" prophecy to Zerubbabel (prince of Judah) and Joshua (descendant of the last High Priest). Jesus is both priest and king (cf. NT book of Hebrews)!

30:21
NASB  "leader"
NKJV  "governor"
NRSV, TEV, NJB  "prince"
JPSOA  "chieftain"
REB  "a ruler"
LXX  "strong ones"
Peshitta  "king"

This is the term (BDB 12, KB 13) used to describe the leader of the congregation in the new day of restoration. It is parallel to "ruler" (BDB 605).

This term appears two other times in Jeremiah denoting leaders.

  1. Jer. 14:3 - nobles
  2. Jer. 25:34-36 - shepherds/lords

The fact that this context has a priestly orientation may denote the Messianic aspect of the Messiah as

  1. Davidic ‒ Genesis 49
  2. priestly ‒ Psalm 110:1-3; Zech. 3:8; 4:11-14; 6:13

The Dead Sea Scroll community expected two Messiahs, one from the line of Judah and one from the line of Levi (i.e. Psalm 110; Zechariah 3; 4). Jesus fulfills both (cf. Heb. 1:3; 2:17; 3:1; 4:14-15; 5:5,10; 6:20; 7:26,28; 8:1,3; 9:11; 10:21). He is the High Priest and the ultimate sacrifice (i.e. book of Hebrews)!

The new "leader" (v. 21a) and "ruler" (v. 21b) shall be the faithful remnant of Israel/Judah (cf. Deut. 17:14-15). He will be of the line of David (cf. v. 9).

YHWH's promise in 2 Sam. 7; 1 Chr. 17 seemed abrogated, canceled, but not so. There is a new day and a new leader coming. For Christians this refers to Jesus of Nazareth.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS THE NAZARENE

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS IS GREATER THAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT TITLES OF THE SPECIAL COMING ONE

▣ "I will bring him near and he shall approach Me" These are priestly phrases used in the sense of approaching God at the altar. Because of the next phrase this seems to refer to the vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ (Messiah is Priest and King, cf. Ps. 110:1-3; Zech. 3:8; 4:11-14; 6:13; Heb. 1:2-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS AS HIGH PRIEST

entries.title: Jeremiah 30:23-24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
30:23-24 These verses are almost exactly like Jer. 23:19-20. Remember Jeremiah's poems were recorded and edited/compiled later. He used the same phrases in several poems.

▣ "the tempest of the Lord. . .wrath. . .fierce anger of the Lord" These anthropomorphic phrases (see SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN) are in parallel. The judgment of God has a larger redemptive purpose (cf. Jer. 30:24, see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:1 "At that time"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:1 "At that time" This refers to Jer. 30:23-24 or the words Jeremiah wrote (i.e. Jer. 30:1-24).

▣ Notice the covenant terminology (cf. Jer. 30:22) and that Judah and Israel are united again (cf. Gen. 17:7-8). This covenant terminology can also be seen in Lev. 26:12; Jer. 7:23; 11:4; 24:7; 30:22; 31:33; 32:38.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. Many of these strophes were written in different historical contexts. There is a mixing of references to Israel (the northern ten tribes) and Judah (the southern three tribes). These separate poems were combined in this chapter, which emphasizes the restoration of both.

  2. Note the references in Jeremiah 31 to:
    1. the united seed of Abraham
      1. Jer. 31:1,2 (i.e. the Exodus)
      2. Jer. 31:4,21 ("O virgin of Israel")
      3. Jer. 31:7 ("for Jacob. . .remnant of Israel")
      4. Jer. 31:27 ("the house of Israel and the house of Judah")
      5. Jer. 31:33 ("the house of Israel after those days")
    2. Israel
      1. Jer. 31: 5 ("the hills of Samaria")
      2. Jer. 31:6 ("the hills of Ephraim")
      3. Jer. 31:9 ("Ephraim is My first-born")
      4. Jer. 31:15 ("Ramah. . .Rachel")
      5. Jer. 31:18,20 ("Ephraim")
    3. Judah
      1. Jer. 31:12 ("the height of Zion")
      2. Jer. 31:14 ("the priests")
      3. Jer. 31:23 ("the land of Judah")
      4. Jer. 31:23 ("O holy hill")

  3. The unique reference to a "new covenant" is very important. It points toward a new way of being right with YHWH based on faith and repentance, not human performance to an external code (i.e. Mosaic Covenant). Obedience is an evidence of the new relationship but not the means to it (cf. Eph. 2:8-9,10). Fallen mankind was unable to please God and follow Him. Substitutionary atonement became the new mechanism for a free and full salvation (cf. Isaiah 53; Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21) which issues in Christlikeness (cf. Eph. 1:4). God now has a people who reflect His character to witness to those who do not yet know Him.

  4. For me, this concept of a "new covenant" (i.e. Jer. 31:31-34) is fully inaugurated by Jesus in the Last Supper (i.e. Matt. 26:26-29; Luke 22:20). This is also mentioned by
    1. Paul ‒ 1 Cor. 11:25; 2 Cor. 3:6
    2. author of Hebrews ‒ Heb. 8:8; 9:15

This symbolic inaugurating act fits in well with Jesus' condemnation of the Judaism of His day (cf. Matt. 21; 23; 24). I have come to believe that Jesus' Olivet Discourse (i.e. Matt. 24; Mark 13; Luke 17; 21), Paul's discussion of "the man of lawlessness" (2 Thess. 2), and John's book of Revelation all refer to the destruction of Jerusalem and the temple in A.D. 70 by the Roman Army. At this point, the covenant with national Israel was once and for all negated. The "new covenant" of grace has fully come in Jesus!

If this understanding (i.e. Partial Preterism) is new to you, please see my exegetical commentaries on these texts free online at www.freebiblecommentary.org.

Also, please look at the following Special Topics (second red box on homepage).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:2
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:2 This may be an allusion to a new "wilderness wandering period." The VERB "went to find rest" (BDB 921, KB 1188, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) communicates both a reality of peace and YHWH's presence. A different word (BDB 628) is used in Exod. 33:14 and Deut. 28:65, but reflects the same theological concept (cf. Hosea 2:14).

▣ "the sword" The Aramaic Targums have "Egypt's sword," therefore, the "sword" is imagery for death more than a reference to war. This section seems to refer to God's loving acts during the Wilderness Wandering Period.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:3 "him"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:3 "him" The MT has "me" (cf. NKJV, NJB; the UBS Text Project, p. 263, gives the MT a "B" rating). The LXX has "him" (cf NRSV). It seems to refer to the descendants of Jacob/Israel (cf. Deut. 4:37; 7:8).

▣ "I have loved you. . .I have drawn you" Both of these VERBS are Qal PERFECTS.

The word "you" must be a COLLECTIVE FEMININE SINGULAR (twice) because of

  1. the context of Jer. 31:4 as national renewal and restoration
  2. the continuation of the COLLECTIVE FEMININE SINGULAR

▣ "everlasting love. . .lovingkindness" These are covenant terms and promises. God wants His exiled people to know He has not forsaken them.

  1. everlasting love ‒ BDB 12 CONSTRUCT BDB 761, see SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)
  2. lovingkindness ‒ BDB 338, see SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

There is a paradoxical relationship between YHWH's justice and mercy. Both are true and appropriate. Some texts that illustrate this tension in the character of God are:

  1. Ps. 30:5; 103:8-14
  2. Isa. 54:7-8; 57:16-19

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE (biblical paradoxes)

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGE, JUDGMENT, AND JUSTICE

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:4c,d
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:4c,d This imagery of "tambourines" and "dances" seems to relate to the victory dance at the Red Sea by Miriam and the young Israeli women in Exod. 15. Israel's deliverance from Assyrian and Neo-Babylonian exile by Cyrus II in 538 B.C. will be a time of rejoicing again.

The exile canceled the normal activities of daily life in Palestine (cf. Jer. 7:34; 25:10).

▣ "O virgin of Israel" This phrase is used several times in the OT (cf. Jer. 31:21; 14:17; 18:13; 46:11; Amos 5:2; see full note at Jer. 46:11). God's people have committed spiritual adultery (cf. Jer. 31:22b). God forgives and restores them.

The title "Israel" is used in three ways in this chapter.

  1. as a reference to Jacob
  2. as the whole nation of his descendants
  3. as the northern ten tribes also called Ephraim or Samaria

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:5 "hills of Samaria"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:5 "hills of Samaria" This was the site of the capital of the northern kingdom built by Omri. Jeremiah 31:5-6 speak to the area of the northern tribes, Israel.

▣ "enjoy" This VERB literally means "profane" (BDB 320, KB 319, Piel PERFECT with waw). It is a reference to the OT custom of offering first fruits to God (cf. Lev. 19:23-25; Deut. 20:6). Here "profane" means "to use for normal consumption." The first four years' fruit and then the first ripened fruit of the following years were symbolically given to YHWH in order to show His ownership of all the crops. However, here the phrase is imagery for a long extended period of peace and abundance (cf. Deuteronomy 28).

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:6 "watchmen"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:6 "watchmen" These sentinels may have been stationed

  1. on the roads leading to a walled city
  2. on the highest hills around a walled city
  3. on the wall at different points around the city's walls

They were both messengers

  1. of warning (i.e. invasion, i.e. Jer. 6:17; Ezek. 33:2-6)
  2. good news (i.e. military victories, cf. Isa. 40:9; 52:7-10)
  3. of societal gatherings
    1. worship
    2. civil announcements
  4. YHWH's prophets as watchmen over the covenant people, Ezek. 3:17-21; 33:7-9; Isa. 62:6 (the negative relating to false prophets is Isa. 56:10)

▣ "Ephraim" This is a reference to the northern ten tribes who had by Jeremiah's day already been exiled by Assyria (722 B.C.). It went by several names after the united monarchy under Saul, David, and Solomon split in 922 B.C.

  1. Israel (a collective term)
  2. Samaria (their capital)
  3. Ephraim (their largest tribe)

To keep Ephraim from returning to Zion to worship YHWH, Jeroboam I set up "golden calves" at the cities of Bethel and Dan (i.e. alternate sites of temples to YHWH). They had, in reality, been turned into sites of Ba'al worship, but now they no longer exist!

Now, Ephraim watchmen will call for the people to make the three annual pilgrimages to Jerusalem and the only official temple of YHWH. All the nations will come, too (cf. Isa. 2:2-4).

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:7 Jer. 31:7-9 are another poem/strophe. There is a series of IMPERATIVES expressing YHWH's will for the reunified covenant people (Israel/Jacob).

  1. sing aloud ‒ BDB 943, KB 1247, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. shout ‒ BDB 843, KB 1007, Qal IMPERATIVE
  3. proclaim ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  4. give praise ‒ BDB 237, KB 248, Piel IMPERATIVE
  5. say ‒ BDB 55, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE
  6. save ‒ BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil imperative (this is a prayer to YHWH expressed loudly. The LXX changes the IMPERATIVE to a DECLARATIVE, which makes it the OBJECT of the other IMPERATIVES)
▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB, Peshitta  "chief of the nations"
TEV  "the greatest of the nations"
JPSOA  "at the crossroads of the
 nations"
REB  "lead the nations"
LXX  "the head of the nations"

This imagery goes back to

  1. Exod. 4:22; Ps. 2:7, where Israel is YHWH's firstborn
  2. Ps. 18:43, where David is called "the head of the nations"
  3. Both of the above are combined in Ps. 89:27.
  4. In Deut. 28:13 Israel is called "the head and not the tail," which is the same imagery (cf. Isa. 61:9)

This imagery shows the central place of Abraham's descendants (cf. Deut. 26:19) in YHWH's plan for all the earth.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN)

▣
NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "O Lord, save Your people"
NRSV, JPSOA  "Save, O Lord, Your people"
TEV, REB, LXX  "the Lord has saved his people"
NJB  "Yahweh has saved his people"

The MT is reflected in the NASB. The issue is the form of the VERB; is it an IMPERATIVE or a PERFECT? The UBS Text Project, p. 263, gives the MT Hiphil IMPERATIVE a "C" rating (considerable doubt). The LXX fits the context best.

The JPSOA footnote mentions the possible emendatiom found in the LXX.

▣ "the remnant of Israel" In this context it is parallel to "those who survived the sword" of Jer. 31:2b. Jeremiah uses this term (BDB 984) twenty-three times.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, THREE SENSES

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:8 "I am bringing them from the north country"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:8 "I am bringing them from the north country" This reference is to the Assyrian exile of the northern kingdom in 722 B.C. The only land route into Palestine from Mesopotamia was from the north because the Arabian Desert was to the east. It became a symbol of invasion, but here is a symbol of hope and restoration.

▣ Notice how the returnees are characterized.

  1. from the remote parts of the earth (cf. Isa. 11:11; 43:6)
  2. the blind (cf. Isa. 42:16)
  3. the lame (cf. Micah 4:6; Zeph. 3:19)
  4. women with children
  5. pregnant women

This is in contrast to how they were taken into captivity. Only the strong, middle-aged were taken. The young, the old, the sick, the weak, and the leaders were all killed!

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:9 "with weeping. . . by supplication"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:9 "with weeping. . . by supplication" Verse 9 refers to the repentant nature of the returners (cf. Jer. 31:7e,9b; Deut. 30:6). This same form appears in Zech. 12:10 for Israel's repentance and faith in the Messiah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

▣
NASB, NKJV  "supplication"
NRSV, LXX, Targums, Vulgate  "consolation"
JPSOA  "compassion"
REB  "I will comfort them"
Peshitta  "shall return with fervent prayer"

The MT has "supplications" (BDB 337, cf. Jer. 3:21; Zech. 12:10), but the Targums and LXX have "consolation" (BDB 636).

  1. supplications ‒ ובתחנונים
  2. consolations ‒ ובתנחומים

The UBS Text Project, p. 264, gives the MT a "B" rating. In context, verse 9 refers to a repentant, prayerful people brought back to the Promised Land by YHWH.

▣ "walk by streams of water" This imagery describes the new age (cf. Deut. 28:1-14) of abundance. The desert is transformed into a "watered garden" (cf. Jer. 31:12; Isa. 58:11). This is imagery from Isaiah (cf. Jer. 35:7-8; 41:17-20; 43:19-20; 49:10-11).

The way home (i.e. highway) will be easy and "without want!" YHWH is bringing His people back to the Promised Land. A new exodus and wilderness wandering period has begun.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WATERS

▣ "on a straight path in which they shall not stumble" The way home will be smooth and easy. YHWH will prepare the road (physically and spiritually). This is the "highway of holiness" described by Isaiah (cf. Jer. 35:8; 40:3; 49:11; 57:14; 62:10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH. . .THE WAY

▣ "I am a Father to Israel" God is spoken of as "Father" to the descendants of Abraham. God is spoken of as a husband to them in Jer. 11:15 (cf. Hosea 1-3). The Bible uses the most intimate family terms to describe the relationship between YHWH and His people (cf. Hosea 1-3,11).

It is difficult in this chapter (which seems to combine poems from several periods of Jeremiah's ministry) to know when the terminology refers to the Northern Ten Tribes (i.e. "Ephraim is My firstborn"; also note v. 20) or to all Israelites (see Contextual Insights, B).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHERHOOD OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRSTBORN

▣ This strophe is describing the joyful return of the exiles. The theology is twofold.

  1. YHWH exiled them for their sin. He will restore them in their repentance and faith (Jer. 31:9).
  2. YHWH is sovereign over all nations (cf. Jer. 31:10; LXX of Deut. 32:8), not the non-existent idols of the pagan nations. He alone controls time/history.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:10 There are three IMPERATIVES.

  1. hear ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE
  2. declare ‒ BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  3. say ‒ BDB 55, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE

The nations must hear YHWH's message of restoration. They must know Him: His love, power, provision! YHWH works with the descendants of Abraham in special ways to inform and attract the descendants of Adam! This is surely the implication of monotheism.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

▣ "shepherd keeps his flock" This is an OT title for "God" (cf. Psalm 23; Isa. 40:11; Ezek. 34:11-14,31). This title is used of Jesus in John 10 (cf. Ezek. 34:23; Micah 5:4). Attributing OT titles for YHWH to Jesus is a common way for NT writers to confirm the Deity of Christ.

  1. OT titles of YHWH applied to Jesus
  2. OT actions of YHWH applied to Jesus
  3. grammatical constructions where God and Jesus are the dual OBJECTS of VERBS or PREPOSITIONS
  4. clear statements (cf. John 1:1; 5:18; 8:58; 10:30; 14:9; 17:11; Rom. 9:5; Heb. 1:8; 2 Pet. 1:1)

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT TITLES OF THE SPECIAL COMING ONE

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:11 "ransomed. . .redeemed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:11 "ransomed. . .redeemed" These two terms are parallel. Both are imagery of God's love for fallen humanity and HIs willingness to save them, both physically and spiritually.

  1. ransom ‒ BDB 804, KB 911, Qal PERFECT, Jer. 15:21; Hosea 13:14; Micah 6:4; Zech. 10:8
  2. redeem ‒ BDB 145, KB 169, Qal PERFECT, so common in Leviticus, Ruth, Isaiah. Title for YHWH in Isa. 41:14; 43:14, but used only twice in Jeremiah, here and 50:34 (also title for YHWH).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:12 "on the height of Zion"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:12 "on the height of Zion" Zion is one of seven hills on which Jerusalem was built. Mt. Zion was the site of the Jebusite fortress captured by David. He built his palace on this hill.

However, in this context, Zion stands for Jerusalem. The word "height" would refer to Mt. Moriah, the site of the rebuilt temple. The place "God chose His name to dwell" (recurrent phrase in Deuteronomy).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION

▣
NASB, NRSV, REB, JPSOA  "be radiant"
NKJV  "streaming"
TEV  "be delighted"
NJB  "thronging"
LXX  "shall come"
Peshitta  "shall be happy"

The MT has the VERB "stream" (BDB 625 I, KB 676, Qal PERFECT with waw). This same VERB is used in the wonderful universal restoration of all nations "streaming" to YHWH in Isa. 2:2 and Micah 4:1; also note the usage in Jer. 51:44.

The NASB translation comes from the same root (BDB 626 II) which means "to shine" or "to beam" (cf. Ps. 34:5; Isa. 60:5). It is a much rarer VERB than the first option. BDB does not even list it as an option in Jer. 31:12!

▣ "they shall never languish again" The covenant blessing of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28 are present and secure (cf. Jer. 31:5). In this statement is the promise of no more exiles (cf. Isa. 35:10; 60:20; 65:17-25; 1 Pet. 1:3-5)! The new day has come!

  1. Was this fulfilled in the post-exilic return?
  2. Was that restoration still conditional?
  3. Has the new day of a new heart, mind, and spirit arrived?

I think this imagery points toward the gospel (initiated covenant) and eschatological fulfillment (consummated covenant).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:13-14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:13-14 Notice the people who were rejoicing.

  1. young women (lit. "virgin")
  2. young men
  3. old men
  4. the priests
  5. "my people" (collective term encompassing all groups)

Jeremiah 31:12 is related to "the nations" which will be included, but Jer. 31:13 relates to the returning exiles. This inclusiveness reminds one of Joel 2:28-29, quoted in the first Apostolic sermon in Acts 2.

31:13
NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "together"
NRSV  "shall be merry"
TEV, REB, LXX  "will rejoice"
NJB  "alike"

The MT is reflected in the NASB. The different options are related to vowels, not consonants. The UBS Text Project, p. 264, gives the MT a "B" rating. The LXX tries to make the line of poetry a better literary parallel.

  1. line 1 ‒ "rejoice" (BDB 970)
  2. line 2 ‒ "merry" (BDB 403)
  3. line 3 ‒ "joy" (BDB 965)
  4. line 4 ‒ "gladness/joy" (BDB 970)

The normal life of the society is restored.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:14 "I will fill the soul of the priests with abundance"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:14 "I will fill the soul of the priests with abundance" This refers to the re-instigation of the sacrificial system. Jeremiah was not opposed to the cultus but wanted faith and ritual (cf. Lev. 7:32-36), not ritual alone.

For "soul" (nephesh) see notes at Gen. 35:18; Lev. 17:11; and Ezek. 18:4 online.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:15 "Ramah"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:15 "Ramah" The Hebrew word "height" (BDB 928) is possibly not a reference to a place name. The rabbis see this as a reference to God's hearing in heaven. However, the MT is not pointed for a place name.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENSD AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

▣ "Rachel" This was Jacob's favorite wife and the mother of Joseph (and, therefore, the grandmother of Ephraim and Manasseh) and Benjamin (cf. Gen. 35:16-18). The rabbis say she was buried by the very road on which the northern tribes were taken into exile by Assyria in 722 B.C. This verse is quoted in Matt. 2:18 concerning Herod's killing of the children of Bethlehem (in order to kill the newborn "King of the Jews" who the Wise Men sought).

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:15-20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 31:15-20 The strophe is addressed to the northern ten tribes. They, too, will participate in YHWH's restoration and new day! The split of the United Monarchy in 922 B.C. was a sad and destructive event, both physically and spiritually. All of the prophets condemned the northern kings. Restoration was the only option.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:16
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 31:16 Rachel should not weep because the exiles from Israel will be brought back to Palestine.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 31:17 This "hope for the future" may refer back to Jer. 29:11.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:18 "I have surely heard"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:18 "I have surely heard" This is an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT VERB from the same root (BDB 1033, KB 1570) for emphasis. God does hear when we pray (cf. Exod. 3:7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

▣ "Like an untrained calf" This is terminology from Jer. 2:20; 5:5; Hosea 4:16 (also note the similar animal imagery in Isa. 1:3).

▣ "Bring me back that I may be restored" This is a Hiphil IMPERATIVE (i.e. a prayer to YHWH). The rabbis say that such a radical repentance is involved that only God can give it (i.e. the new covenant of Jer. 31:31-34, described in Ezek. 36:22-36). The divine initiation is stressed in Jer. 31:19. This reflects Jeremiah's prayer of Jer. 17:12-18.

For the theological interplay between God's gift and human responsibility, see my exegetical note at Acts 5:31.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:19 "I smote on my thigh"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 31:19 "I smote on my thigh" This is a cultural idiom of grief or shame (cf. Ezek. 21:12). The thigh was the largest muscle in the body.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:20
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:20 This verse begins with a question(s). Some translations have

  1. no question mark (possibly assuming the question[s] expect a "yes," LXX, Peshitta, JPSOA, TEV)
  2. one question (NJB, REB, NIV)
  3. two questions (NASB, NKJV, NRSV)

Verse 20 describes YHWH as a loving parent who disciplines His son but still loves him. This may reflect 2 Sam. 7:14-15. The discipline is for the purpose of restoration (cf. Hosea 11:8-9; 14:4-7).

The UBS Handbook for Translators on Jeremiah (p. 641) makes the interesting comment, "This verse is God's reply to Israel's statement of repentance, just as Jer. 4:1-2 is God's response to Israel's repentance in Jer. 3:22-25."

▣ "dear son. . .delightful child" These statements are parallel. The words (BDB 430 and 1044) express YHWH's love in parental terms. It reminds me of Exod. 19:5-6. There was so much potential in the covenant people, but what a disaster their idolatry caused (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36).

▣ "I have spoken against him" The Hebrew can be interpreted as "of him" (Peshitta, NJB), which fits the context better. JPSOA has "whenever I have turned against him."

▣ "remember. . .have mercy" Both of these are the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT VERB of the same root for the intensity of YHWH's love and forgiveness!

  1. I certainly still remember him ‒ BDB 269, KB 269
  2. I will surely have mercy on him ‒ BDB 933, KB 1216

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:21 "roadmarks. . .guideposts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:21 "roadmarks. . .guideposts" These two terms are rare.

  1. roadmarks ‒ BDB 846, usually denotes a grave marker (cf. 2 Kgs. 23:17; Ezek. 39:15)
  2. guideposts ‒ BDB 1071, found only here in the OT

The third line of the verse shows the context as a "highway" (BDB 700, only here in Jeremiah) so the first two parallel lines must fit this imagery. The exiles are to set their minds to the road that took them into exile (i.e. idolatry), but now to the road (i.e. repentance, faith) that will bring them home.

Jeremiah continued to tell Judah that she would go into exile for 70 years. Jerusalem and the temple would be destroyed. Here he seems to say to them, mark your path/road as you travel into exile because one day you will return and these markers you set up in grief will become markers of joy on the way home to Palestine!

31:22
NASB  "go here and there"
NKJV  "gad about"
NRSV, REB, JPSOA  "waver"
NJB, TEV, Peshitta  "hesitate"
NET  "vacillate"
Arabic root (KB)  "to be foolish"

This root (BDB 330, KB 330) appears only twice in the OT.

  1. Song of Songs 5:6 in the Qal stem to denote that the beloved has "turned away"
  2. here, in the Hithpael stem and seems to denote a hesitation for faithless Israel/Judah to accept YHWH's forgiveness and provision to return to Palestine

▣ "For the Lord has created a new thing" The mention of "new" (BDB 294) brings the imagery from Isaiah of the Messianic age (i.e. "new covenant," 31:31-34). See SPECIAL TOPIC: OLD THINGS. . .NEW THINGS and SPECIAL TOPIC: THE MESSIANIC ERA

  1. new things, Isa. 42:9; 48:6
  2. new song, Isa. 42:10 (Rev. 5:9; 14:3)
  3. something new, Isa. 43:19 (Rev. 3:12)
  4. new name, Isa. 62:2 (cf. Isa. 56:5)
  5. new heavens and new earth, Isa. 65:17; 66:22 (cf. 2 Pet. 3:13)

Also note Ezek. 11:19; 18:31; 36:26 (36:22-36 is a description of the new covenant age).

Note that the same VERB (BDB 135, KB 153) used in Gen. 1:1 is used again of YHWH's creative activity in restoring His people (and through them His eternal redemptive plan). Creation was to provide a place for fellowship between God and all humanity (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8), so too, the restoration of Israel. The Messiah will come from her (i.e. Jer. 30:21) and for all humanity!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV  "A woman will encompass a man"
TEV, NET  "a woman protecting a man"
NJB  "the woman sets out to find her husband
  again"
JPSOA  "a woman courts a man"
REB  "a woman will play a man's part"
LXX  "people will go about in safety"
Peshitta  "a woman shall love her husband"

Just a couple of opening lexical items on this difficult verse.

  1. Notice it is addressed to faithless Judah.
  2. YHWH says, "created a new thing in the earth" (i.e. not a normal or expected thing).
  3. The Hebrew root translated "woman" (BDB 666, KB 719) can refer to
    1. a female child
    2. a female animal
    3. a female sexual partner
  4. The Hebrew root translated "man" (BDB 149, KB 175) is from the root "strong" or "mighty." This root is not used by Isaiah or Ezekiel.
  5. The Hebrew VERBAL root translated "encompass" (BDB 685, KB 738, Poel IMPERFECT) is used of YHWH protecting newly formed Israel in Deut. 32:10; in Ps. 32:10, it is YHWH's hesed that surrounds the faithful follower.
     So, this unusual phrase may refer to faith in YHWH (i.e the strong man), not for protection but for devotion.

There are many theories (notice no parallel passages) about the meaning of this phrase.

  1. reference to Israel's renewed love for YHWH, her husband (BDB 686, Poel #1, cf. NJB; see note in 1st paragraph above).
  2. women will stand guard on the way home
  3. the virgin birth (i.e. Jerome, Calvin)
  4. the rabbis say women take on the male characteristics of firmness or strength
  5. cultural proverb whose meaning is lost
  6. the LXX has "in which people will go about in safety" (i.e. different Hebrew text)
  7. if the thrust is "role reversal" (i.e. Jer. 30:6) then I wonder how much it may relate to the subservience of women in Genesis 3, restored to the mutuality of Genesis 1-2? There are many Pentateuch allusions in this chapter.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:21-22
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:21-22 There is a series of IMPERATIVES given to the exiles related to their return trip to Palestine.

  1. set up for yourselves roadmarks ‒ BDB 662, KB 714, Hiphil IMPERATIVE
  2. place for yourselves guideposts ‒ BDB 962, KB 1321, Qal IMPERATIVE
  3. direct your mind to the highway ‒ BDB 1011, KB 1483, Qal IMPERATIVE
  4. return ‒ BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal IMPERATIVE (twice). This same word is often used of "repentance," see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

Notice how the imagery changes.

  1. in Jer. 31:20 Ephraim is a "son," a "child" (MASCULINE, cf. Jer. 31:9)
  2. in Jer. 31:21 she is a "virgin of Israel" (FEMININE, cf. Jer. 31:4; see full note at Jer. 46:11)

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:23-26
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:23-26 These verses are about the restoration of Judah.

  1. her cities, Jer. 31:24)
  2. her capital
  3. the temple (i.e. "holy hill" or "holy mountain," so often in the Psalms and Isaiah)

Jeremiah 31:24 is difficult in the MT, "and they shall wander," but in the LXX, "and he shall be raised up with a flock." The point from the context is that "farmers" and "herdsmen" will dwell together. This may be a veiled allusion to the problem between Cain and Abel (i.e. Genesis 4), but in the new day there will be no tensions related to vocations.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:24
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:24 There seem to be three different types of restored citizens mentioned.

  1. those who dwell in cities
  2. those who aprovide food for #1
  3. those who provide dairy products, meat, and sacrificial animals for #1 (this requires a textual emendation)

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:26 "I awoke and looked, and my sleep was pleasant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:26 "I awoke and looked, and my sleep was pleasant" Jeremiah 31:26 is also difficult. It seems out of place or at least ambiguous as to whom it relates.

  1. northern ten tribes
  2. all descendants of Abraham (TEV)
  3. the prophet receiving this revelation ("I," cf. Jer. 30:1)
    SPECIAL TOPIC: MASORETIC TEXT
    SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

This is possibly a reference to

  1. the prophet's current dream of restoration (Jewish Study Bible marginal note suggests he saw in a dream of the future, much like Abraham in Gen. 15:12-21, p. 990)
  2. a statement of the inhabitants relating to the restored Judah (TEV)

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:27
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:27 The verse is using "abundance imagery" from Lev. 26:1-13 and Deut. 28:1-14; 30:1-10. The fruitfulness of humans, animals, and crops will be restored (cf. Ezek. 36:9,11; Hosea 2:23).

Notice that Jer. 31:27,31, and 38 all begin with the same introductory formula, "Behold, days are coming," which denotes the new Messianic age, the age of the Spirit, the age of the "New" (see note at Jer. 31:31).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:28
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 31:28 This is a series of INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS that describe YHWH's activities of judgment and restoration. This is the prophetic mandate that was given to Jeremiah in Jer. 1:10. The first VERB "watched over them" (BDB 1052, KB 1638; Qal PERFECT also appears in Qal IMPERFECT in v. 28) also occurs in Jer. 1:12.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:28 "from the tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:28 "from the tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate" These were both located on Jerusalem's north wall (cf. Neh. 3:1; 12:39; 2 Kgs. 14:13; 2 Chr. 25:23; 26:9). This may be the very area of Jerusalem's wall that was breached by the Neo-Babylonian army.

▣ "the hill Gareb; then it will turn to Goah" BDB speculates that the first one was located close to Jerusalem towards the southwest (BDB 173, KB 199).

For the second name, BDB says it must have been close to Jerusalem, but where is unknown (BDB 171, KB 199).

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:29 "The fathers have eaten sour grapes"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:29 "The fathers have eaten sour grapes" This was a proverb (cf. Ezek. 18:2; Lam. 5:7) that tried to blame the parent's actions for God's current judgments. Ezekiel 18 was written to help explain Deut. 5:9. Yes, families are affected by sin of parents and ancestors, but God's forgiveness relates to the individual's faith and obedience (cf. Jer. 31:30b; Deut. 7:9; 24:16). This is where Hebrew corporality and individualism meet.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL FAITH IS CORPORATE

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:31 "Behold, days are coming"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:31 "Behold, days are coming" Notice that the same introductory phrase begins three poems in this chapter (Jer. 31:27,31,38),

The question has always been, "When does this new day start?"

  1. the return under Cyrus II in 538 B.C. (i.e. Ezra, Nehemiah, Sheshbazzar, Zerubbabel, Joshua)
  2. the life of Christ (cf. Heb. 8:8-12 which quotes this text)
  3. the Second Coming of Christ

The post-exilic period embodied the hope of a new day of faith, but it did not materialize (cf. Malachi). The new internal nature of the covenant based on God's grace and performance, not mankind's, even covenant mankind (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36), was not manifested until the ministry and death/resurrection of Jesus of Nazareth (cf. Matt. 26:26-29; Luke 22:20; 1 Cor. 11:25; 2 Cor. 3:6; Heb. 8:8; 9:15). The new covenant has been inaugurated with Jesus' first coming and will be consummated at His second coming!

▣ "I will make a new covenant" This is the only mention in the OT of a "new covenant," although Isa. 55:3 mentions "an everlasting covenant" (it is possible that Duet. 18:15-19 implies the need of a new covenant with the coming of the new prophet). This would have been very shocking to Judeans. They thought God's covenant with Moses was unconditional and eternal (cf. Gen. 17:7,13,19; Lev. 16:34; 24:8; Num. 25:13; 1 Chr. 16:17; Ps. 105:10). Isaiah 24:5 says it was broken! Jesus calls His death "the new covenant in My blood," which links to Moses' words in Exod. 24:8 (cf. Matt. 26:26-29; Luke 22:23-26; 1 Cor. 11:23-26; 2 Cor. 3:6; Heb. 9:15).

The Jewish Study Bible, p. 991, has the following quote about "the new covenant."

"The new covenant has been interpreted by Christians as a prophecy of the new covenant through Jesus (New Testament means new covenant), but here it refers to the restoration of Israel after the Babylonian exile and the reconstruction of the Temple. According to this passage, it is not the content of the new covenant which will be different, but how it is learned."

For me, the NT has priority over even OT context (i.e. Matt. 5:17-19, 21-48). Jesus is the full and final revelation. We must view and interpret the OT through the eyes of the NT.

  1. Luke 22:20 ‒ Jesus used the term "new covenant" at the Last Supper to describe Himself and His work.
  2. 1 Corinthians 11:25; 2 Cor. 3:6 ‒ Paul picks up on the same vocabulary and uses it for the Last Supper.
  3. 1 Thessalonians 4:9; 1 John 2:27 use the same OT imagery to show the difference between the letter of the Law and the new way in the Spirit.
  4. Hebrews 8:8-12; 9:15; 10:16-17 ‒ the author of Hebrews reveals the relationship between the covenant of Moses and the new covenant in Jesus. This book is the comparison of the OT vs. NT.

Clearly, my NT bias is showing! I will live and die and stand before God with the priority of NT revelation. Jesus is the perfect and ultimate revelation of the one true God, YHWH (i.e. Matt. 5:17-48).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEWS OF THE MOSAIC LAW

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SUPERIORITY OF THE NEW COVENANT OVER THE MOSAIC COVENANT

▣ "house of Israel. . .house of Judah" The New Covenant would restore unity to the divided kingdom (cf. Jer. 31:1-3,27,33; 32:38-40). It will go far beyond that and restore the unity between God and humanity so obvious in Genesis 1-2 (cf. Rom. 2:28-29; 3:21-31; 9:24-33; 11:11-24,25; 15:7-16; Galatians 2; 3; Eph. 2:11-3:13).

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:32 "not like the covenant which I made with their fathers"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:32 "not like the covenant which I made with their fathers" There is both a continuity and discontinuity between the old covenant and the new covenant. First, it is important to list the different significant covenants.

  1. Abraham
  2. Moses
  3. David
  4. new covenant (i.e. Jesus, cf. Hebrews)

The first and third are still in effect, as far as YHWH's eternal redemptive plan. The fourth is the fulfillment of that plan. Here are some of the similarities.

  1. God initiates it and sets its parameters
  2. humans must respond in repentance, faith, obedience, and perseverance
  3. the Spirit draws humans to respond appropriately (i.e. John 6:44,65)

The big difference is that the performance model is replaced by a grace model. God still wants a people to reflect and reveal His character to a lost world. However, because of the Fall, His covenant people, with all their privileges (cf. Rom. 9:4-5), could not keep the Mosaic covenant (cf. Gal. 3). Therefore, God initiates a covenant of grace that uses the Messiah's obedience and sacrifice (cf. Isaiah 53; Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21) to fulfill the old covenant and begin a new age characterized by a new heart, a new mind, a new spirit (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36). Internal motivation will replace external laws. But remember the goal is still a Christlike people (i.e. covenant language, cf. Jer. 31:33d; 24:7)! The eternal redemptive purpose continues.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "I took them by the hand" The emphasis here is on God's parenthood (cf. Hosea 11:1-4,8-9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD

▣ "My covenant which they broke" This is a summary of the history of the Jewish nation (cf. Jer. 25:4; 33:8; Galatians 3; the book of Hebrews).

▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV  "I was a husband to them"
NJB  "I was their Master"
REB  "I was patient with them"
JPSOA  "though I espoused them"
LXX  "I am unconcerned for them"
Peshitta  "I also despised them"

The translations show a shocking diversity which seems to be related to the term "husband" (BDB 127), which literally means "Lord," "master," or "owner." This was also the title for the Caananite fertility god, Ba'al. YHWH is called "husband" in Jer. 3:14.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:33 "the house of Israel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:33 "the house of Israel" Notice that in Jer. 31:27,31 "Israel" refers to the northern ten tribes after the split of the United Monarchy in 922 B.C. The northern ten tribes, led by Jeroboam I, were called

  1. Israel (collective term)
  2. Samaria (the capital)
  3. Ephraim (the largest tribe)

However, here in Jer. 31:33 it must refer to its original meaning of the descendants of Jacob, whose name was changed to Israel. See full note in Contextual Insights, B.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

▣ "I will put My law within them" This is analogous to

  1. the phrase "circumcise your heart" of Deut. 30:6
  2. David's repentant prayer for forgiveness and restoration in Ps. 51:10
  3. It is parallel to the new heart, new mind, and new spirit of Ezek. 36:22-36.
  4. From the NT this refers to the indwelling Holy Spirit (cf. John 14:16-17; 16:13-15; Rom. 8:8-9; Gal. 4:6).

▣ "on their heart" This refers to the entire person (cf. Deut. 6:6; 11:18; 30:14). See SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART.

The Fall of Genesis 3 affected human's spiritual orientation and worldview (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALLOF MANKIND). They came to focus on "self," not God. This fallenness was the reason that Abraham's descendants could not keep/perform the Mosaic covenant (cf. Deut. 31:29; Josh. 24:19). Therefore, YHWH must give them a new heart (cf. Jer. 24:7 and "the circumcised heart," cf. Deut. 30:6). Then the Scriptures of Deut. 6:6; 30:11,14 can be fulfilled. The clearest description of this new orientation and spiritual worldview is

  1. OT ‒ Ezek. 36:22-36
  2. NT ‒ Sermon on the Mount, Matthew 5-7
  3. Galatians 3
  4. also note the book of Hebrews

▣ "I will write it" As YHWH wrote the Ten Commandments before Moses on Mt. Sinai ("the finger of God," cf. Exod. 31:18; 32:15-16; 34:1,28), He now writes on the human heart by His Spirit. The new covenant is a new internal code from a restored image of God! This faith relationship has always been the plan of God (cf. Lev. 26:41; Deut. 10:16; 30:6; Jer. 4:4; 9:25-26).
SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS (OT)

One of my favorite OT commentators is John H. Walton. He tries to iinterpret OT texts in light of the ANE culture and lexical roots (as does R. K. Harrison). In his book, ANE Thought and the OT, pp. 257-258, he documents the linguistic connections between Jeremiah's words on this context and divination. Humans are seeking information about God and His will for our lives. There is an inappropriate way and an appropriate way.

John H. Walton has several other books in his The Lost World of. . . series. They have all been very stimulating and thought provoking for me. The key to my hermeneutical method is

  1. the intent of the original inspired author as expressed in
    1. his historical setting
    2. his literary structure
    3. his lexical options
    4. his other writings
  2. what would the original aludience have understood

"Bible Interpretation Seminar"

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:34 "for they will all know Me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:34 "for they will all know Me" Notice the play between the IMPERATIVE (BDB 353, KB 390, Qal IMPERATIVE, which relates to the performance model, i.e. the Old Testament) and the IMPERFECT, which relates to the new age, new mind, new heart, new spirit (i.e. new covenant, i.e. Ezek. 36:22-36).

There will be an intimate, personal relationship between YHWH and all of His people. This intimacy is illustrated by the Hebrew concept of "know" in Gen. 4:1 and Jer. 1:5; 9:24.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

▣ "from the least of them to the greatest of them" This inclusive, "no respecter of persons" language is parallel to Joel 2:28-29 (quoted in Acts 2:17-18). It is used in a negative sense in Jer. 6:13; 8:10.

▣ "I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more" When God forgives, God forgets (cf. Isa. 1:18; 38:17; 43:25; 44:22; Ezek. 18:22; 33:16; Ps. 103:10-14; Micah 7:19)! What a great truth! Many believers mentally accept God's forgiveness but do not live in the reality of His forgiveness. Satan will throw our past sin up before us, but we must remember these wonderful texts! Texts have priority over feelings!

SPECIAL TOPIC: FORGIVENESS IN THE OT

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:35-37
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:35-37 YHWH's new covenant is as stable and permanent as the fixed orders (BDB 349) and cycles of creation. Verse 37 expresses the positive truth in a negative statement (i.e. conditional expression which cannot be fulfilled).

31:35
NASB, NRSV  "the fixed order"
NKJV  "the ordinances"
NJB  "who regulates"
REB, LXX  "gave"
JPSOA  "the Laws"
Peshitta  "ordained"

The MT has the FEMININE NOUN, חקת, which could come from

  1. decree ‒ חקק, BDB 349
  2. something prescribed or enacted ‒ חקה, BDB 349

The same word, referring to the regular order of nature, occurs in v. 36. The UBS Text Project, p. 266, gives the MT a "B" rating.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:36
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:36 These OT promises to Abraham's covenant descendants are so clear and strong. The question comes if this divine statement is so sure, what about

  1. Antiochus Epiphanes IV, the Seleucid ruler who defiled the temple in the interbiblical period
  2. the Roman army's destruction of Jerusalem and the temple in A.D. 70
  3. Daniel 9:24-27 prediction of future problems for restored Jerusalem

There seem to be two possible answers.

  1. this text, like all OT national promises, is conditional (i.e. "if. . .then. . .")
    SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT
  2. this text is an eschatological text that refers to a time in a distant age

I am always cognizant that neither Jesus nor any NT writer reaffirms an OT promise to national Israel. The NT is not about Israel; it is about Jesus and a new people of God (i.e. those who have faith in Jesus).

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:38-40
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:38-40 This paragraph is declaring the full restoration of Jerusalem. Not only will the city be rebuilt but expanded. This new city (cf. Isa. 1:26; 45:13; 60:14) will never be

  1. plucked up ‒ BDB 684, KB 737, Niphal IMPERFECT
  2. overthrown ‒ BDB 248, KB 256, Niphal IMPERFECT

Since the rebuilt Jerusalem of the post-exilic period was destroyed by the Roman general Titus in A.D. 70, this must be interpreted as

  1. the promises of God are conditional (see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT)
  2. it points toward the "new Jerusalem" (i.e. heaven) of Rev. 21:1-21 (which also uses "new" imagery)

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:40 "valley of dead bodies and of the ashes"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:40 "valley of dead bodies and of the ashes" This phrase refers to the "Valley of the Sons of Hinnom" (cf. Jer. 7:31; 19:2,6), which became the Hebrew contraction for Gehenna.

This phrase is missing in the LXX. There are some scholars who do not accept this identification because the word used for "valley" (BDB 770) is different in Jer. 7:31-32 and 19:2,6 (BDB 161). However, the dead bones and ashes seem to demand it.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DEAD, WHERE ARE THEY? (Sheol/Hades, Gehenna, Tartarus)

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:40 "The Horse Gate"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
31:40 "The Horse Gate" This is located close to the southeast corner of the city's wall (cf. Neh. 3:28). Remember, Nehemiah was not able to rebuild the entire wall of the ruined city of Jerusalem, so he planned on a much smaller city.

▣ "shall be holy to the Lord" The Hebrew root "holy" (BDB 871) basically means "set apart for God" or in a sense, dedicated to God's will and service. In this context, it refers to the new heaven and new earth (cf. Rev. 21-22). The restored, redeemed, and forgiven people of God will be safe and secure (cf. 1 Pet. 1:4-5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY ONES

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why was the prophecy so radical to its hearers?
  2. Has this been fulfilled? When?
  3. Why is Jer. 31:30-34 so significant?
  4. What is involved in the New Covenant?
